      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.1701"><b>60A.1701</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60K.19">60K.19</a>]
</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">AGENCY AGREEMENTS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.171">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.171 REHABILITATION AND CANCELLATION OF INDEPENDENT AGENT CONTRACTS BY INSURANCE COMPANIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Termination rights and obligations.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) After an agency contractual relationship has been in effect for a period of three years, an insurance company writing fire or casualty loss insurance in this state may not terminate the agency contractual relationship with any appointed agent unless the company has provided written notice of termination to the agent at least 60 days in advance of the effective date of the termination.</p>
          <p>(b) The notice of termination must include the reasons for termination.</p>
          <p>(c) An insurance company may not terminate an agency contract based upon any of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) an adverse loss experience for a single year;</p>
          <p>(2) the geographic location of the agent's auto and homeowners insurance business; or</p>
          <p>(3) the performance of obligations required of an insurer under Minnesota Statutes.</p>
          <p>(d) For purposes of this section, "fire or casualty loss insurance" means any line of insurance which an insurance agent with a personal lines, property, or casualty license under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60K.30">60K.30</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60K.56">60K.56</a> may write in this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Agent request to renew insurance contract.</span></h2>
          <p>The company shall at the request of the agent renew any insurance contract written by the agent for the company for not more than one year for fire or casualty loss insurance during a period of 18 months after the effective date of the termination, but in the event any risk does not meet current underwriting standards of the company, the company may decline its renewal, provided that the company shall give the agent not less than 60 days' notice of its intention not to renew the contract of insurance. The company shall not reduce the agent's commissions, unless the company is reducing the commissions for other appointed agents in the state at the same time.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Authority to write new contract limited.</span></h2>
          <p>No new insurance or bond contract shall be written by the agent for the company after the effective date of the termination without the written approval of the company. The agent may increase liability on renewal or in force business for not more than one year for the insured after the effective date of the termination if the increased liability meets the current underwriting standards of the company.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.</h2>
          <p>[Renumbered subd 4]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>MS 1990 [Renumbered subd 5]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>MS 2004 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/74/#laws.0.13.0">2005 c 74 s 13</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>MS 1990 [Renumbered subd 6]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Earlier termination allowed.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing contained in this section prohibits the earlier termination of an amendment or addendum subsequent to the inception date of the original agency agreement provided that the subsequent amendment or addendum provides for termination on shorter notice and the agent agrees in writing to the earlier termination.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>MS 1990 [Renumbered subd 7]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Limitation on refusal to renew business during contract term.</span></h2>
          <p>During the term of the contract the company shall not refuse to renew such business from the agent as would be in accordance with the company's current underwriting standards.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.</h2>
          <p>MS 1990 [Renumbered subd 8]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Nonapplication of section.</span></h2>
          <p>The provisions of this section do not apply to the termination of an agent's contract for insolvency, abandonment, gross and willful misconduct, or failure to pay over to the company money due to the company after receipt by the agent of a written demand therefor, or after revocation of the agent's license by the commissioner of commerce. This section does not apply to the termination of an agent's contract if the agent is directly employed by the company or if the agent writes 80 percent or more of the agent's gross annual insurance business for one company or any or all of its subsidiaries.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.</h2>
          <p>MS 1990 [Renumbered subd 9]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Application to contract between agent and fire and casualty loss company.</span></h2>
          <p>All future and presently existing agency contractual relationships between an agent and a company writing fire or casualty loss insurance in this state are subject to the provisions of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>If it is found, after notice and an opportunity to be heard as determined by the commissioner of commerce, that an insurance company has violated this section, the insurance company shall be subject to a civil action by the agent for actual damages suffered because of the premature termination of the contract by the company. The commissioner of commerce shall employ the department's investigative and enforcement authority if the commissioner has a reason to believe that an insurer has violated this section. An insurer found in violation of this section is subject to a civil penalty imposed by the commissioner not to exceed $10,000 per violation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Compliance relief.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event that a company's compliance with this section is demonstrated to the satisfaction of the commissioner to represent a hazard or potential hazard to the financial integrity of the company, the commissioner may, after a hearing, issue an order relieving the company from its obligation to provide the renewal policies otherwise required by this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Business solicitation in notice of nonrenewal prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon termination of an agency, a company is prohibited from soliciting business in the notice of nonrenewal required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.37">60A.37</a>. If termination of an agency contract is the ground for nonrenewal of a policy of homeowner's insurance, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/65A.27#stat.65A.27.4">65A.27, subdivision 4</a>, the company must provide notice to the policyholder that the policy is not being renewed due to the termination of the company's contract with the agency. If the agency is unable to replace the homeowner's insurance policy with a suitable policy from another insurer, the agent must notify the policyholder of the policyholder's right to renew with the company terminating the agency contract. The company must renew the policy if the insured or the insured's agent makes a written request for the renewal before the renewal date.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.171.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Cancellation of line of business as cancellation or termination of agency.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, a cancellation or termination of an agent's contract is considered to have occurred if the company cancels a line of insurance business or a volume of insurance business that equals or exceeds 75 percent of the insurance business placed by that agent with the company.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.171.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/287/#laws.0.1.0">1977 c 287 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/289/#laws.0.114.0">1983 c 289 s 114</a> subd 1; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/655/#laws.1.92.0">1984 c 655 art 1 s 92</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/92/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 92 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/39/#laws.0.1.0">1991 c 39 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/446/#laws.1.4.0">1996 c 446 art 1 s 4</a>,5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/117/#laws.2.5.0">2001 c 117 art 2 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/74/#laws.0.4.0">2005 c 74 s 4</a>,5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/132/#laws.0.2.0">2005 c 132 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.172">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.172 INSURANCE AGENCY CONTRACTS; CANCELLATION.</h1>
        <p>(a) An insurer may not cancel a written agreement with an agent or reduce or restrict an agent's underwriting authority with respect to property or casualty insurance, based solely on the loss ratio experience on that agent's book of business, if: the insurer required the agent to submit the application for underwriting approval, all material information on the application was fully completed, and the agent has not omitted or altered any information provided by the applicant.</p>
        <p>(b) For purposes of this section, "loss ratio experience" means the ratio of claims paid divided by the premiums paid.</p>
        <p>(c) This section applies only to agents who write 80 percent or more of their gross annual insurance business for one company or any or all of its subsidiaries, and are not in the direct employ of the company.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.172.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/288/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 288 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/170/#laws.0.1.0">1989 c 170 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/379/#laws.0.1.0">1992 c 379 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.173">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.173 EFFECTIVE DATE.</h1>
        <p>Section 60A.172 is effective January 1, 1987, and applies to cancellations begun as of that date. As a condition of doing business in the state of Minnesota, an insurer shall promptly reinstate any agreements canceled under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.172">60A.172</a> and shall restore any authority reduced or restricted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.172">60A.172</a> from January 1, 1987, until May 29, 1987.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.173.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/288/#laws.0.2.0">1987 c 288 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.174">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.174 SEVERABILITY.</h1>
        <p>If section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.173">60A.173</a> is determined by a final, nonappealable order of any Minnesota or federal court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unconstitutional, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.172">60A.172</a> is effective May 29, 1987.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.174.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/288/#laws.0.3.0">1987 c 288 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.175">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.175 AGENT COMMISSIONS.</h1>
        <p>(a) An insurer that cancels a written agreement with an agent under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.171">60A.171</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.172">60A.172</a> or cancels a line of business sold by the agent must pay to the agent all commissions, bonuses, and other compensation earned by that agent prior to or after termination. The commission rate must be the rate in effect at the time of the notice of termination.</p>
        <p>(b) An insurer may not reduce agent commissions, bonuses, or other compensation contained in written agreements without first providing written notice of the change to the agent at least 180 days before its effective date.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.175.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/170/#laws.0.2.0">1989 c 170 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/39/#laws.0.2.0">1991 c 39 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.1755">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.1755 AGENT ERRORS AND OMISSIONS INSURANCE; CHOICE OF SOURCE.</h1>
        <p>An insurance company shall not require an insurance agent to maintain insurance coverage for the agent's errors and omissions from a specific insurance company. This section does not apply if the insurance producer is a captive producer or employee of the insurance company imposing the requirement, or if that insurance company or affiliated broker-dealer pays for or contributes to the premiums for the errors and omissions coverage. For purposes of this section, "captive producer" means a producer that writes 80 percent or more of the producer's gross annual insurance business for that insurance company or any or all of its subsidiaries. Nothing in this section shall prohibit an insurance company from requiring an insurance producer to maintain errors and omissions coverage or requiring that errors and omissions coverage meet certain criteria.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.1755.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/178/#laws.1.6.0">2009 c 178 art 1 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.176">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.176 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.176.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>The definitions in this section apply to this section and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.177">60A.177</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.176.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/207/#laws.0.8.0">1991 c 207 s 8</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.176.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Agent.</span></h2>
          <p>"Agent" means an agent who is not an employee of the insurer, who has an agency contractual relationship that has been in effect for five or more years, and who writes 80 percent or more of the agent's business through one insurer or its subsidiaries.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.176.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Insurer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Insurer" means an insurance company writing property or casualty loss insurance in this state through agents.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.176.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/457/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 457 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/207/#laws.0.1.0">1991 c 207 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.177">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.177 INVOLUNTARY TERMINATION OF AN AGENT BY THE INSURER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.177.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Termination review process.</span></h2>
          <p>An insurer shall establish a termination review process for an agent involuntarily terminated by the insurer. The review process is available for use at the option of the agent. The review process must be completed within 15 days of the request or before the date of termination, whichever is later.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.177.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Notice; hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>If an agent is terminated by an insurer, the agent may request a hearing before the board of review. If an insurer initiates the termination of an agent's agreement, the written notice of termination must advise the agent of the agent's right to a hearing before the board of review. Upon receipt of an agent's request for a hearing, the commissioner shall establish a hearing date within 30 days of the request or longer with the approval of the agent and the insurer. The agent and the insurer shall be notified in writing of the date, time, and place of the hearing. The hearing provided for under this section is not subject to chapter 14. The review board shall provide the parties to the hearing with an opportunity to present evidence and arguments in support of their respective positions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.177.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Board of review.</span></h2>
          <p>A three-member board of review shall be selected from a list of ten agents and ten insurer representatives compiled by the commissioner. One member shall be selected by the agent and one by the insurer. The third member shall be mutually agreed upon by both parties. If the parties do not agree upon a third member, the commissioner shall request the American Arbitration Association to provide the commissioner with three names of potential members. If the American Arbitration Association declines to provide the names, the commissioner of the Bureau of Mediation Services shall provide the names. The agent member and the insurer member shall each strike one person from the list. The remaining person shall be selected as the third member of the review board. The insurer and the agent shall each pay one-half of the fee charged by the third member. The board member selected by the agent may not be a relative of the agent. The board members selected by the agent and insurer may not be presently or formerly associated with an insurer represented by the agent. An insurer is immune from civil liability to the agent for disclosures made at the hearing. This immunity does not extend to disclosures made in bad faith or with knowledge of their falseness.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.177.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Board's determination.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon completion of the hearing, the board of review shall determine if the termination of the agent's agreement is justified. If in the opinion of the board of review an involuntary termination is not justified, and in the absence of a reasonable contractual financial provision for termination as determined by the board, the board shall order the insurer to pay an amount of compensation that the board considers appropriate to the agent.</p>
          <p>If in the opinion of the board of review a voluntary termination was not voluntary and the insurer is not justified in terminating the agent's agreement, and in the absence of a reasonable contractual financial provision for termination as determined by the board, the board shall order the insurer to pay an amount of compensation that the board considers appropriate to the agent.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.177.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Appeal.</span></h2>
          <p>A final determination of the board of review under subdivision 4 may be appealed to district court by either party for a trial de novo. If the insurer appeals and the agent prevails, the insurer is responsible for the agent's legal fees as approved by the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.177.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Civil penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who intimidates or coerces a member of the board of review is subject to a civil penalty imposed by the commissioner in an amount not to exceed $25,000.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.177.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Exemption.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to an agent whose license has expired, is revoked, or is currently under suspension.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.177.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Administrative penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>Failure to comply with a final order or determination of the review board constitutes a basis for disciplinary action under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/45.027#stat.45.027.7">45.027, subdivision 7</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.177.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/457/#laws.0.2.0">1990 c 457 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/207/#laws.0.2.0">1991 c 207 s 2</a>-5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/379/#laws.0.2.0">1992 c 379 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">LIFE OR HEALTH SALES QUOTAS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.178">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.178 LIFE OR HEALTH INSURANCE SALES QUOTAS.</h1>
        <p>No insurer, its officers, or managers shall require licensed property and casualty agents to sell a specified number of life or health insurance policies or a specified dollar amount of life and health insurance as a condition of selling property-casualty insurance. No insurer, its officers, or managers may reduce or restrict an agent's underwriting authority on property-casualty insurance policies based upon the sale of life or health insurance. The provisions of this section do not apply to agents who are directly employed by the insurer or who write 80 percent or more of their gross annual insurance business for one company or any or all of its subsidiaries.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.178.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/152/#laws.0.1.0">1995 c 152 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.179">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.179 LIFE OR HEALTH INSURANCE SALES QUOTAS FOR EXCLUSIVE AGENTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.179.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>This section applies to licensed insurance agents as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.176">60A.176</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.179.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibited practice.</span></h2>
          <p>No insurer shall require an agent who has been licensed as an agent three years or more to sell a specified number of life or health insurance policies or a specified dollar amount of life and health insurance in relation to the sale of other insurance products. No insurer may terminate an agent's contract or reduce or restrict an agent's underwriting authority on property and casualty insurance policies based upon the sale of life or health insurance.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.179.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/446/#laws.1.6.0">1996 c 446 art 1 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.18"><b>60A.18</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/222/#laws.1.58.0">2014 c 222 art 1 s 58</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">FOREIGN COMPANIES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.19">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.19 FOREIGN COMPANIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.19.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>Any insurance company of another state, upon compliance with all laws governing such corporations in general and with the foregoing provisions so far as applicable and the following requirements, shall be admitted to do business in this state:</p>
          <p>(1) It shall deposit with the commissioner a certified copy of its charter or certificate of incorporation and its bylaws, and a statement showing its financial condition and business, verified by its president and secretary or other proper officers;</p>
          <p>(2) It shall furnish the commissioner satisfactory evidence of its legal organization and authority to transact the proposed business and that its capital, assets, deposits with the proper official of its own state, amount insured, number of risks, reserve and other securities, and guaranties for protection of policyholders, creditors, and the public, comply with those required of like domestic companies;</p>
          <p>(3) By a duly executed instrument filed in the office of the commissioner, it shall appoint the commissioner and successors in office its lawful attorneys in fact and therein irrevocably agree that legal process in any action or proceeding against it may be served upon them with the same force and effect as if personally served upon it, so long as any of its liability exists in this state;</p>
          <p>(4) It shall appoint, as its agents in this state, residents thereof, and obtain from the commissioner a license to transact business;</p>
          <p>(5) Regardless of what lines of business an insurer of another state is seeking to write in this state, the lines of business it is licensed to write in its state of incorporation shall be the basis for establishing the financial requirements it must meet for admission in this state or for continuance of its authority to write business in this state;</p>
          <p>(6) No insurer of another state shall be admitted to do business in this state for a line of business that it is not authorized to write in its state of incorporation, unless the statutes of that state prohibit all insurers from writing that line of business.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.19.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Service of garnishee process.</span></h2>
          <p>When garnishee process is served upon the commissioner, as attorney for any insurance company, no garnishee fee shall be paid the commissioner. After the receipt of copy of the process the insurance company may demand of the attorney of the person making the garnishee the proper fees, and if the demand is not complied with before the day fixed for the disclosure of the garnishee, the proceeding may be dismissed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.19.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Commissioner appointed attorney for service of process.</span></h2>
          <p>Before any corporation, association, or company issuing policies of insurance of any character and not organized or existing pursuant to the laws of this state is admitted to or authorized to transact the business of insurance in this state, it shall, by a duly executed instrument to be filed in the office of the commissioner, constitute and appoint the commissioner and successors in office its true and lawful attorney, upon whom proofs of loss, any notice authorized or required by any contract with the company to be served on it, summonses and all lawful processes in any action or legal proceeding against it may be served, and that the authority thereof shall continue in force irrevocable so long as any liability of the company remains outstanding in this state.</p>
          <p>This instrument shall contain a provision and agreement declaring that the company, association, or corporation desires to transact the business of insurance in this state, and that it will accept a license therefor according to the laws of this state.</p>
          <p>In case of the failure of any such insurance company to comply with any of the provisions of this subdivision and subdivision 4, or if it shall violate any of the conditions or agreements contained in the instrument filed, its right to transact insurance business in this state shall cease and it shall be the duty of the commissioner to immediately declare its license revoked; and, in case of revocation, the company shall not be again licensed to transact business in this state for the period of one year from date of the revocation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.19.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Service of process.</span></h2>
          <p>The service of process authorized by this section shall be made in compliance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/45.028#stat.45.028.2">45.028, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.19.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Provision as to alien companies.</span></h2>
          <p>(1) <b>Deposit.</b> Such company of any foreign country, except fraternal benefit societies, shall not be admitted until, besides complying with the foregoing requirements, it has made a deposit with the commissioner in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.10#stat.60A.10.4">60A.10, subdivision 4</a>, or with the proper officer of some other state of the United States, of a sum not less than the deposit required of a like company by the laws of this state and this deposit shall be of the same class of securities and subject to the same limitations required for the deposit of domestic companies that must by law maintain a deposit.</p>
          <p>This deposit shall be in exclusive trust for all its policyholders and creditors in the United States, and for all purposes of the insurance laws shall be deemed assets of the company.</p>
          <p>(2) <b>Trustees, investments and funds.</b> Any company of a foreign country may duly appoint one or more citizens of the United States, approved by the commissioner, to hold funds or other property for the benefit of its policyholders and creditors therein. A certified copy of their appointment and of the instrument of trust shall be filed with the commissioner, who shall have the same authority in the premises as in the case of the affairs of all companies. These funds shall be invested in the same securities as required of other insurance companies and, together with the deposits required, shall constitute the assets of the company in respect to its policyholders and creditors in the United States.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.19.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Retaliatory provisions.</span></h2>
          <p>(1) In the event that a domestic insurance company, after complying with all reasonable laws and rulings of any other state or country, is refused permission by that state or country to transact business therein after the commissioner of commerce of Minnesota has determined that that company is solvent and properly managed and after the commissioner has so certified to the proper authority of that other state or country, then, and in every such case, the commissioner may forthwith suspend or cancel the certificate of authority of every insurance company organized under the laws of that other state or country to the extent that it insures, or seeks to insure, in this state against any of the risks or hazards which that domestic company seeks to insure against in that other state or country. Without limiting the application of the foregoing provision, it is hereby determined that any law or ruling of any other state or country which prescribes to a Minnesota domestic insurance company the premium rate or rates for life insurance issued or to be issued outside that other state or country shall not be reasonable.</p>
          <p>(2) This section does not apply to insurance companies organized or domiciled in a state or country, the laws of which do not impose retaliatory taxes, fines, deposits, penalties, licenses, or fees or which grant, on a reciprocal basis, exemptions from retaliatory taxes, fines, deposits, penalties, licenses, or fees to insurance companies domiciled in this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.19.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Policy not invalidated by occurrence of hostilities.</span></h2>
          <p>No policy of insurance issued to a resident of this state shall be invalidated by the occurrence of hostilities between any foreign country and the United States.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.19.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.</h2>
          <p class="in">MS 2010 [Renumbered, 60A.198 subd 8]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.19.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/395/#laws.1.19.0">1967 c 395 art 1 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/291/#laws.0.3.0">1969 c 291 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/145/#laws.0.21.0">1971 c 145 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/425/#laws.0.4.0">1974 c 425 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/195/#laws.0.2.0">1977 c 195 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/465/#laws.0.7.0">1978 c 465 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/289/#laws.0.114.0">1983 c 289 s 114</a> subd 1; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/592/#laws.0.38.0">1984 c 592 s 38</a>,39; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/609/#laws.0.3.0">1984 c 609 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/655/#laws.1.92.0">1984 c 655 art 1 s 92</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/1/1/#laws.10.4.0">1Sp1989 c 1 art 10 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/291/#laws.9.2.0">1991 c 291 art 9 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/511/#laws.7.2.0">1992 c 511 art 7 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/564/#laws.1.54.0">1992 c 564 art 1 s 54</a>; art 2 s 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/485/#laws.0.10.0">1994 c 485 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/632/#laws.4.24.0">1994 c 632 art 4 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/177/#laws.0.16.0">1999 c 177 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/243/#laws.7.1.0">1999 c 243 art 7 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/394/#laws.2.4.0">2000 c 394 art 2 s 4</a>,5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.10.0">2011 c 108 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">SURPLUS LINES INSURANCE</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.195">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.195 CITATION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a> shall be known and may be cited as the "Minnesota Surplus Lines Insurance Act."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.195.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 221 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.196">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.196 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <p class="in">Unless the context otherwise requires, the following terms have the meanings given them for the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>:</p>
        <p>(a) "Affiliated group" means a group which includes the insured and any entity, or group of entities, that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with the insured. An entity has control over another entity when: (1) the entity directly, indirectly, or acting through one or more persons owns, controls, or has the power to vote 25 percent or more of any class of voting securities of the other entity; or (2) the entity controls in any manner the election of a majority of the directors or trustees of the other entity.</p>
        <p class="in">(b) "Alien insurer" means any insurer which is incorporated or otherwise organized outside of the United States.</p>
        <p class="in">(c) "Association" means an association registered under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.208">60A.208</a>.</p>
        <p class="in">(d) "Eligible surplus lines insurer" means a nonadmitted insurer recognized as eligible to write insurance business under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>.</p>
        <p>(e) "Exempt commercial purchaser" means any person purchasing commercial insurance that, at the time of placement, meets the following requirements:</p>
        <p>(1) the person employs or retains a qualified risk manager to negotiate insurance coverage;</p>
        <p>(2) the person has paid aggregate nationwide commercial property and casualty insurance premiums in excess of $100,000 in the immediately preceding 12 months;</p>
        <p>(3) the person meets at least one of the following criteria:</p>
        <p>(i) the person possesses a net worth in excess of $20,000,000, as such amount is adjusted pursuant to clause (4);</p>
        <p>(ii) the person generates annual revenues in excess of $50,000,000, as such amount is adjusted pursuant to clause (4);</p>
        <p>(iii) the person employs more than 500 full-time or full-time equivalent employees per individual insured or is a member of an affiliated group employing more than 1,000 employees in the aggregate;</p>
        <p>(iv) the person is a not-for-profit organization or public entity generating annual budgeted expenditures of at least $30,000,000, as such amount is adjusted pursuant to clause (4); or</p>
        <p>(v) the person is a municipality with a population in excess of 50,000 persons.</p>
        <p>(4) Effective January 1, 2015, and every five years thereafter, the amounts in clause (3), items (i), (ii), and (iv), shall be adjusted to reflect the percentage change for the five-year period in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics of the Department of Labor.</p>
        <p>(f) "Home state" means the state in which an insured maintains its principal place of business, or in the case of an individual, the individual's principal residence. If 100 percent of the insured risk is located out of the state, the term means the state to which the greatest percentage of the insured's taxable premium for that insurance contract is allocated. If more than one insured from an affiliated group are named insureds on a single nonadmitted insurance contract, the term means the home state of the member of the affiliated group that has the largest percentage of premium attributed to it under that insurance contract.</p>
        <p class="in">(g) "Ineligible surplus lines insurer" means a nonadmitted insurer not recognized as an eligible surplus lines insurer under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>.</p>
        <p class="in">(h) "Insurance laws" means chapters 60 to 79 inclusive.</p>
        <p class="in">(i) "Nonadmitted insurance" means any property and casualty insurance permitted to be placed directly or through a surplus lines broker with a nonadmitted insurer in this state only under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>.</p>
        <p>(j) "Nonadmitted insurer" means an insurer not licensed to engage in the business of insurance in Minnesota, but does not include a risk retention group, as the term is defined in section 2(a)(4) of the Liability Risk Retention Act of 1986, United States Code, title 15, section 3901(a)(4).</p>
        <p>(k) "Qualified risk manager" means, with respect to a policyholder of commercial insurance, a person who meets all of the following requirements:</p>
        <p>(1) the person is an employee of, or third-party consultant retained by, the commercial policyholder;</p>
        <p>(2) the person provides skilled services in loss prevention, loss reduction, or risk and insurance coverage analysis, and purchase of insurance;</p>
        <p>(3) the person:</p>
        <p>(i) has a bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited college or university in risk management, business administration, finance, economics, or any other field determined by a state insurance commissioner or other state regulatory official or entity to demonstrate minimum competence in risk management and has three years of experience in risk financing, claims administration, loss prevention, risk and insurance analysis, or purchasing commercial lines of insurance;</p>
        <p>(ii) has a designation as a Chartered Property and Casualty Underwriter (CPCU) issued by the American Institute for CPCU/Insurance Institute of America, an Associate in Risk Management (ARM) issued by the American Institute for CPCU/Insurance Institute of America, a Certified Risk Manager (CRM) issued by the National Alliance for Insurance Education and Research, a RIMS Fellow (RF) issued by the Global Risk Management Institute, or any other designation, certification, or license determined by a state insurance commissioner or other state insurance regulatory official or entity to demonstrate minimum competency in risk management;</p>
        <p>(iii) has at least seven years of experience in risk financing, claims administration, loss prevention, risk and insurance coverage analysis, or purchasing commercial lines of insurance and one of the designations specified in item (ii);</p>
        <p>(iv) has at least ten years of experience in risk financing, claims administration, loss prevention, risk and insurance coverage analysis, or purchasing commercial lines of insurance; or</p>
        <p>(v) has a graduate degree from an accredited college or university in risk management, business administration, finance, economics, or any other field determined by a state insurance commissioner or other state regulatory official or entity to demonstrate minimum competence in risk management.</p>
        <p class="in">(l) "Stamping" means electronically assigning a unique identifying number that is specific to a submitted policy, contract, or insurance document.</p>
        <p class="in">(m) "Surplus lines broker" or "broker" means an individual, firm, or corporation which is licensed in this state to sell, solicit, or negotiate insurance on properties, risks, or exposures located or to be performed in this state with nonadmitted insurers only under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.196.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.2.0">1981 c 221 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/337/#laws.0.11.0">1987 c 337 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/366/#laws.17.1.0">2008 c 366 art 17 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.11.0">2011 c 108 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.197">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.197 RATES AND FORMS.</h1>
        <p>(a) Rates used by eligible and ineligible surplus lines insurers shall not be subject to the insurance laws except that a rate shall not be unfairly discriminatory.</p>
        <p>(b) Forms used by eligible and ineligible surplus lines insurers pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a> shall not be subject to the insurance laws, except that a policy shall not contain language which misrepresents the true nature of the policy or class of policies.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.197.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.3.0">1981 c 221 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.198">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.198 TRANSACTION OF NONADMITTED INSURANCE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.198.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">License required.</span></h2>
          <p>A person, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.02#stat.60A.02.7">60A.02, subdivision 7</a>, shall not act in any other manner as an agent or broker in the transaction of nonadmitted insurance unless licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>. A surplus lines license is not required for a licensed agent who assists in the placement of nonadmitted insurance with a surplus lines broker pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>. This subdivision does not apply to nonadmitted insurance procured by a surplus lines broker when an insured's home state is a state other than Minnesota.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.198.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Compliance with statutory provisions.</span></h2>
          <p>A person shall not offer, solicit, make a quotation on, sell, or issue a policy of insurance, binder, or any other evidence of insurance with a nonadmitted insurer, except in compliance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>. This subdivision does not apply when an insured's home state is a state other than Minnesota.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.198.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Procedure for obtaining license.</span></h2>
          <p>A person licensed as an agent in this state pursuant to other law may obtain a surplus lines license by doing the following:</p>
          <p>(a) filing an application in the form and with the information the commissioner may reasonably require to determine the ability of the applicant to act in accordance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>;</p>
          <p>(b) maintaining an agent's license in this state;</p>
          <p>(c) registering with the association created pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.2085">60A.2085</a>;</p>
          <p>(d) agreeing to file with the commissioner of revenue all returns required by chapter 297I and paying to the commissioner of revenue all amounts required under chapter 297I;</p>
          <p>(e) agreeing to file all documents required pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.2086">60A.2086</a> and to pay the stamping fee assessed pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.2085#stat.60A.2085.7">60A.2085, subdivision 7</a>; and</p>
          <p>(f) paying a fee as prescribed by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60K.55">60K.55</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.198.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Broker's powers.</span></h2>
          <p>A surplus lines broker may do any or all of the following:</p>
          <p>(a) place insurance on risks in this state with eligible surplus lines insurers;</p>
          <p>(b) place insurance on risks in this state with ineligible surplus lines insurers in strict compliance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>. If the insurance is provided through the participation of several nonadmitted insurers and the broker has reason to believe that a substantial portion of the insurance would be assumed by eligible surplus lines insurers, then with respect to the ineligible surplus lines insurers, the insured or the insured's representative shall be informed as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209#stat.60A.209.1">60A.209, subdivision 1</a>, clause (a); or</p>
          <p>(c) engage in any other acts expressly or implicitly authorized by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a> and the other insurance laws.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.198.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Disclosures.</span></h2>
          <p>Before placement of insurance with an eligible surplus lines insurer, a surplus lines broker shall inform an insured or the insured's representative that coverage may be placed in conformance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a> with an insurer not licensed in this state and that payment of loss is not guaranteed in the event of insolvency of the eligible surplus lines insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.198.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/394/#laws.2.28.0">2000 c 394 art 2 s 28</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.198.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Participation in national producer database for surplus lines brokers.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of carrying out the provisions of the Nonadmitted and Reinsurance Reform Act of 2010, the commissioner is authorized to utilize the national insurance producer database of the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, or any other equivalent uniform national database, for the licensure of surplus lines brokers and for renewal of the licenses.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.198.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Insurance from unlicensed foreign companies.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Any person, firm, or corporation whose home state is Minnesota, that procures insurance on any property, interests, or risks of any nature other than life insurance directly from a nonadmitted insurer, must agree to file with the commissioner of revenue all returns required under chapter 297I and pay to the commissioner of revenue any amounts required to be paid under chapter 297I. Upon that agreement, the commissioner of commerce shall issue a license, good for one year. Insurance procured under the license is valid and the provisions of the policies are considered to be in accordance, and construed as if identical in effect, with the standard policy prescribed by the laws of this state. The insurers may enter the state to perform any act necessary or proper in the conduct of the business.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.199">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.199 EXAMINATIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.199.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Examination of books and records.</span></h2>
          <p>If the commissioner considers it necessary, the commissioner may examine the books and records of a surplus lines broker to determine whether the broker is conducting business in accordance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>. For the purposes of facilitating examinations, the broker shall allow the commissioner free access at reasonable times to all of the broker's books and records relating to the transactions to which sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a> apply. If an examination is conducted, the cost of the examination shall be paid by the surplus line agent or agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.199.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>

			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.5.0">1981 c 221 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/592/#laws.0.41.0">1984 c 592 s 41</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/1/14/#laws.15.2.0">1Sp1985 c 14 art 15 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/1/3/#laws.1.82.0">1Sp1986 c 3 art 1 s 82</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/268/#laws.2.2.0">1987 c 268 art 2 s 2</a>-10; art 17 s 41; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/480/#laws.1.46.0">1990 c 480 art 1 s 46</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/375/#laws.10.5.0">1993 c 375 art 10 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/264/#laws.13.2.0">1995 c 264 art 13 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.13.0">2011 c 108 s 13</a></p>

      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.20"><b>60A.20</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.15.0">1981 c 221 s 15</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.201">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.201 PLACEMENT OF INSURANCE BY BROKER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.201.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Restrictions.</span></h2>
          <p>Insurance shall not be placed by the surplus lines broker with a nonadmitted insurer when coverage is available from a licensed insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.201.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Availability of other coverage; presumption.</span></h2>
          <p>There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the following coverages are available from a licensed insurer:</p>
          <p>(a) all mandatory automobile insurance coverages required by chapter 65B;</p>
          <p>(b) private passenger automobile physical damage coverage;</p>
          <p>(c) homeowners and property insurance on owner-occupied dwellings whose value is less than $500,000. This figure shall be changed annually by the commissioner by the same percentage as the Consumer Price Index for the Minneapolis-St. Paul Metropolitan Area is changed;</p>
          <p>(d) any coverage readily available from three or more licensed insurers unless the licensed insurers quote a premium and terms not competitive with a premium and terms quoted by an eligible surplus lines insurer; and</p>
          <p>(e) workers' compensation insurance, except excess workers' compensation insurance which is not available from the Workers' Compensation Reinsurance Association.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.201.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Unavailability of other coverage; presumption.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the following coverages are unavailable from a licensed insurer:</p>
          <p class="in">(a) coverages where one portion of the risk is acceptable to licensed insurers but another portion of the same risk is not acceptable. The entire coverage may be placed with eligible surplus lines insurers if it can be shown that the eligible surplus lines insurer will accept the entire coverage but not the rejected portion alone; and</p>
          <p class="in">(b) any coverage that the broker is unable to procure after diligent search among licensed insurers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.201.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/178/#laws.1.69.0">2009 c 178 art 1 s 69</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.201.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Streamlined application for exempt commercial purchasers.</span></h2>
          <p>A surplus lines broker is not required to make a diligent search to determine whether the full amount or type of insurance can be obtained from licensed insurers when the broker is seeking to procure or place nonadmitted insurance for an exempt commercial purchaser provided:</p>
          <p>(1) the broker procuring or placing the nonadmitted insurance has disclosed to the exempt commercial purchaser that the insurance may or may not be available from a licensed insurer that may provide greater protection with more regulatory oversight; and</p>
          <p>(2) the exempt commercial purchaser has subsequently requested in writing for the broker to procure or place the insurance from a nonadmitted insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.201.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Coverage deemed unavailable.</span></h2>
          <p>Coverage for a risk that was referred to a surplus lines broker by a Minnesota licensed insurance producer who is not affiliated with the surplus lines broker is deemed unavailable from a licensed insurer.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.201.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.6.0">1981 c 221 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/564/#laws.1.21.0">1992 c 564 art 1 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/178/#laws.1.9.0">2009 c 178 art 1 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.14.0">2011 c 108 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/114/#laws.1.1.0">2024 c 114 art 1 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.202">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.202 EVIDENCE OF PLACEMENT OF INSURANCE BY BROKER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.202.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Restriction.</span></h2>
          <p>Only a surplus lines broker shall issue evidence of placement of insurance with a nonadmitted insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.202.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Written communication of coverage to be delivered.</span></h2>
          <p>A broker shall, within seven working days after the date on which the risk was bound or the insured or applicant was advised that coverage has been or will be obtained, deliver to the insured or the insured's representative a policy, a written binder, a certificate or other written evidence of insurance placed with a nonadmitted insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.202.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Contents of written communication.</span></h2>
          <p>The written communication showing that insurance has been obtained shall identify all known nonadmitted insurers directly assuming any risk of loss. If there is more than one nonadmitted insurer, any document issued or certified by the broker pursuant to subdivision 2 shall specify, to the extent known by the broker, whether the obligation is joint or several, and if the obligation is several, the proportion of the obligation assumed by each insurer.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.202.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.7.0">1981 c 221 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.15.0">2011 c 108 s 15</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.203">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.203 RETENTION OF RECORDS.</h1>
        <p>Each surplus lines broker shall keep a separate account of each transaction entered into pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>. Evidence of these transactions shall be documented in the form and manner designated by the commissioner and retained by the broker for a minimum of five years. The forms must be readily available for review and audit by the commissioner.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.203.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.8.0">1981 c 221 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/564/#laws.1.22.0">1992 c 564 art 1 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.16.0">2011 c 108 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.204">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.204 FEES AND COMMISSIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.204.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed by amendment, 2010 c 384 s 6]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.204.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Regulation of fees and commissions.</span></h2>
          <p>A surplus lines broker may charge a fee and commission, in addition to the premium, that is not excessive or discriminatory. The broker shall maintain complete documentation of all fees and commissions charged.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.204.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed by amendment, 2010 c 384 s 6]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.204.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.9.0">1981 c 221 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/384/#laws.0.6.0">2010 c 384 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.17.0">2011 c 108 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.205">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.205 COMPENSATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.205.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authorization.</span></h2>
          <p>A surplus lines broker may be compensated by an eligible surplus lines insurer and the broker may compensate a licensed agent in this state for obtaining nonadmitted insurance business. A licensed agent authorized by the broker may collect a premium on behalf of the broker, and as between the insured and the broker, the broker shall be considered to have received the premium if the premium payment has been made to the agent.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.205.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Consequences of receipt.</span></h2>
          <p>If an eligible surplus lines insurer has assumed a risk, and if the premium for that risk has been received by the broker who placed the insurance, then as between the insurer and the insured, the insurer shall be considered to have received the premium due to it for the coverage and shall be liable to the insured for any loss covered by the insurance and for the unearned premium upon cancellation of the insurance, regardless of whether the broker is indebted to the insurer.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.205.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.10.0">1981 c 221 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/178/#laws.1.10.0">2009 c 178 art 1 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.18.0">2011 c 108 s 18</a>,19</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.206">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.206 QUALIFICATION AS ELIGIBLE SURPLUS LINES INSURER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.206.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Insurers to be recognized by commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>A surplus lines broker shall place nonadmitted insurance only with insurers which are in a stable and unimpaired financial condition. An insurer recognized by the commissioner as an eligible surplus lines insurer pursuant to subdivision 2 shall be considered to meet the requirements of this subdivision. Recognition as an eligible surplus lines insurer shall be conditioned upon the insurers continued compliance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.206.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Application for recognition.</span></h2>
          <p>An insurer not otherwise licensed to engage in the business of insurance in Minnesota may apply for recognition as an eligible surplus lines insurer by filing an application in the form and with the information as reasonably required by the commissioner regarding the insurer's financial stability, reputation, integrity and operating plans, accompanied by a license fee of $500. The commissioner may delegate to an association the power to process and make recommendations on applications for recognition as an eligible surplus lines insurer. Notwithstanding delegation by the commissioner, an applicant may file an application directly with the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.206.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Standards to be met by insurers.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall recognize the insurer as an eligible surplus lines insurer when satisfied that the insurer is in a stable, unimpaired financial condition and that the insurer is qualified to provide coverage in compliance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>. If filed with full supporting documentation before July 1 of any year, applications submitted under subdivision 2 shall be acted upon by the commissioner before December 31 of the year of submission.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner shall not authorize a foreign insurer as an eligible surplus lines insurer unless the insurer:</p>
          <p>(1) is domiciled within a United States jurisdiction and authorized to write the type of insurance in its domiciliary jurisdiction; and</p>
          <p>(2) has capital and surplus or its equivalent under the laws of its domiciliary jurisdiction which equals the greater of:</p>
          <p>(i) the minimum capital and surplus requirements under the laws of Minnesota; or</p>
          <p>(ii) $15,000,000.</p>
          <p>The requirements of item (i) may be satisfied by an insurer's possessing less than the minimum capital and surplus upon an affirmative finding of acceptability by the commissioner. The finding shall be based upon factors such as quality of management, capital and surplus of any parent company, company underwriting profit and investment income trends, market availability, and company record and reputation within the industry. In no event shall the commissioner make an affirmative finding of acceptability when the surplus lines insurer's capital and surplus is less than $4,500,000.</p>
          <p>(c) Eligible surplus lines insurers domiciled within the United States shall file an annual statement and an annual financial audit, under the terms and conditions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.13">60A.13, subdivisions 1, 3a, and 6</a>, and are subject to the penalties of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/72A.061">72A.061</a>, and are subject to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.03#stat.60A.03.5">60A.03, subdivision 5</a>, in regard to those requirements. The commissioner also has the powers provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.13#stat.60A.13.2">60A.13, subdivision 2</a>, in regard to eligible surplus lines insurers.</p>
          <p>(d) Eligible surplus lines insurers domiciled outside the United States shall file an annual statement on the standard nonadmitted insurers information office financial reporting format as prescribed by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners and an annual financial audit performed by an independent accounting firm. The commissioner shall not prohibit a surplus lines broker from placing nonadmitted insurance with, or procuring nonadmitted insurance from, an alien insurer that is included on the Quarterly Listing of Alien Insurers maintained by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners International Insurers Department.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.206.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Removal of insurers.</span></h2>
          <p>When the commissioner considers it necessary, the commissioner may request information about or examine the affairs of any eligible surplus lines insurer at the expense of the insurer, to determine whether the insurer should continue to remain on the list of eligible surplus lines insurers. If the commissioner determines that it is in the public interest to remove an insurer from the list because the insurer no longer meets the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>, or is no longer qualified to provide coverage under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>, the commissioner shall do so. If an insurer removed from the list desires a hearing pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Act, the hearing shall be scheduled within 30 days following request for the hearing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.206.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Trust fund to be maintained.</span></h2>
          <p>Before recognition as an eligible surplus lines insurer in this state, an alien insurer shall maintain a trust fund in the United States in cash, marketable securities, or other substantially equivalent instruments of at least $1,500,000 with a United States bank which is a member of the Federal Reserve System or which is on deposit with regulatory authorities in this or another state for the benefit of all United States policyholders and beneficiaries. A trust fund required under this subdivision shall not have an expiration date which is at any time less than five years in the future, on a continuing basis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.206.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Alternative means of compliance.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivisions 3 and 5 shall not apply to a group including incorporated and unincorporated, individual alien insurers which, in place of the requirements prescribed in subdivisions 3 and 5, maintain assets as provided in subdivision 3 and hold in trust for all policyholders and beneficiaries in the United States not less than $50,000,000 in the aggregate. The incorporated members of the group shall not be engaged in any business other than underwriting as a member of the group and must be subject to the same level of solvency regulation and control by the group's domiciliary regulator as are the unincorporated members.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.206.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Appointment of agent for service of process.</span></h2>
          <p>Each eligible surplus lines insurer shall appoint the commissioner as its resident agent, for purposes of service of process.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.206.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.11.0">1981 c 221 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/358/#laws.0.95.0">1987 c 358 s 95</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/564/#laws.1.23.0">1992 c 564 art 1 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/426/#laws.0.8.0">1994 c 426 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/485/#laws.0.11.0">1994 c 485 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.20.0">2011 c 108 s 20</a>,21; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/187/#laws.1.11.0">2012 c 187 art 1 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.207">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.207 POLICIES TO INCLUDE NOTICE.</h1>
        <p>Each policy, cover note, or instrument evidencing nonadmitted insurance from an eligible surplus lines insurer which is delivered to an insured or a representative of an insured shall have printed, typed, or stamped upon its face in not less than 10 point type, the following notice: "THIS INSURANCE IS ISSUED PURSUANT TO THE MINNESOTA SURPLUS LINES INSURANCE ACT. THE INSURER IS AN ELIGIBLE SURPLUS LINES INSURER BUT IS NOT OTHERWISE LICENSED BY THE STATE OF MINNESOTA. IN CASE OF INSOLVENCY, PAYMENT OF CLAIMS IS NOT GUARANTEED." This notice shall not be covered or concealed in any manner.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.207.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/221/#laws.0.12.0">1981 c 221 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/204/#laws.0.5.0">2006 c 204 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/108/#laws.0.22.0">2011 c 108 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.208">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.208 BROKER ASSOCIATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.208.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Broker's right to associate.</span></h2>
          <p>Surplus lines brokers may associate and the commissioner may register the association for one or more of the following purposes:</p>
          <p>(a) advising the commissioner as to the availability of nonadmitted insurance coverage and market practices and standards for nonadmitted insurers and brokers;</p>
          <p>(b) collecting and furnishing records and statistics; or</p>
          <p>(c) submitting recommendations regarding administration of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.195">60A.195</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.209">60A.209</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.208.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Filing requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Each association shall file with the commissioner for approval all of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a copy of the association's constitution and articles of agreement or association, or the association's certificate of incorporation and bylaws and any rules governing the association's activities; and</p>
          <p>(2) an agreement that, as a condition of continued registration under subdivision 1, the commissioner may examine the association.</p>
          <p>(b) Each association shall file with the commissioner and keep current all of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a list of members; and</p>
          <p>(2) the name and address of a resident of this state upon whom notices or orders of the commissioner or process issued by the commissioner may be served.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.208.3">
