Contributions must be based on sound actuarial principles and be adequate to fund the operation of the trust fund. Contributions may not be excessive, in relation to the benefits provided, or unfairly discriminatory.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Risk pooling or sharing agreements prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>No trust fund established under this section shall enter into an agreement with any other trust fund whereby the risks assumed by each are pooled or shared.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Board of trustees.</span></h2>
          <p>Every trust fund established under this section shall be governed by a board of no fewer than five trustees. The initial trustees need not be appointed or elected by the beneficiaries of the trust fund. During the second year following the creation of an authorized trust fund, at least one-fourth of all its trustees in office shall have been elected or appointed by the beneficiaries. After the end of the second year following the creation of an authorized trust fund, a majority of all trustees in office shall have been elected or appointed by the beneficiaries. All trustees serving during the first two years following the creation of an authorized trust fund shall be elected or appointed for one-year terms. All trustees serving thereafter shall be elected or appointed for two-year terms, provided that the trustees may be elected or appointed for one-year terms to the extent necessary in order to create staggered terms. Any trustee may be removed at any time, with or without cause, by a majority vote of the beneficiaries. The board of trustees shall meet no fewer than four times each year.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Trustees; compensation.</span></h2>
          <p>No trustee shall be paid a salary or receive other compensation for service as a trustee, except that the bylaws or plan of operation may provide for reimbursement for actual expenses incurred on behalf of the trust fund and for the payment of a reasonable per diem amount for attendance at meetings of the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Bylaws; plan of operation.</span></h2>
          <p>The trustees of each trust fund authorized under this section shall cause to be adopted a set of bylaws or plan of operation which shall govern the operation of the trust fund. All bylaws or plans of operation or amendments to them are subject to prior approval by the commissioner. The commissioner shall adopt rules governing the content and approval of bylaws or plans of operation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Financial statement; report on operations.</span></h2>
          <p>Every trust fund authorized under this section shall, by June 1 of every year, file with the commissioner a financial statement for the previous year's operations. The financial statement must include the opinion of a certified public accountant that the statement was prepared in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles. Also by June 1 of every year, every trust fund must file with the commissioner, on forms provided by the department, a report summarizing the trust fund's operations during the previous year.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Financial standards.</span></h2>
          <p>Every authorized trust fund shall have and maintain financial assets sufficient to satisfy all current and future financial obligations and responsibilities to beneficiaries. The commissioner shall adopt rules establishing minimum financial standards for authorized trust funds.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Contracts; fees.</span></h2>
          <p>Authorized trust funds may enter into contracts with risk management service providers, actuarial consultants, or other vendors as are necessary to ensure the effective and efficient operation of the trust fund. Fees paid to vendors for services provided must not be excessive.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Reinsurance.</span></h2>
          <p>Authorized trust funds may insure or reinsure their obligations and liabilities with:</p>
          <p>(1) insurance companies authorized to do business in Minnesota, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.06">60A.06</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) insurance companies similarly authorized in any other state of the United States;</p>
          <p>(3) insurance companies not authorized in Minnesota or any other state if the unauthorized insurance company establishes reinsurance security in favor of the ceding trust fund conforming to the general rules for allowance of reinsurance credits stated in the Financial Condition Examiners Handbook adopted by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners; or</p>
          <p>(4) other trust funds organized under this section or under similar laws of any other state if the reinsuring trust fund establishes reinsurance security as specified in clause (3) in favor of the ceding trust fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Interbeneficiary cause of action.</span></h2>
          <p>No beneficiary shall have any cause of action against any other beneficiary arising solely out of the insolvency or inability of the trust fund to meet its obligations.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Examination.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may examine authorized trust funds to the same extent and with the same purpose as is provided, with respect to insurance companies, by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.031">60A.031</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.19">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">Security deposit.</span></h2>
          <p>As a condition of authorization, every trust fund shall deposit with the commissioner an acceptable security of a value equal to not less than $500,000. In the event that a trust fund fails to honor the obligations assumed by it under trust agreements issued to its beneficiaries, use of the security deposit shall revert to the commissioner for the purpose of executing the trust fund's obligations to its beneficiaries. The commissioner shall adopt rules governing the amount of security required and the acceptable forms of security.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.20">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20.<span class="headnote">Rules.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may adopt rules to enforce and administer the requirements of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.21">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 21.<span class="headnote">Trust funds not subject to insurance rules.</span></h2>
          <p>Trust funds established under this section shall not be considered insurance companies or to be in the business of insurance nor shall they be subject to regulation by the commissioner, except as provided for in this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.22">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 22.<span class="headnote">Foreign trust funds.</span></h2>
          <p>A trust fund organized and existing under the laws of another state for the sole purpose of indemnifying nonprofit beneficiary organizations and their officers, directors, and agents for financial loss due to the imposition of legal liability or for damage or destruction of property, as provided in subdivisions 2 and 4, may apply to the commissioner for authority to operate within this state, provided that:</p>
          <p>(1) the trust fund has been continuously in operation for a period of not less than five years prior to the date it applies for authorization under this subdivision, during which period it must have issued only nonassessable indemnification agreements to its beneficiaries, and during each of those years the trust fund received not less than $1,000,000 in contributions from beneficiaries for protections afforded by the trust fund;</p>
          <p>(2) the trust fund has been authorized by and is subject to regulation and examination by the department of insurance of its domiciliary state;</p>
          <p>(3) the trust fund must file with the commissioner its trust agreement, bylaws or plan of operation, schedule of benefits, forms of indemnification agreements, and contribution schedules applicable to beneficiaries in this state;</p>
          <p>(4) the trust fund must be governed by a board of not fewer than five trustees, all of whom must be elected by the beneficiaries of the trust fund, and none of whom may receive compensation for service as a trustee;</p>
          <p>(5) the trust fund has, as of the last day of the calendar year immediately prior to its application for authority, a net fund balance surplus of not less than $1,000,000, as evidenced by its financial statements certified by an independent certified public accountant in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles consistently applied; and</p>
          <p>(6) the trust fund must, upon and at all times after authorization by the commissioner, maintain a registered office within this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.23">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 23.<span class="headnote">Standards for authorization.</span></h2>
          <p>Within 60 days after receipt of the documents specified under subdivision 22 and supporting evidence which establishes compliance with the standards set forth under that subdivision, the commissioner shall grant to the trust fund a certificate of authority to conduct operations in this state. The operations in this state are subject to the limitations and standards set forth in subdivisions 4 to 22. In the event an authorized foreign trust fund violates one of those subdivisions or the rules of the commissioner applicable to foreign trust funds, the commissioner may suspend or revoke the certificate of authority.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.29.24">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 24.<span class="headnote">Rules.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may adopt rules to enforce and administer requirements of subdivisions 22 and 23.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.29.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/455/#laws.0.8.0">1986 c 455 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/337/#laws.0.15.0">1987 c 337 s 15</a>-20</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.30"><b>60A.30</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.351">60A.351</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.31"><b>60A.31</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.352">60A.352</a>]
</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">EXPEDITED FORM AND RATE FILING</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.315">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.315 EXPEDITED FORM AND RATE FILING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.315.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority.</span></h2>
          <p>An insurer or rate service organization otherwise required to file rates and forms may use the expedited filing procedure under this section for homeowner's insurance as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/65A.27#stat.65A.27.4">65A.27, subdivision 4</a>, and automobile insurance as governed by chapter 65B.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.315.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Compliance certifications.</span></h2>
          <p>An insurer or rate service organization shall file with the Department of Commerce on a prescribed form a description of the policy, amendment, or endorsement and a written certification signed by an officer of the insurer or the rate service organization that the forms, policies, amendments, and endorsements comply with all applicable Minnesota statutes, rules, and case law, and a copy of the policy, amendment, or endorsement. If the filing will impact rates, the filing must comply with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/70A.06">70A.06</a>, subdivisions 1 and 1a. Forms and rates filed under this procedure are effective upon receipt by the department. Anyone using the expedited filing procedures authorized by this section must provide copies of the form filings within 24 hours of receiving a request from the commissioner. Insurers may comply with this requirement by providing the form filings in paper or electronic format.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.315.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Application of law.</span></h2>
          <p>If an insurer uses the services of a rate service organization for purposes of filing a certificate of compliance under this section, the certification by the rate service organization under subdivision 2 does not excuse the insurer from its obligation to ensure that its filing complies with all applicable Minnesota statutes, rules, and case law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.315.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Fees.</span></h2>
          <p>In order to be effective, the filing must be accompanied by payment of the filing fee applicable to the policy, amendment, endorsement, or rate unless the fee is remitted in accordance with an alternative procedure allowed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.14">60A.14</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.315.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Record keeping.</span></h2>
          <p>The insurer or rate service organization shall retain the policy, amendment, or endorsement for at least five years after that policy, amendment, or endorsement ceased providing coverage to any Minnesota policyholder, and shall provide to the Department of Commerce upon request a copy of any form in use pursuant to these filing procedures.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.315.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Audits; penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner is authorized to conduct audits and investigations under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/45.027">45.027</a> and this chapter to determine if the insurers are complying with Minnesota law in the issuance of policies described under this section. If the policy filings contain provisions that are inconsistent with or violate Minnesota law, the commissioner may take action against the insurer under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/45.027">45.027</a>. The commissioner shall assess the insurer for the costs of the investigation performed by the department and shall deposit all such assessments into the revolving fund established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.03">60A.03</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.315.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/74/#laws.0.3.0">2005 c 74 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CROP HAIL INSURANCE RATE FILING</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.32">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.32 RATE FILING FOR CROP HAIL INSURANCE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.32.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority.</span></h2>
          <p>An insurer issuing policies of insurance against crop damage by hail in this state shall file its insurance rates with the commissioner using the expedited filing procedure under subdivision 2. The insurance rates must be filed before February 1 of the year in which a policy is issued.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.32.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Compliance certifications.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to the proposed rates, an insurer shall file with the Department of Commerce on a form prescribed by the commissioner a written certification, signed by an officer of the insurer, that the rates comply with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/70A.04">70A.04</a>. Rates filed under this procedure are effective upon the date of receipt or on a subsequent date requested by the insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.32.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Fee.</span></h2>
          <p>In order to be effective, the filing must be accompanied by payment of the applicable filing fee.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.32.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/688/#laws.9.1.0">1988 c 688 art 9 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/24/#laws.0.1.0">1995 c 24 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/177/#laws.0.17.0">1999 c 177 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/178/#laws.1.17.0">2009 c 178 art 1 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CANCELLATION AND RENEWAL OF COMMERCIAL<br>LIABILITY AND/OR PROPERTY POLICIES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.35">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.35 SCOPE.</h1>
        <p>Except as specifically limited in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.351">60A.351</a>, sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.35">60A.35</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.38">60A.38</a> apply to all commercial liability and/or property insurance policies issued by companies licensed to do business in this state except ocean marine insurance, accident and health insurance, excess insurance, surplus lines insurance, and reinsurance.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.35.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/337/#laws.0.23.0">1987 c 337 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/485/#laws.0.65.0">1994 c 485 s 65</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.351">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.351 RENEWAL OF INSURANCE POLICY WITH ALTERED RATES.</h1>
        <p>If an insurance company licensed to do business in this state offers or purports to offer to renew any commercial liability and/or property insurance policy at less favorable terms as to the dollar amount of coverage or deductibles, higher rates, and/or higher rating plan, the new terms, the new rates and/or rating plan may take effect on the renewal date of the policy if the insurer has sent to the policyholder notice of the new terms, new rates and/or rating plan at least 30 days prior to the expiration date. If the insurer has not so notified the policyholder, the policyholder may elect to cancel the renewal policy within the 60-day period after receipt of the notice. Earned premium for the period of coverage, if any, shall be calculated pro rata upon the prior rate. This section does not apply to ocean marine insurance, accident and health insurance, reinsurance, and coverage under the federal Terrorism Risk Insurance Act.</p>
        <p>This section does not apply if the change relates to guide "a" rates or excess rates also known as "consent to rates" or if there has been any change in the risk insured.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.351.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/455/#laws.0.58.0">1986 c 455 s 58</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/337/#laws.0.21.0">1987 c 337 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/485/#laws.0.65.0">1994 c 485 s 65</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/330/#laws.0.2.0">2002 c 330 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/74/#laws.0.6.0">2005 c 74 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/104/#laws.0.1.0">2007 c 104 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.352">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.352 WORKERS' COMPENSATION INSURANCE.</h1>
        <p>In addition to the requirements of Minnesota Statutes 1984, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/176.185#stat.176.185.1">176.185, subdivision 1</a>, a policy of insurance issued to cover the liability to pay compensation under Minnesota Statutes 1984, chapter 176, shall comply with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.35">60A.35</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.38">60A.38</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.352.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/455/#laws.0.59.0">1986 c 455 s 59</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/337/#laws.0.22.0">1987 c 337 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/485/#laws.0.65.0">1994 c 485 s 65</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.36">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.36 MIDTERM CANCELLATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.36.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reason for cancellation.</span></h2>
          <p>No insurer may cancel a policy of commercial liability and/or property insurance during the term of the policy, except for one or more of the following reasons:</p>
          <p>(1) nonpayment of premium;</p>
          <p>(2) misrepresentation or fraud made by or with the knowledge of the insured in obtaining the policy or in pursuing a claim under the policy;</p>
          <p>(3) actions by the insured that have substantially increased or substantially changed the risk insured;</p>
          <p>(4) refusal of the insured to eliminate known conditions that increase the potential for loss after notification by the insurer that the condition must be removed;</p>
          <p>(5) substantial change in the risk assumed, except to the extent that the insurer should reasonably have foreseen the change or contemplated the risk in writing the contract;</p>
          <p>(6) loss of reinsurance by the insurer which provided coverage to the insurer for a significant amount of the underlying risk insured. A notice of cancellation under this clause shall advise the policyholder that the policyholder has ten days from the date of receipt of the notice to appeal the cancellation to the commissioner of commerce and that the commissioner will render a decision as to whether the cancellation is justified because of the loss of reinsurance within 30 business days after receipt of the appeal;</p>
          <p>(7) a determination by the commissioner that the continuation of the policy could place the insurer in violation of the insurance laws of this state; or</p>
          <p>(8) nonpayment of dues to an association or organization, other than an insurance association or organization, where payment of dues is a prerequisite to obtaining or continuing the insurance. This provision for cancellation for failure to pay dues does not apply to persons who are retired at 62 years of age or older or who are disabled according to Social Security standards.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.36.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Notice.</span></h2>
          <p>Cancellation under subdivision 1, clauses (2) to (8), shall not be effective before 60 days after notice to the policyholder. The notice of cancellation shall contain a specific reason for cancellation as provided in subdivision 1.</p>
          <p>A policy shall not be canceled for nonpayment of premium pursuant to subdivision 1, clause (1), unless the insurer, at least ten days before the effective cancellation date, has given notice to the policyholder of the amount of premium due and the due date. The notice shall state the effect of nonpayment by the due date. No cancellation for nonpayment of premium shall be effective if payment of the amount due is made before the effective date in the notice.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.36.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Third-party notices.</span></h2>
          <p>An insurer shall provide notice to a third party if:</p>
          <p>(1) the policyholder has, separately from the certificate, notified the insurer of the identity of the third party; and</p>
          <p>(2) the third party is a licensing authority authorized by statute to receive the notice or a state, city, or county governmental unit on whose behalf the insured is providing services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.36.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">New policies.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivisions 1 and 2 do not apply to any insurance policy that has not been previously renewed if the policy has been in effect less than 90 days at the time the notice of cancellation is mailed or delivered. No cancellation under this subdivision is effective until at least ten days after the written notice to the policyholder.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.36.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Longer-term policies.</span></h2>
          <p>A policy may be issued for a term longer than one year or for an indefinite term with a clause providing for cancellation by the insurer for the reasons stated in subdivision 1 by giving notice as required by subdivision 2 at least 60 days before any anniversary date.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.36.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Rescission.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) No insurer may rescind or void a contract of liability or property insurance unless there was material misrepresentation, material omission, or fraud made by or with the knowledge of the insured in obtaining the contract or in pursuing a claim under the policy.</p>
          <p>(b) No misrepresentation or omission shall be material unless knowledge by the insurer of the facts misrepresented or omitted would have led to a refusal by the insurer to make such a contract. In determining the question of materiality, evidence of the practice of the insurer with respect to the acceptance or rejection of similar risks shall be admissible.</p>
          <p>(c) For purposes of this section, a representation is a statement as to past or present fact, made to an insurer or the insurer's agent by the applicant as an inducement for issuing a contract of commercial liability or property insurance. A misrepresentation is a false representation, and the facts misrepresented are those facts which make the representation false.</p>
          <p>(d) This subdivision does not limit the right to cancel the policy prospectively for the reasons stated in subdivision 1, clause (2).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.36.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/337/#laws.0.24.0">1987 c 337 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/485/#laws.0.13.0">1994 c 485 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/446/#laws.1.7.0">1996 c 446 art 1 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/384/#laws.0.7.0">2010 c 384 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.37">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.37 NONRENEWAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.37.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Notice required.</span></h2>
          <p>At least 60 days before the date of expiration provided in the policy, a notice of intention not to renew the policy beyond the agreed expiration date must be made to the policyholder by the insurer. If the notice is not given at least 60 days before the date of expiration provided in the policy, the policy shall continue in force until 60 days after a notice of intent not to renew is received by the policyholder.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.37.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply if the policyholder has insured elsewhere, has accepted replacement coverage, or has requested or agreed to nonrenewal.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.37.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/337/#laws.0.25.0">1987 c 337 s 25</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.38">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.38 INTERPRETATION AND PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.38.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Sections not exclusive.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.35">60A.35</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.38">60A.38</a> are not exclusive, and the commissioner may also consider other provisions of Minnesota law to be applicable to the circumstances or situations addressed by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.35">60A.35</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.38">60A.38</a>. The rights provided by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.35">60A.35</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.38">60A.38</a> are in addition to and do not prejudice any other rights the policyholder may have at common law, under statute, or rules.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.38.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>A violation of any provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.35">60A.35</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.38">60A.38</a> shall be deemed to be an unfair trade practice in the business of insurance and shall subject the violator to the penalties provided by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/72A.17">72A.17</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/72A.32">72A.32</a> in addition to any other penalty provided by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.38.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Notices required.</span></h2>
          <p>All notices required by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.35">60A.35</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.38">60A.38</a> shall only be made by first class mail addressed to the policyholder's last known address or by delivery to the policyholder's last known address. Notice by first class mail is effective upon deposit in the United States mail. In addition to giving notice to the policyholder, the insurer must also give notice to the agent of record, if any, in the manner specified for the policyholder.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.38.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Proof of mailing notice.</span></h2>
          <p>Unless otherwise specifically required, United States Postal Service proof of mailing of the notice of cancellation, reduction in the limits of liability of coverage, or nonrenewal of an insurance policy is sufficient proof the proper notice has been given.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.38.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/337/#laws.0.26.0">1987 c 337 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/475/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 475 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CERTIFICATES OF INSURANCE</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.39">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.39 CERTIFICATES OF INSURANCE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.39.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Issuance.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensed insurer or insurance producer may provide to a third party a certificate of insurance which documents insurance coverage. For the purposes of this chapter, a certificate of insurance is a document that provides evidence of property or liability insurance coverage and the amount of insurance issued, and does not convey any contractual rights to the certificate holder.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.39.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Approval.</span></h2>
          <p>An insurer or licensed producer shall not issue a certificate of insurance or other document or instrument that either affirmatively or negatively amends, extends, or alters the coverage provided by an approved policy, form, or endorsement without the written approval of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.39.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Required statement.</span></h2>
          <p>A certificate or memorandum of property or casualty insurance when issued to any person other than the policyholder must contain the following or similar statement: "This certificate or memorandum of insurance does not affirmatively or negatively amend, extend, or alter the coverage afforded by the insurance policy."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.39.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Cancellation notice.</span></h2>
          <p>A certificate provided to a third party must not provide for notice of cancellation that exceeds the statutory notice of cancellation provided to the policyholder or a period of notice specified in the policy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.39.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Filing.</span></h2>
          <p>An insurer not using the standard ACORD or ISO form "Certificate of Insurance" shall file with the commissioner, prior to its use, a similar alternative "Certificate of Insurance" covering the same information for use by the insurer. Filed forms may not be amended at the request of a third party.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.39.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Opinion letters.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensed insurance producer may not issue, in lieu of a certificate, an agent's opinion letter or other correspondence that is inconsistent with this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.39.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/178/#laws.1.18.0">2009 c 178 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/384/#laws.0.8.0">2010 c 384 s 8</a>-10</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.40"><b>60A.40</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/446/#laws.1.72.0">1996 c 446 art 1 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/339/#laws.0.12.0">1998 c 339 s 12</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">SUBROGATION AGAINST INSURED</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.41">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.41 SUBROGATION AGAINST INSUREDS PROHIBITED.</h1>
        <p>(a) An insurance company providing insurance coverage or its reinsurer for that underlying insurance coverage may not proceed against its insured in a subrogation action where the loss was caused by the nonintentional acts of the insured.</p>
        <p>(b) An insurance company providing insurance coverage or its reinsurer for that underlying insurance coverage may not subrogate itself to the rights of its insured to proceed against another person if that other person is insured for the same loss, by the same company. This provision applies only if the loss was caused by the nonintentional acts of the person against whom subrogation is sought.</p>
        <p>(c) This provision does not apply to or affect claims of a surety against its principal.</p>
        <p>(d) Nothing in this section prevents an insurer from allocating the loss internally to the at-fault insured for purposes of underwriting, agency, and claims information.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.41.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/201/#laws.0.1.0">1989 c 201 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/399/#laws.0.1.0">1990 c 399 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">DISABILITY INCOME COVERAGE</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.42">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.42 DISABILITY INCOME COVERAGE; PROHIBITED PROVISION.</h1>
        <p>No policy, contract, certificate, or agreement offered or issued in this state providing for disability income protection coverage may contain a provision purporting to reserve discretion to the insurer to interpret the terms of the contract or provide a standard of review that is inconsistent with the laws of this state, or less favorable to the enrollee when a claim is denied than a preponderance of the evidence standard.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.42.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/59/#laws.0.1.0">2015 c 59 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.43">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.43 DISABILITY INCOME COVERAGE; DISCLOSURE.</h1>
        <p>(a) No contract or policy of long-term disability insurance that limits the duration of coverage for mental health or substance use disorders shall be offered in this state without a disclosure, provided at the time of application, that includes the following:</p>
        <p>(1) a notification that the long-term disability coverage selected by the potential policyholder or plan sponsor limits the duration of coverage for mental health or substance use disorders; and</p>
        <p>(2) that the potential policyholder or plan sponsor has the right to request more information about the limitation and other coverage options that include an unlimited duration, if available.</p>
        <p>(b) Receipt of the disclosure described in paragraph (a) must be acknowledged by the potential policyholder or plan sponsor and evidence of the disclosure and acknowledgment must be retained by the insurance company offering the coverage for a period of no less than two years.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.43.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/114/#laws.1.2.0">2024 c 114 art 1 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">RISK-BASED CAPITAL FOR HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.50">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.50 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a>, the terms in subdivisions 2 to 13 have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Adjusted RBC report.</span></h2>
          <p>"Adjusted RBC report" means an RBC report which has been adjusted by the commissioner in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.51#stat.60A.51.3">60A.51, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of commerce or the commissioner of health, whichever commissioner otherwise regulates the health organization.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Corrective order.</span></h2>
          <p>"Corrective order" means an order issued by the commissioner specifying corrective actions which the commissioner has determined are required.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Domestic health organization.</span></h2>
          <p>"Domestic health organization" means a health organization domiciled in this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Foreign health organization.</span></h2>
          <p>"Foreign health organization" means a health organization that is licensed to do business in this state but is not domiciled in this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">NAIC.</span></h2>
          <p>"NAIC" means the National Association of Insurance Commissioners.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Health organization.</span></h2>
          <p>"Health organization" means an entity licensed under this chapter or chapter 62C or 62D. This definition does not include an organization that is licensed or regulated as either a life and health insurer or a property and casualty insurer that is otherwise subject to either the life or property and casualty risk-based capital requirements.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">RBC instructions.</span></h2>
          <p>"RBC instructions" means the RBC report including risk-based capital instructions adopted by the NAIC, as these RBC instructions may be amended by the NAIC from time to time in accordance with the procedures adopted by the NAIC.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">RBC level.</span></h2>
          <p>"RBC level" means a health organization's company action level RBC, regulatory action level RBC, authorized control level RBC, or mandatory control level RBC where:</p>
          <p>(1) "company action level RBC" means, with respect to any health organization, the product of 2.0 and its authorized control level RBC;</p>
          <p>(2) "regulatory action level RBC" means the product of 1.5 and its authorized control level RBC;</p>
          <p>(3) "authorized control level RBC" means the number determined under the risk-based capital formula in accordance with the RBC instructions; and</p>
          <p>(4) "mandatory control level RBC" means the product of .70 and the authorized control level RBC.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">RBC plan.</span></h2>
          <p>"RBC plan" means a comprehensive financial plan containing the elements specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.52#stat.60A.52.2">60A.52, subdivision 2</a>. If the commissioner rejects the RBC plan, and it is revised by the health organization, with or without the commissioner's recommendation, the plan must be called the "revised RBC plan."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">RBC report.</span></h2>
          <p>"RBC report" means the report required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.51">60A.51</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.50.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Total adjusted capital.</span></h2>
          <p>"Total adjusted capital" means the sum of:</p>
          <p>(1) a health organization's statutory capital and surplus as determined in accordance with the statutory accounting applicable to the annual financial statements required to be filed; and</p>
          <p>(2) such other items, if any, as the RBC instructions may provide.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.50.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.1.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.51">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.51 RBC REPORTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.51.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Submissions.</span></h2>
          <p>A domestic health organization shall, on or before each April 1, prepare and submit to the commissioner a report of its RBC levels as of the end of the calendar year just ended, in a form and containing the information required by the RBC instructions. In addition, a domestic health organization shall file its RBC report:</p>
          <p>(1) with the NAIC in accordance with the RBC instructions; and</p>
          <p>(2) with the insurance commissioner in any state in which the health organization is authorized to do business, if the insurance commissioner has notified the health organization of its request in writing, in which case the health organization shall file its RBC report not later than the later of:</p>
          <p>(i) 15 days from the receipt of notice to file its RBC report with that state; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the filing date.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.51.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Determination.</span></h2>
          <p>A health organization's RBC must be determined in accordance with the formula set forth in the RBC instructions. The formula must take the following into account, and may adjust for the covariance between, determined in each case by applying the factors in the manner set forth in the RBC instructions:</p>
          <p>(1) asset risk;</p>
          <p>(2) credit risk;</p>
          <p>(3) underwriting risk; and</p>
          <p>(4) all other business risks and such other relevant risks as are set forth in the RBC instructions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.51.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Excess of capital.</span></h2>
          <p>An excess of capital (net worth) over the amount produced by the risk-based capital requirements contained in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a> and the formulas, schedules, and instructions referenced in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a> is desirable in the business of health insurance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.51.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Adjusted report.</span></h2>
          <p>If a domestic health organization files an RBC report that in the judgment of the commissioner is inaccurate, then the commissioner shall adjust the RBC report to correct the inaccuracy and shall notify the health organization of the adjustment. The notice must contain a statement of the reason for the adjustment. An RBC report as so adjusted is referred to as an "adjusted RBC report."</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.51.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.2.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/26/#laws.3.1.0">2019 c 26 art 3 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.52">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.52 COMPANY ACTION LEVEL EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.52.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Company action level event" means the following events:</p>
          <p>(1) the filing of an RBC report by a health organization that indicates that the health organization's total adjusted capital is greater than or equal to its regulatory action level RBC but less than its company action level RBC. If a health organization has total adjusted capital greater than or equal to its company action level RBC but less than the product of its authorized control level RBC multiplied by three, and triggers the trend test determined in accordance with the trend test calculation included in the health RBC instructions;</p>
          <p>(2) notification by the commissioner to the health organization of an adjusted RBC report that indicates an event in clause (1), provided the health organization does not challenge the adjusted RBC report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>; or</p>
          <p>(3) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>, a health organization challenges an adjusted RBC report that indicates the event in clause (1), the notification by the commissioner to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the health organization's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.52.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">RBC plan required.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a company action level event, the health organization shall prepare and submit to the commissioner an RBC plan that:</p>
          <p>(1) identifies the conditions that contribute to the company action level event;</p>
          <p>(2) contains proposals of corrective actions that the health organization intends to take and that would be expected to result in the elimination of the company action level event;</p>
          <p>(3) provides projections of the health organization's financial results in the current year and at least the two succeeding years, both in the absence of proposed corrective actions and giving effect to the proposed corrective actions, including projections of statutory balance sheets, operating income, net income, capital and surplus, and RBC levels. The projections for both new and renewal business might include separate projections for each major line of business and separately identify each significant income, expense, and benefit component;</p>
          <p>(4) identifies the key assumptions impacting the health organization's projections and the sensitivity of the projections to the assumptions; and</p>
          <p>(5) identifies the quality of, and problems associated with, the health organization's business, including, but not limited to, its assets, anticipated business growth and associated surplus strain, extraordinary exposure to risk, mix of business, and use of reinsurance, if any, in each case.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.52.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">RBC plan submission.</span></h2>
          <p>The RBC plan must be submitted:</p>
          <p>(1) within 45 days of the company action level event; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the health organization challenges an adjusted RBC report pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>, within 45 days after notification to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the health organization's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.52.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">RBC plan implementation.</span></h2>
          <p>Within 60 days after the submission by a health organization of an RBC plan to the commissioner, the commissioner shall notify the health organization whether the RBC plan must be implemented or is, in the judgment of the commissioner, unsatisfactory. If the commissioner determines the RBC plan is unsatisfactory, the notification to the health organization must set forth the reasons for the determination, and may set forth proposed revisions which will render the RBC plan satisfactory, in the judgment of the commissioner. Upon notification from the commissioner, the health organization shall prepare a revised RBC plan, which may incorporate by reference any revisions proposed by the commissioner, and shall submit the revised RBC plan to the commissioner:</p>
          <p>(1) within 45 days after the notification from the commissioner; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the health organization challenges the notification from the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>, within 45 days after a notification to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the health organization's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.52.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Unsatisfactory plan.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a notification by the commissioner to a health organization that the health organization's RBC plan or revised RBC plan is unsatisfactory, the commissioner may, at the commissioner's discretion, subject to the health organization's right to a hearing under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>, specify in the notification that the notification constitutes a regulatory action level event.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.52.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Additional filing.</span></h2>
          <p>Every domestic health organization that files an RBC plan or revised RBC plan with the commissioner shall file a copy of the RBC plan or revised RBC plan with the insurance commissioner in any state in which the health organization is authorized to do business if:</p>
          <p>(1) the state has an RBC provision substantially similar in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.57#stat.60A.57.1">60A.57, subdivision 1</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) the insurance commissioner of that state has notified the health organization of its request for the filing in writing, in which case the health organization shall file a copy of the RBC plan or revised RBC plan in that state no later than the later of:</p>
          <p>(i) 15 days after the receipt of notice to file a copy of its RBC plan or revised RBC plan with the state; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the date on which the RBC plan or revised RBC plan is filed under subdivisions 3 and 4.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.52.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.3.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/26/#laws.3.2.0">2019 c 26 art 3 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.53">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.53 REGULATORY ACTION LEVEL EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.53.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Regulatory action level event" means, with respect to a health organization, any of the following events:</p>
          <p>(1) the filing of an RBC report by the health organization that indicates that the health organization's total adjusted capital is greater than or equal to its authorized control level RBC but less than its regulatory action level RBC;</p>
          <p>(2) notification by the commissioner to a health organization of an adjusted RBC report that indicates the event in clause (1), provided the health organization does not challenge the adjusted RBC report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>, the health organization challenges an adjusted RBC report that indicates the event in clause (1), the notification by the commissioner to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the health organization's challenge;</p>
          <p>(4) the failure of the health organization to file an RBC report by the filing date, unless the health organization has provided an explanation for the failure that is satisfactory to the commissioner and has cured the failure within ten days after the filing date;</p>
          <p>(5) the failure of the health organization to submit an RBC plan to the commissioner within the time period set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.52#stat.60A.52.3">60A.52, subdivision 3</a>;</p>
          <p>(6) notification by the commissioner to the health organization that:</p>
          <p>(i) the RBC plan or revised RBC plan submitted by the health organization is, in the judgment of the commissioner, unsatisfactory; and</p>
          <p>(ii) notification constitutes a regulatory action level event with respect to the health organization, provided the health organization has not challenged the determination under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>;</p>
          <p>(7) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>, the health organization challenges a determination by the commissioner under clause (6), the notification by the commissioner to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the challenge;</p>
          <p>(8) notification by the commissioner to the health organization that the health organization has failed to adhere to its RBC plan or revised RBC plan, but only if the failure has a substantial adverse effect on the ability of the health organization to eliminate the company action level event in accordance with its RBC plan or revised RBC plan and the commissioner has so stated in the notification, provided the health organization has not challenged the determination under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a>; or</p>
          <p>(9) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>, the health organization challenges a determination by the commissioner under clause (8), the notification by the commissioner to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.53.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's duties.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a regulatory action level event the commissioner shall:</p>
          <p>(1) require the health organization to prepare and submit an RBC plan or, if applicable, a revised RBC plan;</p>
          <p>(2) perform any examination or analysis the commissioner considers necessary of the assets, liabilities, and operations of the health organization, including a review of its RBC plan or revised RBC plan; and</p>
          <p>(3) after the examination or analysis, issue a corrective order specifying the corrective actions the commissioner determines are required.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.53.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Corrective actions.</span></h2>
          <p>In determining corrective actions, the commissioner may take into account factors the commissioner considers relevant with respect to the health organization based upon the commissioner's examination or analysis of the assets, liabilities, and operations of the health organization, including, but not limited to, the results of any sensitivity tests undertaken pursuant to the RBC instructions. The RBC plan or revised RBC plan must be submitted:</p>
          <p>(1) within 45 days after the occurrence of the regulatory action level event;</p>
          <p>(2) if the health organization challenges an adjusted RBC report pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a> and the challenge is not frivolous in the judgment of the commissioner within 45 days after the notification to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the health organization's challenge; or</p>
          <p>(3) if the health organization challenges a revised RBC plan pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a> and the challenge is not frivolous in the judgment of the commissioner, within 45 days after the notification to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the health organization's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.53.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Consultants.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may retain actuaries and investment experts and other consultants as may be necessary in the judgment of the commissioner to review the health organization's RBC plan or revised RBC plan, examine or analyze the assets, liabilities, and operations, including contractual relationships, of the health organization and formulate the corrective order with respect to the health organization. The fees, costs, and expenses relating to consultants must be borne by the affected health organization or such other party as directed by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.53.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.4.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.54">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.54 AUTHORIZED CONTROL LEVEL EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.54.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Authorized control level event" means any of the following events:</p>
          <p>(1) the filing of an RBC report by the health organization that indicates that the health organization's total adjusted capital is greater than or equal to its mandatory control level RBC but less than its authorized control level RBC;</p>
          <p>(2) the notification by the commissioner to the health organization of an adjusted RBC report that indicates the event in clause (1), provided the health organization does not challenge the adjusted RBC report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>, the health organization challenges an adjusted RBC report that indicates the event in clause (1), notification by the commissioner to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the health organization's challenge;</p>
          <p>(4) the failure of the health organization to respond, in a manner satisfactory to the commissioner, to a corrective order, provided the health organization has not challenged the corrective order under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>; or</p>
          <p>(5) if the health organization has challenged a corrective order under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a> and the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the challenge or modified the corrective order, the failure of the health organization to respond, in a manner satisfactory to the commissioner, to the corrective order subsequent to rejection or modification by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.54.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's duties.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of an authorized control level event with respect to a health organization, the commissioner shall:</p>
          <p>(1) take such actions as are required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.53">60A.53</a> regarding a health organization with respect to which a regulatory action level event has occurred; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the commissioner considers it to be in the best interests of the policyholders and creditors of the health organization and of the public, take such actions as are necessary to cause the health organization to be placed under regulatory control under chapter 60B. In the event the commissioner takes such actions, the authorized control level event is considered sufficient grounds for the commissioner to take action under chapter 60B, and the commissioner shall have the rights, powers, and duties with respect to the health organization as are set forth in chapter 60B. In the event the commissioner takes actions under this clause pursuant to an adjusted RBC report, the health organization is entitled to the protections afforded health organizations under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.11">60B.11</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.13">60B.13</a> pertaining to summary proceedings.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.54.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.5.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.55">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.55 MANDATORY CONTROL LEVEL EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.55.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Mandatory control level event" means any of the following events:</p>
          <p>(1) the filing of an RBC report which indicates that the health organization's total adjusted capital is less than its mandatory control level RBC;</p>
          <p>(2) notification by the commissioner to the health organization of an adjusted RBC report that indicates the event in clause (1), provided the health organization does not challenge the adjusted RBC report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>; or</p>
          <p>(3) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.56">60A.56</a>, the health organization challenges an adjusted RBC report that indicates the event in clause (1), notification by the commissioner to the health organization that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the health organization's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.55.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's duties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) In the event of a mandatory control level event, the commissioner shall take such actions as are necessary to place the health organization under regulatory control under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.13">60B.13</a>. In that event, the mandatory control level event is considered sufficient grounds for the commissioner to take action under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.13">60B.13</a>, and the commissioner shall have the rights, powers, and duties with respect to the health organization as are set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.13">60B.13</a>. If the commissioner takes actions pursuant to an adjusted RBC report, the health organization is entitled to the protections of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.11">60B.11</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.13">60B.13</a> pertaining to summary proceedings.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), the commissioner may forgo action for up to 90 days after the mandatory control level event if the commissioner finds there is a reasonable expectation that the mandatory control level event may be eliminated within the 90-day period.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.55.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.6.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.56">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.56 HEARINGS.</h1>
        <p>Upon the occurrence of any of the following events, the health organization has the right to a confidential departmental hearing, on a record, at which the health organization may challenge any determination or action by the commissioner. The health organization shall notify the commissioner of its request for a hearing within five days after the notification by the commissioner under clause (1), (2), (3), or (4). Upon receipt of the health organization's request for a hearing, the commissioner shall set a date for the hearing, which must be no less than ten nor more than 30 days after the date of the health organization's request. The events include:</p>
        <p>(1) notification to a health organization by the commissioner of an adjusted RBC report;</p>
        <p>(2) notification to a health organization by the commissioner that:</p>
        <p>(i) the health organization's RBC plan or revised RBC plan is unsatisfactory; and</p>
        <p>(ii) notification constitutes a regulatory action level event with respect to the health organization;</p>
        <p>(3) notification to a health organization by the commissioner that the health organization has failed to adhere to its RBC plan or revised RBC plan and that the failure has a substantial adverse effect on the ability of the health organization to eliminate the company action level event with respect to the health organization in accordance with its RBC plan or revised RBC plan; or</p>
        <p>(4) notification to a health organization by the commissioner of a corrective order with respect to the health organization.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.56.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.7.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.57">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.57 ACCESS TO AND USE OF RBC INFORMATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.57.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Confidentiality; prohibition on announcements.</span></h2>
          <p>Section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.67">60A.67</a>, subdivisions 1 and 2, apply to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.57.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibition for rate making or premium setting.</span></h2>
          <p>The RBC instructions, RBC reports, adjusted RBC reports, RBC plans, and revised RBC plans are intended solely for use by the commissioner in monitoring the solvency of health organizations and the need for possible corrective action with respect to health organizations and shall not be used by the commissioner for rate making nor considered or introduced as evidence in any rate proceeding nor used by the commissioner to calculate or derive any elements of an appropriate premium level or rate of return for any line of insurance that a health organization or any affiliate is authorized to write.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.57.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.8.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.58">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.58 SUPPLEMENTAL PROVISIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.58.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Effect.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a> are supplemental to any other provisions of the laws of this state, and must not preclude or limit any other powers or duties of the commissioner under such laws, including, but not limited to, chapter 60B and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62D.041">62D.041</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62D.042">62D.042</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62D.18">62D.18</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62D.181">62D.181</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.58.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Exemption.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may exempt from the application of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a> a domestic health organization that:</p>
          <p>(1) writes direct business only in this state;</p>
          <p>(2) assumes no reinsurance in excess of five percent of direct premium written; and</p>
          <p>(3) writes direct annual premiums for comprehensive medical business of $2,000,000 or less.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.58.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.9.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 9</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.59">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.59 FOREIGN HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.59.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">RBC report.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A foreign health organization shall, upon the written request of the commissioner, submit to the commissioner an RBC report as of the end of the calendar year just ended the later of:</p>
          <p>(1) the date an RBC report would be required to be filed by a domestic health organization under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) 15 days after the request is received by the foreign health organization.</p>
          <p>(b) A foreign health organization shall, at the written request of the commissioner, promptly submit to the commissioner a copy of any RBC plan that is filed with the insurance commissioner of any other state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.59.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">RBC plan.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a company action level event, regulatory action level event, or authorized control level event with respect to a foreign health organization as determined under the RBC statute applicable in the state of domicile of the health organization or, if no RBC statute is in force in that state, under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a>, if the insurance commissioner of the state of domicile of the foreign health organization fails to require the foreign health organization to file an RBC plan in the manner specified under that state's RBC statute or, if no RBC statute is in force in that state, under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.52">60A.52</a>, the commissioner may require the foreign health organization to file an RBC plan with the commissioner. In such event, the failure of the foreign health organization to file an RBC plan with the commissioner shall be grounds to order the health organization to cease and desist from writing new insurance business in this state. This section does not limit the commissioner's authority to require a foreign insurer to file a copy of the risk-based capital plan submitted to the commissioner in the state of domicile.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.59.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Liquidation of property.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a mandatory control level event with respect to a foreign health organization, if no domiciliary receiver has been appointed with respect to the foreign health organization under the rehabilitation and liquidation statute applicable in the state of domicile of the foreign health organization, the commissioner may make application to the district court permitted under chapter 60B with respect to the liquidation of property of foreign health organizations found in this state, and the occurrence of the mandatory control level event shall be considered adequate grounds for the application.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.59.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.10.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
