      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.591">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.591 IMMUNITY.</h1>
        <p>There is no liability on the part of, and no cause of action arises against, the commissioner or the department or its employees or agents for any action taken by them in the performance of their powers and duties under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.591.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.11.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 11</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.592">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.592 NOTICES.</h1>
        <p>All notices by the commissioner to a health organization that may result in regulatory action under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.50">60A.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.592">60A.592</a> are effective upon dispatch if transmitted by registered or certified mail, or in the case of any other transmission are effective upon the health organization's receipt of notice.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.592.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.1.12.0">2004 c 285 art 1 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">REGULATION OF RISK-BASED CAPITAL</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.60">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.60 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Adjusted risk-based capital report.</span></h2>
          <p>"Adjusted risk-based capital report" means a risk-based capital report that has been adjusted by the commissioner according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.61#stat.60A.61.5">60A.61, subdivision 5</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Corrective order.</span></h2>
          <p>"Corrective order" means an order issued by the commissioner specifying corrective actions that the commissioner has determined are required.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Domestic insurer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Domestic insurer" means an insurance company incorporated or organized in this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Foreign insurer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Foreign insurer" means an insurance company that is admitted to do business in this state under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.19">60A.19</a> but is not incorporated or organized in this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">NAIC.</span></h2>
          <p>"NAIC" means the National Association of Insurance Commissioners.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Life and/or health insurer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Life and/or health insurer" means an insurance company authorized to transact business under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.06#stat.60A.06.1">60A.06, subdivision 1</a>, clause (4), or a property and casualty insurer transacting business only under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.06#stat.60A.06.1">60A.06, subdivision 1</a>, clause (5)(a).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Property and casualty insurer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Property and casualty insurer" means an insurance company authorized to transact business under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.06#stat.60A.06.1">60A.06, subdivision 1</a>, clauses (1), (2), (3), (5), (6), (8), (9), (10), (11), (12), (13), (14), and (15), but does not include monoline mortgage guaranty insurers, and financial guaranty insurers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Negative trend.</span></h2>
          <p>"Negative trend" means negative trend over a period of time, as determined according to the "trend test calculation" included in the risk-based capital instructions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Risk-based capital instructions.</span></h2>
          <p>"Risk-based capital instructions" means the risk-based capital report including risk-based capital instructions adopted by the NAIC, as those risk-based instructions may be amended by the NAIC from time to time according to the procedures adopted by the NAIC.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Risk-based capital level.</span></h2>
          <p>"Risk-based capital level" means an insurer's company action level risk-based capital, regulatory action level risk-based capital, authorized control level risk-based capital, or mandatory control level risk-based capital where:</p>
          <p>(1) "company action level risk-based capital" means, with respect to an insurer, the product of 2.0 and its authorized control level risk-based capital;</p>
          <p>(2) "regulatory action level risk-based capital" means the product of 1.5 and its authorized control level risk-based capital;</p>
          <p>(3) "authorized control level risk-based capital" means the number determined under the risk-based capital formula according to the risk-based capital instructions;</p>
          <p>(4) "mandatory control level risk-based capital" means the product of .70 and the authorized control level risk-based capital.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Risk-based capital plan.</span></h2>
          <p>"Risk-based capital plan" means a comprehensive financial plan containing the elements specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.62#stat.60A.62.2">60A.62, subdivision 2</a>. If the commissioner rejects the risk-based capital plan, and it is revised by the insurer, with or without the commissioner's recommendation, the plan must be called the "revised risk-based capital plan."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Risk-based capital report.</span></h2>
          <p>"Risk-based capital report" means the report required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.61">60A.61</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.60.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Total adjusted capital.</span></h2>
          <p>"Total adjusted capital" means the sum of:</p>
          <p>(1) an insurer's statutory capital and surplus as determined in accordance with statutory accounting applicable to the annual statement required to be filed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.13">60A.13</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) other items, if any, as the risk-based capital instructions may provide.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.60.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.2.0">1995 c 253 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/61/#laws.0.2.0">2011 c 61 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.61">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.61 RISK-BASED CAPITAL REPORTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.61.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">General requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>Every domestic insurer shall, on or before each March 1, prepare and submit to the commissioner a report of its risk-based capital levels as of the end of the calendar year just ended, in a form and containing the information required by the risk-based capital instructions. In addition, every domestic insurer shall file its risk-based capital report:</p>
          <p>(1) with the NAIC according to the risk-based capital instructions; and</p>
          <p>(2) with the insurance commissioner in a state in which the insurer is authorized to do business, if the insurance commissioner has notified the insurer of its request in writing, in which case the insurer shall file its risk-based capital report not later than the later of:</p>
          <p>(i) 15 days from the receipt of notice to file its risk-based capital report with that state; or</p>
          <p>(ii) March 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.61.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Life and/or health insurers.</span></h2>
          <p>A life and/or health insurer's risk-based capital must be determined according to the formula set forth in the risk-based capital instructions. The formula must take into account, and may adjust for the covariance between:</p>
          <p>(1) the risk with respect to the insurer's assets;</p>
          <p>(2) the risk of adverse insurance experience with respect to the insurer's liabilities and obligations;</p>
          <p>(3) the interest rate risk with respect to the insurer's business; and</p>
          <p>(4) all other business risks and other relevant risks set forth in the risk-based capital instructions;</p>
          <p class="bl">determined in each case by applying the factors in the manner set forth in the risk-based capital instructions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.61.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Property and casualty insurers.</span></h2>
          <p>A property and casualty insurer's risk-based capital must be determined according to the formula set forth in the risk-based capital instructions. The formula must take into account, and may adjust for the covariance between:</p>
          <p>(1) asset risk;</p>
          <p>(2) credit risk;</p>
          <p>(3) underwriting risk; and</p>
          <p>(4) all other business risks and other relevant risks set forth in the risk-based capital instructions;</p>
          <p class="bl">determined in each case by applying the factors in the manner set forth in the risk-based capital instructions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.61.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Maintaining additional capital.</span></h2>
          <p>An excess of capital over the amount produced by the risk-based capital requirements contained in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a> and the formulas, schedules, and instructions referenced in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a> is desirable in the business of insurance. Accordingly, insurers should seek to maintain capital above the risk-based capital levels required by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a>. Additional capital is used and useful in the insurance business and helps to secure an insurer against various risks inherent in, or affecting, the business of insurance and not accounted for or only partially measured by the risk-based capital requirements contained in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.61.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Adjusted risk-based capital report.</span></h2>
          <p>If a domestic insurer files a risk-based capital report that in the judgment of the commissioner is inaccurate, then the commissioner shall adjust the risk-based capital report to correct the inaccuracy and shall notify the insurer of the adjustment. The notice must contain a statement of the reason for the adjustment. A risk-based capital report as so adjusted is referred to as an "adjusted risk-based capital report."</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.61.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.3.0">1995 c 253 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.62">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.62 COMPANY ACTION LEVEL EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.62.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Company action level event" means any of the following events:</p>
          <p>(1) the filing of a risk-based capital report by an insurer which indicates that:</p>
          <p>(i) the insurer's total adjusted capital is greater than or equal to its regulatory action level risk-based capital but less than its company action level risk-based capital;</p>
          <p>(ii) if a life and/or health insurer, the insurer has total adjusted capital that is greater than or equal to its company action level risk-based capital but less than the product of its authorized control level risk-based capital and 3.0 and has a negative trend; or</p>
          <p>(iii) if a property and casualty insurer, the insurer has total adjusted capital which is greater than or equal to its company action level risk-based capital but less than the product of its authorized control level risk-based capital and 3.0 and triggers the trend test determined in accordance with the trend test calculation included in the property and casualty risk-based capital instructions;</p>
          <p>(2) the notification by the commissioner to the insurer of an adjusted risk-based capital report that indicates an event in clause (1), provided the insurer does not challenge the adjusted risk-based report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>; or</p>
          <p>(3) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>, an insurer challenges an adjusted risk-based capital report that indicates the event in clause (1), the notification by the commissioner to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the insurer's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.62.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Plan.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a company action level event, the insurer shall prepare and submit to the commissioner a risk-based capital plan that:</p>
          <p>(1) identifies the conditions that contribute to the company action level event;</p>
          <p>(2) contains proposals of corrective actions that the insurer intends to take and would be expected to result in the elimination of the company action level event;</p>
          <p>(3) provides projections of the insurer's financial results in the current year and at least the four succeeding years, both in the absence of proposed corrective actions and giving effect to the proposed corrective actions, including projected statutory balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements. The projections for both new and renewal business might include separate projections for each major line of business and separately identify each significant income, expense, and benefit component;</p>
          <p>(4) identifies the key assumptions impacting the insurer's projections and the sensitivity of the projections to the assumptions; and</p>
          <p>(5) identifies the quality of, and problems associated with, the insurer's business, including, but not limited to, its assets, anticipated business growth and associated surplus strain, extraordinary exposure to risk, mix of business, and use of reinsurance, if any, in each case.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.62.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Submission.</span></h2>
          <p>The risk-based capital plan must be submitted:</p>
          <p>(1) within 45 days of the company action level event; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the insurer challenges an adjusted risk-based capital report pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>, within 45 days after notification to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the insurer's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.62.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Notification by commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>Within 60 days after the submission by an insurer of a risk-based capital plan to the commissioner, the commissioner shall notify the insurer whether the risk-based capital plan must be implemented or is, in the judgment of the commissioner, unsatisfactory. If the commissioner determines the risk-based capital plan is unsatisfactory, the notification to the insurer must set forth the reasons for the determination, and may set forth proposed revisions that will render the risk-based capital plan satisfactory, in the judgment of the commissioner. Upon notification from the commissioner, the insurer shall prepare a revised risk-based capital plan, that may incorporate by reference any revisions proposed by the commissioner, and shall submit the revised risk-based capital plan to the commissioner:</p>
          <p>(1) within 45 days after the notification from the commissioner; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the insurer challenges the notification from the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>, within 45 days after a notification to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the insurer's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.62.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Unsatisfactory plan.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a notification by the commissioner to an insurer that the insurer's risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan is unsatisfactory, the commissioner may at the commissioner's discretion, subject to the insurer's right to a hearing under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>, specify in the notification that the notification constitutes a regulatory action level event.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.62.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Filings to other states.</span></h2>
          <p>Every domestic insurer that files a risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan with the commissioner shall file a copy of the risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan with the insurance commissioner in any state in which the insurer is authorized to do business if:</p>
          <p>(1) the state has a risk-based capital provision substantially similar to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.67#stat.60A.67.1">60A.67, subdivision 1</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) the insurance commissioner of that state has notified the insurer of its request for the filing in writing, in which case the insurer shall file a copy of the risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan in that state no later than the later of:</p>
          <p>(i) 15 days after the receipt of notice to file a copy of its risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based plan with the state; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the date on which the risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan is filed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.62">60A.62</a>, subdivisions 3 and 4.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.62.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.4.0">1995 c 253 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/135/#laws.3.8.0">2013 c 135 art 3 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.63">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.63 REGULATORY ACTION LEVEL EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.63.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Regulatory action level event" means, with respect to an insurer, any of the following events:</p>
          <p>(1) the filing of a risk-based capital report by the insurer that indicates that the insurer's total adjusted capital is greater than or equal to its authorized control level risk-based capital but less than its regulatory action level risk-based capital;</p>
          <p>(2) the notification by the commissioner to an insurer of an adjusted risk-based capital report that indicates the event in clause (1), provided the insurer does not challenge the adjusted risk-based capital report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>, the insurer challenges an adjusted risk-based capital report that indicates the event in clause (1), the notification by the commissioner to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the insurer's challenge;</p>
          <p>(4) the failure of the insurer to file a risk-based capital report by March 1, unless the insurer has provided an explanation for the failure that is satisfactory to the commissioner and has cured the failure within ten days after March 1;</p>
          <p>(5) the failure of the insurer to submit a risk-based capital plan to the commissioner within the time period set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.62#stat.60A.62.3">60A.62, subdivision 3</a>;</p>
          <p>(6) notification by the commissioner to the insurer that:</p>
          <p>(i) the risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan submitted by the insurer is, in the judgment of the commissioner, unsatisfactory; and</p>
          <p>(ii) the notification constitutes a regulatory action level event with respect to the insurer, provided the insurer has not challenged the determination under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>;</p>
          <p>(7) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>, the insurer challenges a determination by the commissioner under clause (6), the notification by the commissioner to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the challenge;</p>
          <p>(8) notification by the commissioner to the insurer that the insurer has failed to adhere to its risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan, but only if the failure has a substantial adverse effect on the ability of the insurer to eliminate the company action level event according to its risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan and the commissioner has so stated in the notification, provided the insurer has not challenged the determination under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>; or</p>
          <p>(9) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>, the insurer challenges a determination by the commissioner under clause (8), the notification by the commissioner to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.63.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's duties.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a regulatory action level event, the commissioner shall:</p>
          <p>(1) require the insurer to prepare and submit a risk-based capital plan, or, if applicable, a revised risk-based capital plan;</p>
          <p>(2) examine or analyze as the commissioner considers necessary the assets, liabilities, and operations of the insurer including reviewing its risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan; and</p>
          <p>(3) subsequent to the examination or analysis, issue a corrective order specifying the corrective actions the commissioner determines are required.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.63.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Corrective action.</span></h2>
          <p>In determining corrective actions, the commissioner may take into account factors considered relevant with respect to the insurer based upon the commissioner's examination or analysis of the assets, liabilities and operations of the insurer, including, but not limited to, the results of any sensitivity tests undertaken pursuant to the risk-based capital instructions. The risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan must be submitted:</p>
          <p>(1) within 45 days after the occurrence of the regulatory action level event;</p>
          <p>(2) if the insurer challenges an adjusted risk-based capital report pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a> and the challenge is not frivolous in the judgment of the commissioner, within 45 days after the notification to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the insurer's challenge; or</p>
          <p>(3) if the insurer challenges a revised risk-based capital plan pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a> and the challenge is not frivolous in the judgment of the commissioner, within 45 days after the notification to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the insurer's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.63.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Examination and review.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may retain actuaries and investment experts and other consultants as may be necessary in the judgment of the commissioner to review the insurer's risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan, examine or analyze the assets, liabilities, and operations of the insurer and formulate the corrective order with respect to the insurer. The fees, costs, and expenses relating to consultants shall be borne by the affected insurer or other party as directed by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.63.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.5.0">1995 c 253 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.64">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.64 AUTHORIZED CONTROL LEVEL EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.64.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Authorized control level event" means any of the following events:</p>
          <p>(1) the filing of a risk-based capital report by the insurer that indicates that the insurer's total adjusted capital is greater than or equal to its mandatory control level risk-based capital but less than its authorized control level risk-based capital;</p>
          <p>(2) the notification by the commissioner to the insurer of an adjusted risk-based capital report that indicates the event in clause (1), provided the insurer does not challenge the adjusted risk-based capital report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>, the insurer challenges an adjusted risk-based capital report that indicates the event in clause (1), notification by the commissioner to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the insurer's challenge;</p>
          <p>(4) the failure of the insurer to respond, in a manner satisfactory to the commissioner, to a corrective order, provided the insurer has not challenged the corrective order under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>; or</p>
          <p>(5) if the insurer has challenged a corrective order under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a> and the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the challenge or modified the corrective order, the failure of the insurer to respond, in a manner satisfactory to the commissioner, to the corrective order subsequent to rejection or modification by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.64.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's duties.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of an authorized control level event with respect to an insurer, the commissioner shall:</p>
          <p>(1) take the actions required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.63">60A.63</a> regarding an insurer with respect to which a regulatory action level event has occurred; or</p>
          <p>(2) if the commissioner considers it to be in the best interests of the policyholders and creditors of the insurer and of the public, take the actions necessary to cause the insurer to be placed under regulatory control under chapter 60B. In the event the commissioner takes these actions, the authorized control level event is considered sufficient grounds for the commissioner to take action under chapter 60B, and the commissioner has the rights, powers, and duties with respect to the insurer set forth in chapter 60B. In the event the commissioner takes actions under this clause pursuant to an adjusted risk-based capital report, the insurer is entitled to the protections afforded to insurers under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.11">60B.11</a> pertaining to summary proceedings.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.64.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.6.0">1995 c 253 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.65">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.65 MANDATORY CONTROL LEVEL EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.65.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Mandatory control level event" means any of the following events:</p>
          <p>(1) the filing of a risk-based capital report that indicates that the insurer's total adjusted capital is less than its mandatory control level risk-based capital;</p>
          <p>(2) notification by the commissioner to the insurer of an adjusted risk-based capital report that indicates the event in clause (1), provided the insurer does not challenge the adjusted risk-based capital report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>; or</p>
          <p>(3) if, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.66">60A.66</a>, the insurer challenges an adjusted risk-based capital report that indicates the event in clause (1), notification by the commissioner to the insurer that the commissioner has, after a hearing, rejected the insurer's challenge.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.65.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's duties.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a mandatory control level event:</p>
          <p>(1) with respect to a life and/or health insurer, the commissioner shall take the actions necessary to place the insurer under regulatory control under chapter 60B. In that event, the mandatory control level event is considered sufficient grounds for the commissioner to take action under chapter 60B, and the commissioner has the rights, powers, and duties with respect to the insurer set forth in chapter 60B. If the commissioner takes actions pursuant to an adjusted risk-based capital report, the insurer is entitled to the protections of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.11">60B.11</a> pertaining to summary proceedings. However, the commissioner may forgo action for up to 90 days after the mandatory control level event if the commissioner finds there is a reasonable expectation that the mandatory control level event may be eliminated within the 90-day period; and</p>
          <p>(2) with respect to a property and casualty insurer, the commissioner shall take the actions necessary to place the insurer under regulatory control under chapter 60B, or, in the case of an insurer that is writing no business and that is running off its existing business, may allow the insurer to continue its run-off under the supervision of the commissioner. In either event, the mandatory control level event is sufficient grounds for the commissioner to take action under chapter 60B, and the commissioner has the rights, powers, and duties with respect to the insurer set forth in chapter 60B. If the commissioner takes actions pursuant to an adjusted risk-based capital report, the insurer is entitled to the protections of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60B.11">60B.11</a> pertaining to summary proceedings. However, the commissioner may forgo action for up to 90 days after the mandatory control level event if the commissioner finds there is a reasonable expectation that the mandatory control level event may be eliminated within the 90-day period.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.65.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.7.0">1995 c 253 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.66">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.66 HEARINGS.</h1>
        <p>Upon:</p>
        <p>(1) notification to an insurer by the commissioner of an adjusted risk-based report;</p>
        <p>(2) notification to an insurer by the commissioner that:</p>
        <p>(i) the insurer's risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan is unsatisfactory; and</p>
        <p>(ii) the notification constitutes a regulatory action level event with respect to the insurer;</p>
        <p>(3) notification to an insurer by the commissioner that the insurer has failed to adhere to its risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan and that the failure has substantial adverse effect on the ability of the insurer to eliminate the company action level event with respect to the insurer according to its risk-based capital plan or revised risk-based capital plan; or</p>
        <p>(4) notification to an insurer by the commissioner of a corrective order with respect to the insurer,</p>
        <p class="bl">the insurer has the right to a confidential hearing conducted in accordance with chapter 14, on a record, at which the insurer may challenge any determination or action by the commissioner. The insurer shall notify the commissioner of its request for a hearing within five days after the notification by the commissioner under clause (1), (2), (3), or (4). Upon receipt of the insurer's request for a hearing, the commissioner shall set a date for the hearing no less than ten nor more than 30 days after the date of the insurer's request.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.66.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.8.0">1995 c 253 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.67">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.67 CONFIDENTIALITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.67.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Generally.</span></h2>
          <p>All risk-based capital reports, to the extent the information in them is not required to be set forth in a publicly available annual statement schedule, and risk-based capital plans, including the results or report of an examination or analysis of an insurer performed pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a>, and any corrective order issued by the commissioner pursuant to an examination or analysis, with respect to a domestic insurer or foreign insurer that are filed with the commissioner constitute information that might be damaging to the insurer if made available to its competitors, and shall be maintained by the commissioner as nonpublic data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.9">13.02, subdivision 9</a>. This information is not subject to subpoena, other than by the commissioner and then only for the purpose of enforcement actions taken by the commissioner pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a> or other provision of the insurance laws of this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.67.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prohibition on announcements.</span></h2>
          <p>The comparison of an insurer's total adjusted capital to any of its risk-based capital levels is a regulatory tool that may indicate the need for possible corrective action with respect to the insurer and is not intended as a means to rank insurers generally. Except as otherwise required under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a>, the making, publishing, dissemination, circulating, or placing before the public, or causing, directly or indirectly to be made, published, disseminated, circulated, or placed before the public, in a newspaper, magazine, or other publication, or in the form of a notice, circular, pamphlet, letter, or poster, or over any radio or television station, or in any other way, an advertisement, announcement, or statement containing an assertion, representation, or statement with regard to the risk-based capital levels of an insurer, or of any component derived in the calculation, by an insurer, agent, broker, or other person engaged in any manner in the insurance business would be misleading and is prohibited. However, if a materially false statement with respect to the comparison regarding an insurer's total adjusted capital to its risk-based capital levels, or any of them, or an inappropriate comparison of any other amount to the insurer's risk-based capital levels is published in a written publication and the insurer is able to demonstrate to the commissioner with substantial proof the falsity of the statement, or the inappropriateness, as the case may be, then the insurer may publish an announcement in a written publication if the sole purpose of the announcement is to rebut the materially false statement. This subdivision does not prohibit an insurance company or its holding company from disclosing information about its risk-based capital levels in the notes to its financial statements if required by pronouncements of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants or the Financial Accounting Standards Board, or making this disclosure as required by other governmental regulatory agencies.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.67.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Prohibition on use in ratemaking.</span></h2>
          <p>The risk-based capital instructions, risk-based capital reports, adjusted risk-based capital reports, risk-based capital plans, and revised risk-based capital plans are intended solely for use by the commissioner in monitoring the solvency of insurers and the need for possible corrective action with respect to insurers. This information shall not be used by the commissioner for ratemaking nor considered or introduced as evidence in a rate proceeding nor used by the commissioner to calculate or derive any elements of an appropriate premium level or rate of return for a line of insurance that an insurer or an affiliate is authorized to write.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.67.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.9.0">1995 c 253 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/446/#laws.2.6.0">1996 c 446 art 2 s 6</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.68">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.68 SUPPLEMENTAL PROVISIONS; RULES; EXEMPTION.</h1>
        <p>(a) Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a> are supplemental to other laws of this state and do not preclude or limit other powers or duties of the commissioner under those laws, including, but not limited to, chapters 60B and 60G.</p>
        <p>(b) The commissioner may exempt from the application of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a> a domestic property and casualty insurer that:</p>
        <p>(1) writes direct business only in this state;</p>
        <p>(2) writes direct annual premiums of $2,000,000 or less; and</p>
        <p>(3) assumes no reinsurance in excess of five percent of direct premium written.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.68.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.10.0">1995 c 253 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.69">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.69 FOREIGN INSURERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.69.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reporting requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>A foreign insurer shall, upon the written request of the commissioner, submit to the commissioner a risk-based capital report as of the end of the calendar year just ended not later than the later of:</p>
          <p>(1) the date a risk-based capital report would be required to be filed by a domestic insurer under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) fifteen days after the request is received by the foreign insurer.</p>
          <p>A foreign insurer shall, at the written request of the commissioner, promptly submit to the commissioner copies of all risk-based capital plans that are filed by the insurer with the insurance commissioners of other states.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.69.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">A risk-based capital plan requirement.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a company action level event, regulatory action level event, or authorized control level event with respect to a foreign insurer as determined under the risk-based capital statute applicable in the state of domicile of the insurer, or, if no risk-based capital statute is in force in that state, under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a>, if the insurance commissioner of the state of domicile of the foreign insurer fails to require the foreign insurer to file a risk-based capital plan in the manner specified under that state's risk-based capital statute, or, if no risk-based capital statute is in force in that state, under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.62">60A.62</a>, the commissioner may require the foreign insurer to file a risk-based capital plan with the commissioner. In this event, the failure of the foreign insurer to file a risk-based capital plan with the commissioner shall be grounds to order the insurer to cease and desist from writing new insurance business in this state. This section does not limit the commissioner's authority to require a foreign insurer to file a copy of the risk-based capital plan submitted to the commissioner in the state of domicile.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.69.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Liquidation of property.</span></h2>
          <p>In the event of a mandatory control level event with respect to a foreign insurer, if no domiciliary receiver has been appointed with respect to the foreign insurer under the rehabilitation and liquidation statute applicable in the state of domicile of the foreign insurer, the commissioner may make application to the district court permitted under chapter 60B with respect to the liquidation of property of foreign insurers found in this state, and the occurrence of the mandatory control level event is adequate grounds for the application.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.69.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.11.0">1995 c 253 s 11</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.695">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.695 IMMUNITY.</h1>
        <p>There is no liability on the part of, and no cause of action arises against, the commissioner or the commerce department or its employees or agents for an action taken by them in the performance of their powers and duties under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.695.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.12.0">1995 c 253 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.696">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.696 NOTICES.</h1>
        <p>All notices by the commissioner to an insurer that may result in regulatory action under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.60">60A.60</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.696">60A.696</a> are effective upon dispatch if transmitted by registered or certified mail, or in the case of other transmission is effective upon the insurer's receipt of the notice.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.696.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/253/#laws.0.13.0">1995 c 253 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">REINSURANCE INTERMEDIARY ACT</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.70">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.70 TITLE.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a> may be cited as the "Reinsurance Intermediary Act."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.70.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.1.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.705">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.705 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Terms.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Actuary.</span></h2>
          <p>"Actuary" means a person who is a member in good standing of the American Academy of Actuaries.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Controlling person.</span></h2>
          <p>"Controlling person" means a person, firm, association, or corporation who directly or indirectly has the power to direct or cause to be directed, the management, control, or activities of the reinsurance intermediary.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Insurer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Insurer" means any person, firm, association, or corporation duly licensed in this state pursuant to the applicable provisions of the insurance law as an insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Licensed producer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensed producer" means an agent, broker, or reinsurance intermediary licensed pursuant to the applicable provision of the insurance law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Reinsurance intermediary.</span></h2>
          <p>"Reinsurance intermediary" means a reinsurance intermediary-broker or a reinsurance intermediary-manager.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Reinsurance intermediary-broker; RB.</span></h2>
          <p>"Reinsurance intermediary-broker" or "RB" means any person, other than an officer or employee of the ceding insurer, firm, association, or corporation who solicits, negotiates, or places reinsurance cessions or retrocessions on behalf of a ceding insurer without the authority or power to bind reinsurance on behalf of this insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Reinsurance intermediary-manager; RM.</span></h2>
          <p>"Reinsurance intermediary-manager" or "RM" means any person, firm, association, or corporation who has authority to bind or manages all or part of the assumed reinsurance business of a reinsurer, including the management of a separate division, department, or underwriting office, and acts as an agent for that reinsurer whether known as an RM, manager, or other similar term. However, the following persons are not considered an RM, with respect to that reinsurer, for the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a>:</p>
          <p>(1) an employee of the reinsurer;</p>
          <p>(2) a United States manager of the United States branch of an alien reinsurer;</p>
          <p>(3) an underwriting manager which, pursuant to contract, manages all or part of the reinsurance operations of the reinsurer, is under common control with the reinsurer, subject to the Holding Company Act, and whose compensation is not based on the volume of premiums written; or</p>
          <p>(4) the manager of a group, association, pool, or organization of insurers which engage in joint underwriting or joint reinsurance and who are subject to examination by the insurance commissioner of the state in which the manager's principal business office is located.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Reinsurer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Reinsurer" means a person, firm, association, or corporation licensed in this state as an insurer with the authority to assume reinsurance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">To be in violation.</span></h2>
          <p>"To be in violation" means that the reinsurance intermediary, insurer, or reinsurer for whom the reinsurance intermediary was acting failed to substantially comply with the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.705.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Qualified United States financial institution.</span></h2>
          <p>"Qualified United States financial institution" means an institution that:</p>
          <p>(1) is organized, or in the case of a United States office of a foreign banking organization, is licensed, under the laws of the United States or any state;</p>
          <p>(2) is regulated, supervised, and examined by United States federal or state authorities having regulatory authority over banks and trust companies; and</p>
          <p>(3) has been determined by either the commissioner, or the securities valuation office of the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, to meet the standards of financial condition and standing considered necessary and appropriate to regulate the quality of financial institutions whose letters of credit will be acceptable to the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.705.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.2.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/214/#laws.0.10.0">1995 c 214 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.71">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.71 LICENSURE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.71.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reinsurance intermediary-broker requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>No person, firm, association, or corporation shall act as an RB in this state if the RB maintains an office either directly or as a member or employee of a firm or association, or an officer, director, or employee of a corporation:</p>
          <p>(1) in this state, unless the RB is a licensed producer in this state; or</p>
          <p>(2) in another state, unless the RB is a licensed producer in this state or another state having a law substantially similar to this law or the RB is licensed in this state as a nonresident reinsurance intermediary.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.71.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Reinsurance intermediary-manager requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>No person, firm, association, or corporation shall act as an RM:</p>
          <p>(1) for a reinsurer domiciled in this state, unless the RM is a licensed producer in this state;</p>
          <p>(2) in this state, if the RM maintains an office either directly or as a member or employee of a firm or association, or an officer, director, or employee of a corporation in this state, unless the RM is a licensed producer in this state; or</p>
          <p>(3) in another state for a nondomestic insurer, unless the RM is a licensed producer in this state or another state having a law substantially similar to this law or the person is licensed in this state as a nonresident reinsurance intermediary.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.71.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Bond and insurance requirements for reinsurance intermediary-manager.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may require an RM subject to subdivision 2 to:</p>
          <p>(1) file a bond in an amount from an insurer acceptable to the commissioner for the protection of the reinsurer; and</p>
          <p>(2) maintain an errors and omissions policy in an amount acceptable to the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.71.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Terms.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner may issue a reinsurance intermediary license to any person, firm, association, or corporation who has complied with the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a>. The license issued to a firm or association will authorize all the members of the firm or association and any designated employees to act as reinsurance intermediaries under the license, and these persons shall be named in the application and any supplements to it. The license issued to a corporation shall authorize all of the officers, and any designated employees and directors of the corporation to act as reinsurance intermediaries on behalf of the corporation, and all these persons shall be named in the application and any supplements to it.</p>
          <p>(b) If the applicant for a reinsurance intermediary license is a nonresident, the applicant, as a condition precedent to receiving or holding a license, shall designate the commissioner as agent for service of process in the manner, and with the same legal effect, provided for by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a> for designation of service of process upon unauthorized insurers. The applicant shall also furnish the commissioner with the name and address of a resident of this state upon whom notices or orders of the commissioner or process affecting the nonresident reinsurance intermediary may be served. The licensee shall promptly notify the commissioner in writing of every change in its designated agent for service of process, and the change shall not become effective until acknowledged by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.71.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Refusal to issue.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may refuse to issue a reinsurance intermediary license if, in the commissioner's judgment, the applicant, anyone named on the application, or any member, principal, officer, or director of the applicant, is not trustworthy, or that any controlling person of the applicant is not trustworthy to act as a reinsurance intermediary, or that any of the foregoing has given cause for revocation or suspension of the license, or has failed to comply with any prerequisite for the issuance of the license. Upon written request, the commissioner will furnish a summary of the basis for refusal to issue a license. This document is privileged and not subject to chapter 13.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.71.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Attorneys exemption.</span></h2>
          <p>Licensed attorneys at law of this state when acting in their professional capacity as such are exempt from this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.71.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Duration; fees.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Each applicant for a reinsurance intermediary license shall pay to the commissioner a fee of $200 for an initial two-year license and a fee of $150 for each renewal. Applications shall be submitted on forms prescribed by the commissioner.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Initial licenses issued under this chapter are valid for a period not to exceed 24 months and expire on October 31 of the renewal year assigned by the commissioner. Each renewal reinsurance intermediary license is valid for a period of 24 months.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) All fees are nonreturnable, except that an overpayment of any fee may be refunded upon proper application.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.71.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.3.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/200/#laws.1.42.0">1997 c 200 art 1 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/223/#laws.2.6.0">1999 c 223 art 2 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/344/#laws.0.6.0">2008 c 344 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.4.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.715">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.715 REQUIRED CONTRACT PROVISIONS; REINSURANCE INTERMEDIARY-BROKERS.</h1>
        <p>Transactions between an RB and the insurer it represents in this capacity shall only be entered into pursuant to a written authorization, specifying the responsibilities of each party. The authorization must, at a minimum, provide that:</p>
        <p>(1) the insurer may terminate the RB's authority at any time;</p>
        <p>(2) the RB will render accounts to the insurer accurately detailing all material transactions, including information necessary to support all commissions, charges, and other fees received by, or owing to the RB, and remit all funds due to the ceding insurer or the assuming reinsurer within 30 days of the month of receipt;</p>
        <p>(3) all funds collected for the ceding insurer's or the assuming reinsurer's account will be held by the RB in a fiduciary capacity:</p>
        <p>(i) in a bank that is a qualified United States financial institution; or</p>
        <p>(ii) in direct obligations of, or obligations guaranteed or insured by, the United States, its agencies, or its instrumentalities, excluding mortgage-backed securities, or in obligations described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.11#stat.60A.11.17">60A.11, subdivision 17</a>, paragraphs (a) and (b).</p>
        <p>Investments made under item (ii) must be traded on a national securities exchange, and shall be restricted to the following: direct obligations of the United States government or an agency of the United States government, municipal bonds or corporate bonds or notes with credit ratings of at least AA by Standard &amp; Poors or equivalent ratings from a comparable rating service, or commercial paper with a short-term rating of at least A-1 by Standard &amp; Poors or an equivalent rating from a comparable rating service, but in no event shall the obligations be rated other than in the highest category established by the Securities Valuation Office of the National Association of Insurance Commissioners. The RB shall invest fiduciary funds under item (ii) only if authorized in writing by the ceding insurer or assuming reinsurer in whose account the funds are held, shall secure the investments with security acceptable to the ceding insurer or assuming reinsurer on whose account the funds are held, and shall be responsible for any losses on investments made pursuant to item (ii).</p>
        <p>At least 50 percent of the funds invested under clause (3), based on the prior 30 days' average balance, must be invested in instruments that mature in no more than 120 days. In no case shall an investment mature in greater than three years from the date of purchase. Investments made pursuant to clause (3) should emphasize safety, liquidity, and diversification. The RB is required to structure those investments so that funds are available to remit on a timely basis to the ceding insurer or the assuming reinsurer in accordance with clause (2);</p>
        <p>(4) the RB will comply with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.72">60A.72</a>;</p>
        <p>(5) the RB will comply with the written standards established by the insurer for the cession or retrocession of all risks; and</p>
        <p>(6) the RB will disclose to the insurer any relationship with any reinsurer to which business will be ceded or retroceded.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.715.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.4.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/163/#laws.0.1.0">1995 c 163 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/323/#laws.0.1.0">1998 c 323 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.72">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.72 BOOKS AND RECORDS; REINSURANCE INTERMEDIARY-BROKERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.72.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Records of transactions.</span></h2>
          <p>For at least ten years after expiration of each contract of reinsurance transacted by the RB, the RB will keep a complete record for each transaction showing:</p>
          <p>(1) the type of contract, limits, underwriting restrictions, classes or risks, and territory;</p>
          <p>(2) period of coverage, including effective and expiration dates, cancellation provisions, and notice required of cancellation;</p>
          <p>(3) reporting and settlement requirements of balances;</p>
          <p>(4) rate used to compute the reinsurance premium;</p>
          <p>(5) names and addresses of assuming reinsurers;</p>
          <p>(6) rates of all reinsurance commissioners, including the commissions on any retrocessions handled by the RB;</p>
          <p>(7) related correspondence and memoranda;</p>
          <p>(8) proof of placement;</p>
          <p>(9) details regarding retrocessions handled by the RB including the identity of retrocessionaires and percentage of each contract assumed or ceded;</p>
          <p>(10) financial records, including, but not limited to, premium and loss accounts; and</p>
          <p>(11) when the RB procures a reinsurance contract on behalf of a licensed ceding insurer:</p>
          <p>(i) directly from any assuming reinsurer, written evidence that the assuming reinsurer has agreed to assume the risk; or</p>
          <p>(ii) if placed through a representative of the assuming reinsurer, other than an employee, written evidence that such reinsurer has delegated binding authority to the representative.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.72.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Access by insurer.</span></h2>
          <p>The insurer will have access and the right to copy and audit all accounts and records maintained by the RB related to its business in a form usable by the insurer.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.72.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.5.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.725">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.725 DUTIES OF INSURERS UTILIZING THE SERVICES OF A REINSURANCE INTERMEDIARY-BROKER.</h1>
        <p>(a) An insurer shall not engage the services of a person, firm, association, or corporation to act as an RB on its behalf unless the person is licensed as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.71#stat.60A.71.1">60A.71, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        <p>(b) An insurer may not employ an individual who is employed by an RB with which it transacts business, unless the RB is under common control with the insurer and subject to chapter 60D.</p>
        <p>(c) The insurer shall annually obtain a copy of statements of the financial condition of each RB with which it transacts business.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.725.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.6.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.73">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.73 REQUIRED CONTRACT PROVISIONS; REINSURANCE INTERMEDIARY-MANAGERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Approval by commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>Transactions between an RM and the reinsurer it represents in this capacity must only be entered into pursuant to a written contract, specifying the responsibilities of each party. The contract shall be approved by the reinsurer's board of directors. At least 30 days before the reinsurer assumes or cedes business through this producer, a true copy of the approved contract must be filed with the commissioner for approval. The contract must, at a minimum, contain the provisions in subdivisions 2 to 14.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Terminations.</span></h2>
          <p>The reinsurer may terminate the contract for cause upon written notice to the RM. The reinsurer may immediately suspend the authority of the RM to assume or cede business during the pendency of any dispute regarding the cause for termination.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Periodic accounting.</span></h2>
          <p>The RM will render accounts to the reinsurer accurately detailing all material transactions, including information necessary to support all commissions, charges, and other fees received by, or owing to the RM, and remit all funds due under the contract to the reinsurer on not less than a monthly basis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Handling of funds.</span></h2>
          <p>All funds collected for the reinsurer's account will be held by the RM in a fiduciary capacity in a bank which is a qualified United States financial institution as defined herein and may be invested in direct obligations of, or obligations guaranteed or insured by, the United States, its agencies, or its instrumentalities, excluding mortgage-backed securities. These funds may not be invested in obligations whose maturities exceed 90 days. The RM may retain no more than three months estimated claims payments and allocated loss adjustment expenses. The RM shall maintain a separate account for each reinsurer that it represents.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Business records.</span></h2>
          <p>For at least ten years after expiration of each contract of reinsurance transacted by the RM, the RM will keep a complete record for each transaction showing:</p>
          <p>(1) the type of contract, limits, underwriting restrictions, classes or risks, and territory;</p>
          <p>(2) period of coverage, including effective and expiration dates, cancellation provisions and notice required of cancellation, and disposition of outstanding reserves on covered risks;</p>
          <p>(3) reporting and settlement requirements of balances;</p>
          <p>(4) rate used to compute the reinsurance premium;</p>
          <p>(5) names and addresses of reinsurers;</p>
          <p>(6) rates of all reinsurance commissions, including the commissions on any retrocessions handled by the RM;</p>
          <p>(7) related correspondence and memoranda;</p>
          <p>(8) proof of placement;</p>
          <p>(9) details regarding retrocessions handled by the RM, as permitted by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.74#stat.60A.74.4">60A.74, subdivision 4</a>, including the identity of retrocessionaires and percentage of each contract assumed or ceded;</p>
          <p>(10) financial records, including, but not limited to, premium and loss accounts; and</p>
          <p>(11) when the RM places a reinsurance contract on behalf of a ceding insurer:</p>
          <p>(i) directly from any assuming reinsurer, written evidence that the assuming reinsurer has agreed to assume the risk; or</p>
          <p>(ii) if placed through a representative of the assuming reinsurer, other than an employee, written evidence that the reinsurer has delegated binding authority to the representative.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Reinsurer access to records.</span></h2>
          <p>The reinsurer will have access and the right to copy all accounts and records maintained by the RM related to its business in a form usable by the reinsurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Nonassignment of contract.</span></h2>
          <p>The contract cannot be assigned in whole or in part by the RM.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Underwriting and rating standards.</span></h2>
          <p>The RM will comply with the written underwriting and rating standards established by the insurer for the acceptance, rejection, or cession of all risks.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Charges and commissions.</span></h2>
          <p>The rates, terms and purposes of commission, charges, and other fees which the RM may levy against the reinsurer will be specified in the contract.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Claims settlement.</span></h2>
          <p>If the contract permits the RM to settle claims on behalf of the reinsurer, the contract will specify that:</p>
          <p>(1) all claims will be reported to the reinsurer in a timely manner;</p>
          <p>(2) a copy of the claim file will be sent to the reinsurer at its request or as soon as it becomes known that the claim:</p>
          <p>(i) has the potential to exceed the lesser of an amount determined by the commissioner or the limit set by the reinsurer;</p>
          <p>(ii) involves a coverage dispute;</p>
          <p>(iii) may exceed the RM's claims settlement authority;</p>
          <p>(iv) is open for more than six months; or</p>
          <p>(v) is closed by payment of the lesser of an amount set by the commissioner or an amount set by the reinsurer;</p>
          <p>(3) all claim files will be the joint property of the reinsurer and RM. However, upon an order of liquidation of the reinsurer the files become the sole property of the reinsurer or its estate. The RM shall have reasonable access to and the right to copy the files on a timely basis; and</p>
          <p>(4) settlement authority granted to the RM may be terminated for cause upon the reinsurer's written notice to the RM or upon the termination of the contract. The reinsurer may suspend the settlement authority during the pendency of the dispute regarding the cause of termination.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Interim profits.</span></h2>
          <p>If the contract provides for a sharing of interim profits by the RM, interim profits will not be paid until one year after the end of each underwriting period for property business and five years after the end of each underwriting period for casualty business, or a later period set by the commissioner for specified lines of insurance, and not until the adequacy of reserves on remaining claims has been verified pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.74#stat.60A.74.3">60A.74, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Certified financial statement.</span></h2>
          <p>The RM will annually provide the reinsurer with a statement of its financial condition prepared by an independent certified accountant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">On-site review by reinsurer.</span></h2>
          <p>The reinsurer shall periodically, at least semiannually, conduct an on-site review of the underwriting and claims processing operations of the RM.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Disclosure of insurer relationship.</span></h2>
          <p>The RM will disclose to the reinsurer any relationship it has with any insurer before ceding or assuming any business with the insurer pursuant to this contract.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.73.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Responsibility of reinsurer.</span></h2>
          <p>Within the scope of its actual or apparent authority, the acts of the RM are considered to be the acts of the reinsurer on whose behalf it is acting.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.73.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.7.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/163/#laws.0.2.0">1995 c 163 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.735">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.735 PROHIBITED ACTS.</h1>
