        <p>The RM shall not:</p>
        <p>(1) cede retrocessions on behalf of the reinsurer, except that the RM may cede facultative retrocessions pursuant to obligatory facultative agreements if the contract with the reinsurer contains reinsurance underwriting guidelines for these retrocessions. These guidelines must include a list of reinsurers with which these automatic agreements are in effect, and for each reinsurer, the coverages and amounts or percentages that may be reinsured, and commission schedules;</p>
        <p>(2) commit the reinsurer to participate in reinsurance syndicates;</p>
        <p>(3) appoint any producer without assuring that the producer is lawfully licensed to transact the type of reinsurance for which the producer is appointed;</p>
        <p>(4) without prior approval of the reinsurer, pay or commit the reinsurer to pay a claim, net of retrocessions, that exceeds the lesser of an amount specified by the reinsurer or one percent of the reinsurer's policyholder's surplus as of December 31 of the last complete calendar year;</p>
        <p>(5) collect any payment from a retrocessionaire or commit the reinsurer to any claim settlement with a retrocessionaire, without prior approval of the reinsurer. If prior approval is given, a report must be promptly forwarded to the reinsurer;</p>
        <p>(6) jointly employ an individual who is employed by the reinsurer unless such RM is under common control with the reinsurer subject to chapter 60D;</p>
        <p>(7) appoint a sub-RM.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.735.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.8.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.74">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.74 DUTIES OF REINSURER UTILIZING THE SERVICES OF A REINSURANCE INTERMEDIARY-MANAGER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.74.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Licensed persons to be used.</span></h2>
          <p>A reinsurer shall not engage the services of any person, firm, association, or corporation to act as an RM on its behalf unless the person is licensed as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.71#stat.60A.71.2">60A.71, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.74.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Annual financial statements to be obtained.</span></h2>
          <p>The reinsurer shall annually obtain a copy of statements of the financial condition of each RM which the reinsurer has engaged prepared by an independent certified accountant in a form acceptable to the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.74.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Loss reserve opinions.</span></h2>
          <p>If an RM establishes loss reserves, the reinsurer shall annually obtain the opinion of an actuary attesting to the adequacy of loss reserves established for losses incurred and outstanding on business produced by the RM. This opinion must be in addition to any other required loss reserve certification.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.74.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Binding authority.</span></h2>
          <p>Binding authority for all retrocessional contracts or participation in reinsurance syndicates shall rest with an officer of the reinsurer who shall not be affiliated with the RM.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.74.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Notification of termination.</span></h2>
          <p>Within 30 days of termination of a contract with an RM, the reinsurer shall provide written notification of the termination to the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.74.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Restriction on board appointments.</span></h2>
          <p>A reinsurer shall not appoint to its board of directors, any officer, director, employee, controlling shareholder, or subproducer of its RM. This subdivision does not apply to relationships governed by chapter 60D or, if applicable, the Business Transacted With Producer Controlled Insurer Act, sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60J.06">60J.06</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60J.11">60J.11</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.74.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.9.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/13/#laws.1.16.0">1993 c 13 art 1 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/260/#laws.0.12.0">2000 c 260 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.745">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.745 EXAMINATION AUTHORITY; REINSURANCE INTERMEDIARY - BROKER.</h1>
        <p>(a) A reinsurance intermediary is subject to examination by the commissioner. The commissioner shall have access to all books, bank accounts, and records of the reinsurance intermediary in a form usable to the commissioner.</p>
        <p>(b) An RM may be examined as if it were the reinsurer.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.745.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.10.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.75">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.75 VIOLATIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.75.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Administrative and civil penalties and liabilities.</span></h2>
          <p>A reinsurance intermediary, insurer, or reinsurer found by the commissioner, after a hearing conducted in accordance with chapter 14, to be in violation of any provision of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a>, shall:</p>
          <p>(1) for each separate violation, pay a penalty in an amount not exceeding $5,000; and</p>
          <p>(2) be subject to revocation or suspension of its license.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.75.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Civil remedies.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If it was found that because of the violation the insurer or reinsurer has suffered loss or damage, the commissioner may maintain a civil action for recovery of compensatory damages for the benefit of the reinsurer or insurer and its policyholders and creditors or seek other appropriate relief.</p>
          <p>(b) If an order of rehabilitation or liquidation of the insurer has been entered pursuant to chapter 60B, and the receiver appointed under that order determines that the reinsurance intermediary or any other person has violated sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a>, or any rule or order adopted under those sections, and the insurer suffered any loss or damage, the receiver may maintain a civil action for recovery of damages or other appropriate sanctions for the benefit of the insurer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.75.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Judicial review.</span></h2>
          <p>The decision, determination, or order of the commissioner pursuant to subdivision 1 is subject to judicial review pursuant to chapter 14.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.75.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Other penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing contained in this section affects the right of the commissioner to impose any other penalties provided in the insurance laws.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.75.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.11.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/214/#laws.0.11.0">1995 c 214 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.755">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.755 SCOPE.</h1>
        <p>Nothing contained in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a> is intended to or shall in any manner limit or restrict the rights of policyholders, claimants, creditors, or other third parties or confer any rights to these persons.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.755.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.12.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.756">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.756 RULES.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner may adopt rules for the implementation and administration of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.70">60A.70</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.756">60A.756</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.756.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.11.13.0">1991 c 325 art 11 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">MINIMUM STANDARD OF VALUATION FOR HEALTH INSURANCE</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.76">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.76 PURPOSE AND SCOPE.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.76">60A.76</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a> apply to all individual and group accident and health insurance coverages as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.06#stat.60A.06.1">60A.06, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (5)(a), including single premium credit disability insurance. Other credit insurance is not subject to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.76">60A.76</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>.</p>
        <p>When an insurer determines that adequacy of its health insurance reserves requires reserves in excess of the minimum standards specified in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.76">60A.76</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>, the increased reserves must be held and must be considered the minimum reserves for that insurer.</p>
        <p>With respect to any block of contracts, or with respect to an insurer's health business as a whole, a prospective gross premium valuation is the ultimate test of reserve adequacy as of a given valuation date. The prospective gross premium valuation must take into account, for contracts in force, in a claims status, or in a continuation of benefits status on the valuation date, the present value as of the valuation date of: all expected benefits unpaid, all expected expenses unpaid, and all unearned or expected premiums, adjusted for future premium increases reasonably expected to be put into effect.</p>
        <p>The prospective gross premium valuation must be performed whenever a significant doubt exists as to reserve adequacy with respect to any major block of contracts, or with respect to the insurer's health business as a whole. In the event inadequacy is found to exist, immediate loss recognition must be made and the reserves restored to adequacy. Adequate reserves, inclusive of claim, premium, and contract reserves, if any, must be held with respect to all contracts, regardless of whether contract reserves are required for such contracts under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.76">60A.76</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>.</p>
        <p>Whenever minimum reserves, as defined in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.76">60A.76</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>, exceed reserve requirements as determined by a prospective gross premium valuation, such minimum reserves remain the minimum requirement under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.76">60A.76</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.76.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.2.1.0">2004 c 285 art 2 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.761">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.761 GLOSSARY OF TECHNICAL TERMS USED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.76">60A.76</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>, the terms in subdivisions 2 to 21 have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Annual claim cost.</span></h2>
          <p>"Annual claim cost" means the net annual cost per unit of benefit before the addition of expenses, including claim settlement expenses, and a margin for profit or contingencies. For example, the annual claim cost for a $100 monthly disability benefit, for a maximum disability benefit period of one year, with an elimination period of one week, with respect to a male at age 35, in a certain occupation might be $12, while the gross premium for this benefit might be $18. The additional $6 would cover expenses and profit or contingencies.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Claims accrued.</span></h2>
          <p>"Claims accrued" means that portion of claims incurred on or prior to the valuation date which result in liability of the insurer for the payment of benefits for medical services which have been rendered on or before the valuation date, and for the payment of benefits for days of hospitalization and days of disability which have occurred on or prior to the valuation date, which the insurer has not paid as of the valuation date, but for which it is liable, and will have to pay after the valuation date. This liability is sometimes referred to as a liability for "accrued" benefits. A claim reserve, which represents an estimate of this accrued claim liability, must be established.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Claims reported.</span></h2>
          <p>"Claims reported" means when an insurer has been informed that a claim has been incurred, if the date reported is on or before the valuation date, the claim is considered as a reported claim for annual statement purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Claims unaccrued.</span></h2>
          <p>"Claims unaccrued" means that portion of claims incurred on or before the valuation date which result in liability of the insurer for the payment of benefits for medical services expected to be rendered after the valuation date, and for benefits expected to be payable for days of hospitalization and days of disability occurring after the valuation date. This liability is sometimes referred to as a liability for "unaccrued" benefits. A claim reserve, which represents an estimate of the unaccrued claim payments expected to be made (which may or may not be discounted with interest) must be established.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Claims unreported.</span></h2>
          <p>"Claims unreported" means when an insurer has not been informed, on or before the valuation date, concerning a claim that has been incurred on or prior to the valuation date, the claim is considered as an unreported claim for annual statement purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Date of disablement.</span></h2>
          <p>"Date of disablement" means the earliest date the insured is considered as being disabled under the definition of disability in the contract, based on a doctor's evaluation or other evidence. Normally this date will coincide with the start of any elimination period.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Elimination period.</span></h2>
          <p>"Elimination period" means a specified number of days, weeks, or months starting at the beginning of each period of loss, during which no benefits are payable.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Gross premium.</span></h2>
          <p>"Gross premium" means the amount of premium charged by the insurer. It includes the net premium (based on claim cost) for the risk, together with any loading for expenses, profit, or contingencies.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Group insurance.</span></h2>
          <p>"Group insurance" includes blanket insurance and franchise insurance and any other forms of group insurance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Level premium.</span></h2>
          <p>"Level premium" means a premium calculated to remain unchanged throughout either the lifetime of the policy, or for some shorter projected period of years. The premium need not be guaranteed; in which case, although it is calculated to remain level, it may be changed if any of the assumptions on which it was based are revised at a later time.</p>
          <p>Generally, the annual claim costs are expected to increase each year and the insurer, instead of charging premiums that correspondingly increase each year, charges a premium calculated to remain level for a period of years or for the lifetime of the contract. In this case, the benefit portion of the premium is more than needed to provide for the cost of benefits during the earlier years of the policy and less than the actual cost in the later years. The building of a prospective contract reserve is a natural result of level premiums.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Long-term care insurance.</span></h2>
          <p>"Long-term care insurance" means a qualified long-term care insurance policy or rider as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62S.01#stat.62S.01.18">62S.01, subdivision 18</a>, and a nonqualified long-term insurance policy or rider as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62A.46#stat.62A.46.2">62A.46, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Modal premium.</span></h2>
          <p>"Modal premium" refers to the premium paid on a contract based on a premium term which could be annual, semiannual, quarterly, monthly, or weekly. Thus if the annual premium is $100 and if, instead, monthly premiums of $9 are paid then the modal premium is $9.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Negative reserve.</span></h2>
          <p>"Negative reserve" means normally the terminal reserve is a positive value. However, if the values of the benefits are decreasing with advancing age or duration it could be a negative value, called a negative reserve.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Preliminary term reserve method.</span></h2>
          <p>"Preliminary term reserve method" means that under this method of valuation the valuation net premium for each year falling within the preliminary term period is exactly sufficient to cover the expected incurred claims of that year, so that the terminal reserves will be zero at the end of the year. As of the end of the preliminary term period, a new constant valuation net premium (or stream of changing valuation premiums) becomes applicable such that the present value of all such premiums is equal to the present value of all claims expected to be incurred following the end of the preliminary term period.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Present value of amounts not yet due on claims.</span></h2>
          <p>"Present value of amounts not yet due on claims" means the reserve for "claims unaccrued" which may be discounted at interest.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Rating block.</span></h2>
          <p>"Rating block" means a grouping of contracts determined by the valuation actuary based on common characteristics, such as a policy form or forms having similar benefit designs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Reserve.</span></h2>
          <p>"Reserve" includes all items of benefit liability, whether in the nature of incurred claim liability or in the nature of contract liability relating to future periods of coverage, and whether the liability is accrued or unaccrued.</p>
          <p>An insurer under its contracts promises benefits, which result in:</p>
          <p>(a) claims which have been incurred, that is, for which the insurer has become obligated to make payment, on or prior to the valuation date. On these claims, payments expected to be made after the valuation date for accrued and unaccrued benefits are liabilities of the insurer which should be provided for by establishing claim reserves; or</p>
          <p>(b) claims which are expected to be incurred after the valuation date. Any present liability of the insurer for these future claims should be provided for by the establishment of contract reserves and unearned premium reserves.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.19">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">Terminal reserve.</span></h2>
          <p>"Terminal reserve" means the reserve at the end of a contract year, and is defined as the present value of benefits expected to be incurred after that contract year minus the present value of future valuation net premiums.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.20">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20.<span class="headnote">Unearned premium reserve.</span></h2>
          <p>"Unearned premium reserve" means that portion of the premium paid or due to the insurer which is applicable to the period of coverage extending beyond the valuation date. Thus if an annual premium of $120 was paid on November 1, $20 would be earned as of December 31 and the remaining $100 would be unearned. The unearned premium reserve could be on a gross basis as in this example, or on a valuation net premium basis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.761.21">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 21.<span class="headnote">Valuation net modal premium.</span></h2>
          <p>"Valuation net modal premium" means the modal fraction of the valuation net annual premium that corresponds to the gross modal premium in effect on any contract to which contract reserves apply. Thus if the mode of payment in effect is quarterly, the valuation net modal premium is the quarterly equivalent of the valuation net annual premium.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.761.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.2.2.0">2004 c 285 art 2 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.762">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.762 CATEGORIES OF RESERVES.</h1>
        <p>The following sections set forth minimum standards for three categories of health insurance reserves:</p>
        <p>(1) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.763">60A.763</a>, claim reserves;</p>
        <p>(2) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.764">60A.764</a>, premium reserves; and</p>
        <p>(3) section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.765">60A.765</a>, contract reserves.</p>
        <p>Adequacy of an insurer's health insurance reserves is to be determined on the basis of all three categories combined. However, sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.76">60A.76</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a> emphasize the importance of determining appropriate reserves for each of the three categories separately.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.762.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.2.3.0">2004 c 285 art 2 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.763">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.763 CLAIM RESERVES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.763.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Generally.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Claim reserves are required for all incurred but unpaid claims on all health insurance policies.</p>
          <p>(b) Appropriate claim expense reserves are required with respect to the estimated expense of settlement of all incurred but unpaid claims.</p>
          <p>(c) Claim reserves for prior valuation years are to be tested for adequacy and reasonableness along the lines of claim runoff schedules in accordance with the statutory financial statement including consideration of any residual unpaid liability.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.763.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Minimum standards for claim reserves for disability income.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The maximum interest rate for claim reserves is specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Minimum standards with respect to morbidity are those specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>, except that, at the option of the insurer:</p>
          <p>(1) for claims with a duration from date of disablement of less than two years, reserves may be based on the insurer's experience, if such experience is considered credible, or upon other assumptions designed to place a sound value on the liabilities; and</p>
          <p>(2) for group disability income claims with a duration from date of disablement of more than two years but less than five years, reserves may, with the approval of the commissioner, be based on the insurer's experience for which the insurer maintains underwriting and claim administration control. The request for approval of a plan of modification to the reserve basis must include:</p>
          <p>(i) an analysis of the credibility of the experience;</p>
          <p>(ii) a description of how all of the insurer's experience is proposed to be used in setting reserves;</p>
          <p>(iii) a description and quantification of the margins to be included;</p>
          <p>(iv) a summary of the financial impact that the proposed plan of modification would have had on the insurer's last filed annual statement;</p>
          <p>(v) a copy of the approval of the proposed plan of modification by the commissioner of the state of domicile; and</p>
          <p>(vi) any other information deemed necessary by the commissioner.</p>
          <p>(c) For contracts with an elimination period, the duration of disablement must be measured as dating from the time that benefits would have begun to accrue had there been no elimination period.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.763.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Minimum standards for claim reserves for all other benefits.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The maximum interest rate for claim reserves is specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The reserve must be based on the insurer's experience, if the experience is considered credible, or upon other assumptions designed to place a sound value on the liabilities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.763.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Claim reserve methods generally.</span></h2>
          <p>A generally accepted actuarial reserving method or other reasonable method if the method is approved by the commissioner before the statement date, or a combination of methods as described in this section, may be used to estimate all claim liabilities. The methods used for estimating liabilities generally may be aggregate methods, or various reserve items may be separately valued. Approximations based on groupings and averages may also be employed. Adequacy of the claim reserves, however, must be determined in the aggregate.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.763.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.2.4.0">2004 c 285 art 2 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.764">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.764 PREMIUM RESERVES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.764.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Generally.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Unearned premium reserves are required for all contracts with respect to the period of coverage for which premiums, other than premiums paid in advance, have been paid beyond the date of valuation.</p>
          <p>(b) If premiums due and unpaid are carried as an asset, the premiums must be treated as premiums in force, subject to unearned premium reserve determination. The value of unpaid commissions, premium taxes, and the cost of collection associated with due and unpaid premiums must be carried as an offsetting liability.</p>
          <p>(c) The gross premiums paid in advance for a period of coverage beginning after the next premium due date which follows the date of valuation may be appropriately discounted to the valuation date and must be held either as a separate liability or as an addition to the unearned premium reserve which would otherwise be required as a minimum.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.764.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Minimum standards for unearned premium reserves.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The minimum unearned premium reserve with respect to a contract is the pro rata unearned modal premium that applies to the premium period beyond the valuation date, with the premium determined on the basis of:</p>
          <p>(1) the valuation net modal premium on the contract reserve basis applying to the contract; or</p>
          <p>(2) the gross modal premium for the contract if no contract reserve applies.</p>
          <p>(b) However, in no event may the sum of the unearned premium and contract reserves for all contracts of the insurer subject to contract reserve requirements be less than the gross modal unearned premium reserve on all such contracts, as of the date of valuation. The reserve must never be less than the expected claims for the period beyond the valuation date represented by the unearned premium reserve, to the extent not provided for elsewhere.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.764.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Premium reserve methods generally.</span></h2>
          <p>The insurer may employ suitable approximations and estimates, including, but not limited to, groupings, averages, and aggregate estimation, in computing premium reserves. Approximations or estimates should be tested periodically to determine the continuing adequacy and reliability.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.764.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.2.5.0">2004 c 285 art 2 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.765">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.765 CONTRACT RESERVES REQUIRED.</h1>
        <p>(a) Contract reserves are required, unless otherwise specified in paragraph (b) for:</p>
        <p>(1) all individual and group contracts with which level premiums are used; or</p>
        <p>(2) all individual and group contracts with respect to which, due to the gross premium pricing structure at issue, the value of the future benefits at any time exceeds the value of any appropriate future valuation net premiums at that time. This evaluation may be applied on a rating block basis if the total premiums for the block were developed to support the total risk assumed and expected expenses for the block each year, and a qualified actuary certifies the premium development. The actuary must state in the certification that premiums for the rating block were developed such that each year's premium was intended to cover that year's costs without any prefunding. If the premium is also intended to recover costs for any prior years, the actuary must also disclose the reasons for and magnitude of the recovery. The values specified in this clause must be determined on the basis specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.766">60A.766</a>, subdivisions 1 to 4.</p>
        <p>(b) Contracts not requiring a contract reserve are:</p>
        <p>(1) contracts that cannot be continued after one year from issue; or</p>
        <p>(2) contracts already in force on August 1, 2004, for which no contract reserve was required under the immediately preceding standards.</p>
        <p>(c) The contract reserve is in addition to claim reserves and premium reserves.</p>
        <p>(d) The methods and procedures for contract reserves must be consistent with those for claim reserves for a contract, or else appropriate adjustment must be made when necessary to assure provision for the aggregate liability. The definition of the date of incurral must be the same in both determinations.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.765.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.2.6.0">2004 c 285 art 2 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.766">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.766 MINIMUM STANDARDS FOR CONTRACT RESERVES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.766.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Basis.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Minimum standards with respect to morbidity are those set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>. Valuation net premiums used under each contract must have a structure consistent with the gross premium structure at issue of the contract as this relates to advancing age of insured, contract duration, and period for which gross premiums have been calculated.</p>
          <p>Contracts for which tabular morbidity standards are not specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a> must be valued using tables established for reserve purposes by a qualified actuary and acceptable to the commissioner. The morbidity tables must contain a pattern of incurred claims cost that reflects the underlying morbidity and must not be constructed for the primary purpose of minimizing reserves.</p>
          <p>(b) The maximum interest rate is specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) Termination rates used in the computation of reserves must be on the basis of a mortality table as specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a> except as noted in clauses (1) to (3):</p>
          <p>(1) under contracts for which premium rates are not guaranteed, and where the effects of insurer underwriting are specifically used by policy duration in the valuation morbidity standard or for return of premium or other deferred cash benefits, total termination rates may be used at ages and durations where these exceed specified mortality table rates, but not in excess of the lesser of:</p>
          <p>(i) 80 percent of the total termination rate used in the calculation of the gross premiums; or</p>
          <p>(ii) eight percent;</p>
          <p>(2) for long-term care individual policies or group certificates issued after January 1, 1997, the contract reserve may be established on a basis of separate:</p>
          <p>(i) mortality as specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a>; and</p>
          <p>(ii) terminations other than mortality, where the terminations are not to exceed:</p>
          <p>A. for policy years one through four, the lesser of 80 percent of the voluntary lapse rate used in the calculation of gross premiums and eight percent;</p>
          <p>B. for policy years five and later, the lesser of 100 percent of the voluntary lapse rate used in the calculation of gross premiums and four percent;</p>
          <p>(3) where a morbidity standard specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a> is on an aggregate basis, the morbidity standard may be adjusted to reflect the effect of insurer underwriting by policy duration. The adjustments must be appropriate to the underwriting and be acceptable to the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.766.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Reserve method.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For insurance, except long-term care and return of premium or other deferred cash benefits, the minimum reserve is the reserve calculated on the two-year full preliminary term method; that is, under which the terminal reserve is zero at the first and also the second contract anniversary.</p>
          <p>(b) For long-term care insurance, the minimum reserve is the reserve calculated as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) for individual policies and group certificates issued on or before December 31, 1991, reserves calculated on the two-year full preliminary term methods;</p>
          <p>(2) for individual policies and group certificates issued on or after January 1, 1992, reserves calculated on the one-year full preliminary term method.</p>
          <p>(c) For return of premium or other deferred cash benefits, the minimum reserve is the reserve calculated as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) on the one-year preliminary term method if the benefits are provided at any time before the 20th anniversary;</p>
          <p>(2) on the two-year preliminary term method if the benefits are only provided on or after the 20th anniversary.</p>
          <p>The preliminary term method may be applied only in relation to the date of issue of a contract. Reserve adjustments introduced later, as a result of rate increases, revisions in assumptions, for example projected inflation rates, or for other reasons, are to be applied immediately as of the effective date of adoption of the adjusted basis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.766.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Negative reserves.</span></h2>
          <p>Negative reserves on any benefit may be offset against positive reserves for other benefits in the same contract, but the total contract reserve with respect to all benefits combined may not be less than zero.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.766.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Nonforfeiture benefits for long-term care insurance.</span></h2>
          <p>The contract reserve on a policy basis must not be less than the net single premium for the nonforfeiture benefits at the appropriate policy duration, where the net single premium is computed according to the specifications in this section. While the consideration for nonforfeiture benefits in this section is specific to long-term care insurance, similar consideration may be applicable for other lines of business.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.766.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Alternative valuation methods and assumptions generally.</span></h2>
          <p>Provided the contract reserve on all contracts to which an alternative method or basis is applied is not less in the aggregate than the amount determined according to the applicable standards specified in this section, an insurer may use any reasonable assumptions as to interest rates, termination and mortality rates, and rates of morbidity or other contingency. Also, subject to the preceding condition, the insurer may employ methods other than the methods stated in this section in determining a sound value of its liabilities under such contracts, including, but not limited to, the following: the net level premium method; the one-year full preliminary term method; prospective valuation on the basis of actual gross premiums with reasonable allowance for future expenses; the use of approximations such as those involving age groupings, groupings of several years of issue, average amounts of indemnity, and grouping of similar contract forms; the computation of the reserve for one contract benefit as a percentage of, or by other relation to, the aggregate contract reserves exclusive of the benefit or benefits so valued; and the use of a composite annual claim cost for all or any combination of the benefits included in the contracts valued.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.766.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Test for adequacy and reasonableness of contract reserves.</span></h2>
          <p>Annually, an appropriate review must be made of the insurer's prospective contract liabilities on contracts valued by tabular reserves, to determine the continuing adequacy and reasonableness of the tabular reserves giving consideration to future gross premiums. The insurer shall make appropriate increments to such tabular reserves if such tests indicate that the basis of such reserves is no longer adequate; subject, however, to the minimum standards of subdivisions 1 to 4.</p>
          <p>In the event a company has a contract or a group of related similar contracts for which future gross premiums will be restricted by contract, department rule, or for other reasons, such that the future gross premiums reduced by expenses for administration, commissions, and taxes will be insufficient to cover future claims, the company shall establish contract reserves for such shortfall in the aggregate.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.766.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.2.7.0">2004 c 285 art 2 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.767">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.767 REINSURANCE.</h1>
        <p>Increases to or credits against reserves carried, arising because of reinsurance assumed or reinsurance ceded, must be determined in a manner consistent with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.76">60A.76</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.768">60A.768</a> and with all applicable provisions of the reinsurance contracts which affect the insurer's liabilities.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.767.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/285/#laws.2.8.0">2004 c 285 art 2 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.768">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.768 SPECIFIC STANDARDS FOR MORBIDITY, INTEREST, AND MORTALITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.768.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Morbidity.</span></h2>
          <p>A. Minimum morbidity standards for valuation of specified individual contract health insurance benefits are as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) Disability Income Benefits Due to Accident or Sickness.</p>
          <p>(a) Contract Reserves:</p>
          <p>Contracts issued on or after January 1, 2004:</p>
          <p>The 1985 Commissioners Individual Disability Tables A (85CIDA); or</p>
          <p>The 1985 Commissioners Individual Disability Tables B (85CIDB).</p>
          <p>Each insurer shall elect, with respect to all individual contracts issued in any one statement year, whether it will use Tables A or Tables B as the minimum standard. The insurer may, however, elect to use the other tables with respect to any subsequent statement year.</p>
          <p>(b) Claim Reserves:</p>
          <p>For claims incurred on or after January 1, 2004:</p>

          <p>**Applicable DTS Valuation Table duration rate from exhibits 3c and 4 (TSA XXXVII, pages 462-463).</p>
          <p>The 85CIDA table so adjusted for the computation of claim reserves shall be known as 85CIDC (The 1985 Commissioners Individual Disability Table C).</p>
          <p>(2) Hospital Benefits, Surgical Benefits, and Maternity Benefits (Scheduled benefits or fixed time period benefits only).</p>
          <p>(a) Contract Reserves.</p>
          <p>Contracts issued on or after January 1, 1982:</p>
          <p>The 1974 Medical Expense Tables, Table A, Transactions of the Society of Actuaries, Volume XXX, page 63. Refer to the paper (in the same volume, page 9) to which this table is appended, including its discussions, for methods of adjustment for benefits not directly valued in Table A: "Development of the 1974 Medical Expense Benefits," Houghton and Wolf.</p>
          <p>(b) Claim Reserves:</p>
          <p>No specific standard. See (6).</p>
          <p>(3) Cancer Expense Benefits (Scheduled benefits or fixed time period benefits only).</p>
          <p>(a) Contract Reserves:</p>
          <p>Contracts issued on or after January 1, 2004:</p>
          <p>The 1985 NAIC Cancer Claim Cost Tables.</p>
          <p>(b) Claim Reserves:</p>
          <p>No specific standard. See (6).</p>
          <p>(4) Accidental Death Benefits.</p>
          <p>(a) Contract Reserves:</p>
          <p>Contracts issued on or after January 1, 2004:</p>
          <p>The 1959 Accidental Death Benefits Table.</p>
          <p>(b) Claim Reserves:</p>
          <p>Actual amount incurred.</p>
          <p>(5) Single Premium Credit Disability.</p>
          <p>(a) Contract Reserves:</p>
          <p>(i) For contracts issued on or after January 1, 2004:</p>
          <p>(I) For plans having less than a 30-day elimination period, the 1985 Commissioners Individual Disability Table A (85CIDA) with claim incidence rates increased by 12 percent.</p>
          <p>(ii)(II) For plans having a 30-day and greater elimination period, the 85CIDA for a 14-day elimination period with the adjustment in item (I).</p>
          <p>(b) Claim Reserves:</p>
          <p>Claim reserves are to be determined as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.763">60A.763</a>.</p>
          <p>(6) Other Individual Contract Benefits.</p>
          <p>(a) Contract Reserves:</p>
          <p>For all other individual contract benefits, morbidity assumptions are to be determined as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.765">60A.765</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Claim Reserves:</p>
          <p>For all benefits other than disability, claim reserves are to be determined as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.763">60A.763</a>.</p>
          <p>B. Minimum morbidity standards for valuation of specified group contract health insurance benefits are as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) Disability Income Benefits Due to Accident or Sickness.</p>
          <p>(a) Contract Reserves:</p>
          <p>Contracts issued on or after January 1, 2004:</p>
          <p>The 1987 Commissioners Group Disability Income Table (87CGDT).</p>
          <p>(b) Claim Reserves:</p>
          <p>For claims incurred on or after January 1, 2004:</p>
          <p>The 1987 Commissioners Group Disability Income Table (87CGDT);</p>
          <p>(2) Single Premium Credit Disability</p>
          <p>(a) Contract Reserves:</p>
          <p>(i) For contracts issued on or after January 1, 2004:</p>
          <p>(I) For plans having less than a 30-day elimination period, the 1985 Commissioners Individual Disability Table A (85CIDA) with claim incidence rates increased by 12 percent.</p>
          <p>(ii)(II) For plans having a 30-day and greater elimination period, the 85CIDA for a 14-day elimination period with the adjustment in item (I).</p>
          <p>(b) Claim Reserves:</p>
          <p>Claim reserves are to be determined as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.763">60A.763</a>.</p>
          <p>(3) Other Group Contract Benefits.</p>
          <p>(a) Contract Reserves:</p>
          <p>For all other group contract benefits, morbidity assumptions are to be determined as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.765">60A.765</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Claim Reserves:</p>
          <p>For all benefits other than disability, claim reserves are to be determined as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.763">60A.763</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.768.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Interest.</span></h2>
          <p>A. For contract reserves the maximum interest rate is the maximum rate permitted by law in the valuation of whole life insurance issued on the same date as the health insurance contract.</p>
          <p>B. For claim reserves on policies that require contract reserves, the maximum interest rate is the maximum rate permitted by law in the valuation of whole life insurance issued on the same date as the claim incurred date.</p>
          <p>C. For claim reserves on policies not requiring contract reserves, the maximum interest rate is the maximum rate permitted by law in the valuation of single premium immediate annuities issued on the same date as the claim incurred date, reduced by 100 basis points.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.768.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Mortality.</span></h2>
          <p>A. For individual long-term care insurance policies or group long-term care insurance certificates issued on or after January 1, 2004, the mortality basis used must be the 1983 Group Annuity Mortality Table without projection.</p>
          <p>B. Other mortality tables adopted by the NAIC and adopted by the commissioner may be used in the calculation of the minimum reserves if appropriate for the type of benefits and if approved by the commissioner. The request for approval must include the proposed mortality table and the reason that the standard specified in subsection A is inappropriate.</p>
          <p>C. For single premium credit insurance using the 85CIDA table, no separate mortality must be assumed.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

			">
        <h2>History: </h2>

      <h1 class="fgh">REINSURANCE AGREEMENTS</h1>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.80"><b>60A.80</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/426/#laws.0.14.0">1994 c 426 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.801"><b>60A.801</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/426/#laws.0.14.0">1994 c 426 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.802"><b>60A.802</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/426/#laws.0.14.0">1994 c 426 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.803">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.803 LIFE AND HEALTH REINSURANCE AGREEMENTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.803.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>This section applies to:</p>
          <p>(1) all domestic life and accident and sickness insurers;</p>
          <p>(2) all other licensed life and accident and sickness insurers which are not subject to a substantially similar regulation in their domiciliary state; and</p>
          <p>(3) licensed insurers with respect to their accident and sickness business.</p>
          <p class="bl">This section does not apply to assumption reinsurance, yearly renewable term reinsurance, or certain nonproportional reinsurance such as stop loss or catastrophe reinsurance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.803.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Accounting requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>No insurer subject to this section shall, for reinsurance ceded, reduce any liability or establish any asset in any financial statement filed with the commissioner if, by the terms of the reinsurance agreement, in substance or effect, any of the conditions in paragraphs (a) to (k) exist:</p>
          <p>(a) The renewal expense allowances provided or to be provided to the ceding insurer by the reinsurer in any accounting period, are not sufficient to cover anticipated allocable renewal expenses of the ceding insurer on the portion of the business reinsured, unless a liability is established for the present value of the shortfall, using assumptions equal to the applicable statutory reserve basis on the business reinsured. Those expenses include commissions, premium taxes, and direct expenses including, but not limited to, billing, valuation, claims, and maintenance expected by the company at the time the business is reinsured.</p>
          <p>(b) The ceding insurer can be deprived of surplus or assets at the reinsurer's option or automatically upon the occurrence of some event, such as the insolvency of the ceding insurer, except that termination of the reinsurance agreement by the reinsurer for nonpayment of reinsurance premiums or other amounts due, such as modified coinsurance reserve adjustments, interest and adjustments on funds withheld, and tax reimbursements, shall not be considered to be a deprivation of surplus or assets.</p>
          <p>(c) The ceding insurer is required to reimburse the reinsurer for negative experience under the reinsurance agreement, except that neither offsetting experience refunds against current and prior years' losses under the agreement nor payment by the ceding insurer of an amount equal to the current and prior years' losses under the agreement upon voluntary termination of in force reinsurance by the ceding insurer is considered such a reimbursement to the reinsurer for negative experience. Voluntary termination does not include situations where termination occurs because of unreasonable provisions which allow the reinsurer to reduce its risk under the agreement. An example of such a provision is the right of the reinsurer to increase reinsurance premiums or risk and expense charges to excessive levels forcing the ceding company to prematurely terminate the reinsurance treaty.</p>
          <p>(d) The ceding insurer must, at specific points in time scheduled in the agreement, terminate or automatically recapture all or part of the reinsurance ceded.</p>
          <p>(e) The reinsurance agreement involves the possible payment by the ceding insurer to the reinsurer of amounts other than from income realized from the reinsured policies. It is improper for a ceding company to pay reinsurance premiums, or other fees or charges to a reinsurer, which are greater than the direct premiums collected by the ceding company.</p>
          <p>(f) The reinsurance agreement does not transfer all of the significant risk inherent in the business being reinsured. The following table identifies, for a representative sampling of products or type of business, the risks that are considered to be significant. For products not specifically included, the risks determined to be significant must be consistent with this table.</p>
          <p>Risk categories:</p>
          <p>(1) morbidity;</p>
          <p>(2) mortality;</p>
          <p>(3) lapse, which is the risk that a policy will voluntarily terminate prior to the recoupment of a statutory surplus strain experienced at issue of the policy;</p>
          <p>(4) credit quality (C1), which is the risk that invested assets supporting the reinsured business will decrease in value. The main hazards are that assets will default or that there will be a decrease in earning power. It excludes market value declines due to changes in interest rate;</p>
          <p>(5) reinvestment (C3), which is the risk that interest rates will fall and funds reinvested (coupon payments or money received upon asset maturity or call) will therefore earn less than expected. If asset durations are less than liability durations, the mismatch will increase; and</p>
          <p>(6) disintermediation (C3), which is the risk that interest rates rise and policy loans and surrenders increase or maturing contracts do not renew at anticipated rates of renewal. If asset durations are greater than the liability durations, the mismatch will increase. Policyholders will move their funds into new products offering higher rates. The company may have to sell assets at a loss to provide for these withdrawals.</p>
          <p class="ce">RISK CATEGORY</p>

          <p class="bl1">0 = Insignificant</p>

          <p class="bl1">*LTC = Long-Term Care Insurance</p>
          <p class="bl1">LTD = Long-Term Disability Insurance</p>
          <p>(g)(1) The credit quality, reinvestment, or disintermediation risk is significant for the business reinsured and the ceding company does not, other than for the classes of business excepted in clause (2), either transfer the underlying assets to the reinsurer or legally segregate such assets in a trust or escrow account or otherwise establish a mechanism satisfactory to the commissioner that legally segregates, by contract or contract provision, the underlying assets.</p>
          <p>(2) Notwithstanding the requirements of clause (1), the assets supporting the reserves for the following classes of business and any classes of business that do not have a significant credit quality, reinvestment or disintermediation risk, may be held by the ceding company without segregation of the assets:</p>
          <p>(i) Health Insurance - LTC/LTD;</p>
          <p>(ii) Traditional Nonpar Permanent;</p>
          <p>(iii) Traditional Par Permanent;</p>
          <p>(iv) Adjustable Premium Permanent;</p>
          <p>(v) Indeterminate Premium Permanent; and/or</p>
          <p>(vi) Universal Life Fixed Premium (no dump-in premiums allowed).</p>
          <p>The associated formula for determining the reserve interest rate adjustment must reflect the ceding company's investment earnings and incorporate all realized and unrealized gains and losses reflected in the statutory statement. The following is an acceptable formula:</p>
          <p>Rate = 2(I+CG) / (X + Y - I - CG)</p>
          <table>
            <col style="width:10.2803738317757%">
            <col style="width:10.2803738317757%">
            <col style="width:79.4392523364486%">
            <tr>
              <td>Where:</td>
              <td></td>
              <td>I is the net investment income</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td></td>
              <td></td>
              <td>CG is capital gains less capital losses</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td></td>
              <td></td>
              <td>X is the current year cash and invested assets plus investment<br>income due and accrued less borrowed money</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td></td>
              <td></td>
              <td>Y is the same as X but for the prior year</td>
            </tr>
          </table>
          <p>(h) Settlements are made less frequently than quarterly or payments due from the reinsurer are not made in cash within 90 days of the settlement date.</p>
          <p>(i) The ceding insurer is required to make representations or warranties not reasonably related to the business being reinsured.</p>
          <p>(j) The ceding insurer is required to make representations or warranties about future performance of the business being reinsured.</p>
          <p>(k) The reinsurance agreement is entered into for the principal purpose of producing significant surplus aid for the ceding insurer, typically on a temporary basis, while not transferring all of the significant risks inherent in the business reinsured and, in substance or effect, the expected potential liability to the ceding insurer remains basically unchanged.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.803.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Commissioner approval.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding subdivision 2, an insurer subject to this section may, with the prior approval of the commissioner, take such reserve credit or establish such asset as the commissioner deems consistent with state insurance law or rules.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.803.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Filing.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Agreements entered into after August 1, 1994, that involve the reinsurance of business issued prior to the effective date of the agreements, along with any subsequent amendments thereto, shall be filed by the ceding company with the commissioner within 30 days from their date of execution. Each filing shall include data detailing the financial impact of the transaction. The ceding insurer's actuary who signs the financial statement actuarial opinion with respect to valuation of reserves shall consider this section and any applicable actuarial standards of practice when determining the proper credit in financial statements filed with the commissioner. The actuary shall maintain adequate documentation and be prepared upon request to describe the actuarial work performed for inclusion in the financial statements and to demonstrate that the work conforms to this section.</p>
          <p>(b) Any increase in surplus net of federal income tax resulting from arrangements described in paragraph (a) must be identified separately on the insurer's statutory financial statement as a surplus item (aggregate write-ins for gains and losses in surplus in the capital and surplus account of the annual statement) and recognition of the surplus increase as income must be reflected on a net of tax basis in the "Reinsurance ceded" line of the annual statement as earnings emerge from the business reinsured.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.803.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Written agreements.</span></h2>
          <p>No reinsurance agreement or amendment to any agreement may be used to reduce any liability or to establish any asset in any financial statement filed with the commissioner, unless the agreement, amendment, or a binding letter or intent has been duly executed by both parties no later than the "as of date" of the financial statement. In the case of a letter of intent, a reinsurance agreement or an amendment to a reinsurance agreement must be executed within a reasonable period of time, not exceeding 90 days from the execution date of the letter of intent, in order for credit to be granted for the reinsurance ceded. The reinsurance agreement must provide that:</p>
          <p>(1) the agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the business being reinsured under it and that there are no understandings between the parties other than as expressed in the agreement; and</p>
          <p>(2) any change or modification to the agreement is null and void unless made by amendment to the agreement and signed by both parties.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.803.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Reserve credits.</span></h2>
          <p>Insurers subject to this section shall reduce to zero by December 31, 1995, any reserve credits or assets established with respect to reinsurance agreements entered into prior to August 1, 1994, that under the provisions of this section would not be entitled to recognition of the reserve credits or assets; provided, however, that the reinsurance agreements have been in compliance with laws or regulations in existence immediately preceding August 1, 1994.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <h1 class="fgh">INSURANCE REGULATORY INFORMATION SYSTEM</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.90">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.90 SCOPE.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.90">60A.90</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.94">60A.94</a> apply to all domestic, foreign, and alien insurers who are authorized to transact business in this state.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.90.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.12.1.0">1991 c 325 art 12 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.91">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.91 FILING REQUIREMENTS.</h1>
        <p>(a) A domestic, foreign, and alien insurer who is authorized to transact insurance in this state shall annually on or before March 1 of each year, file with the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) a copy of its annual statement convention blank, along with additional filings prescribed by the commissioner for the preceding year. The information filed with the National Association of Insurance Commissioners must be in the same format and scope as that required by the commissioner and must include the signed jurat page and the actuarial certification. Amendments and addenda to the annual statement filing subsequently filed with the commissioner must also be filed with the NAIC.</p>
        <p>(b) Foreign insurers that are domiciled in a state that has a law substantially similar to paragraph (a) is considered to be in compliance with this section.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.91.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.12.2.0">1991 c 325 art 12 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.92">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.92 IMMUNITY.</h1>
        <p>In the absence of actual malice, members of the NAIC, their duly authorized committees, subcommittees, and task forces, their delegates, NAIC employees, and all others charged with the responsibility of collecting, reviewing, analyzing, and disseminating the information developed from the filing of the annual statement convention blanks are acting as agents of the commissioner under the authority of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.90">60A.90</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.94">60A.94</a> and are not subject to civil liability for libel, slander, or any other cause of action by virtue of their collection, review, and analysis or dissemination of the data and information collected from the filings required under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.90">60A.90</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.94">60A.94</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.92.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.12.3.0">1991 c 325 art 12 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.93">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.93 CONFIDENTIALITY.</h1>
        <p>All financial analysis ratios and examination synopses concerning insurance companies that are submitted to the department by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners' Insurance Regulatory Information System are confidential and may not be disclosed by the department.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.93.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.12.4.0">1991 c 325 art 12 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.94">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.94 REVOCATION OF CERTIFICATE OF AUTHORITY.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner may suspend, revoke, or refuse to renew the certificate of authority of an insurer failing to file its annual statement when due or within any extension of time that the commissioner, for good cause, may have granted.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.94.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/325/#laws.12.5.0">1991 c 325 art 12 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">INSURANCE FRAUD</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.951">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.951 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>The definitions in this section apply to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.951">60A.951</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.956">60A.956</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Authorized person.</span></h2>
          <p>"Authorized person" means the county attorney, sheriff, or chief of police responsible for investigations in the county where the suspected insurance fraud occurred; the superintendent of the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension; the commissioner of commerce; the Commerce Fraud Bureau; the commissioner of labor and industry; the attorney general; or any duly constituted criminal investigative department or agency of the United States.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of commerce for insurers regulated by the commissioner of commerce, and means the commissioner of health for insurers regulated by the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Insurance fraud.</span></h2>
          <p>"Insurance fraud" occurs when a person presents or causes to be presented to any insurer, or prepares with knowledge or belief that it will be so presented, a written or oral statement, including a computer-generated document, an electronic claim filing, or other electronic transmission, that contains materially false or misleading information, or a material and misleading omission, concerning:</p>
          <p>(1) an application for the issuance of an insurance policy;</p>
          <p>(2) the rating of an insurance policy;</p>
          <p>(3) a claim for payment, reimbursement, or benefits payable under an insurance policy to an insured, a beneficiary, or a third party;</p>
          <p>(4) premiums on an insurance policy; or</p>
          <p>(5) payments made in accordance with the terms of an insurance policy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Insurance policy or policy.</span></h2>
          <p>"Insurance policy" or "policy" means the written instrument in which are set forth the terms of any certificate of insurance, binder of coverage, or contract of insurance, including a certificate, binder, or contract issued by a state-assigned risk plan; benefit plan; nonprofit hospital service plan; motor club service plan; or surety bond, cash bond, or any other alternative to insurance authorized by the Minnesota Financial Responsibility Act.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.4b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4b.<span class="headnote">Insurance professional.</span></h2>
          <p>"Insurance professional" means sales agents, agencies, managing general agents, brokers, producers, claims representatives, adjusters, and third-party administrators.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.4c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4c.<span class="headnote">Insurance transaction.</span></h2>
          <p>"Insurance transaction" means a transaction by, between, or among:</p>
          <p>(1) an insurer or a person who acts on behalf of an insurer; and</p>
          <p>(2) an insured, claimant, applicant for insurance, public adjuster, insurance professional, practitioner who performs professional services as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/319B.02#stat.319B.02.19">319B.02, subdivision 19</a>, attorney, or any person who acts on behalf of any of the foregoing for the purpose of obtaining insurance or reinsurance, calculating insurance premiums, submitting a claim, negotiating or adjusting a claim, or otherwise obtaining insurance, self-insurance, or reinsurance, or obtaining the benefits or annuities thereof or therefrom.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Insurer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Insurer" means insurance company, risk retention group as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60E.02">60E.02</a>, service plan corporation as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62C.02">62C.02</a>, health maintenance organization as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62D.02">62D.02</a>, community integrated service network as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62N.02">62N.02</a>, fraternal benefit society regulated under chapter 64B, township mutual company regulated under chapter 67A, joint self-insurance plan or multiple employer trust regulated under chapter 60F, 62H, or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/471.617#stat.471.617.2">471.617, subdivision 2</a>, persons administering a self-insurance plan as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.23#stat.60A.23.8">60A.23, subdivision 8</a>, clause (2), paragraphs (a) and (d), and the Workers' Compensation Reinsurance Association established in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/79.34">79.34</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Person.</span></h2>
          <p>"Person" means a natural person, company, corporation, unincorporated association, partnership, professional corporation, and any other entity.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.5b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5b.<span class="headnote">Premium.</span></h2>
          <p>"Premium" means consideration paid or payable for coverage under an insurance policy. Premium includes any payment, whether due within the insurance policy term or otherwise; any deductible payment, whether advanced by the insurer or insurance professional and subject to reimbursement by the insured or otherwise; any self-insured retention or payment, whether advanced by the insurer or insurance professional and subject to reimbursement by the insured or otherwise; and any collateral or security to be provided to collateralize any such obligations to pay.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.951.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Relevant information.</span></h2>
          <p>"Relevant information" includes, but is not limited to:</p>
          <p>(1) pertinent insurance policy information, including the application for a policy;</p>
          <p>(2) policy premium payment records;</p>
          <p>(3) a history of previous claims made by the insured including, where the insured is a corporation, limited liability company, or partnership, a history of claims by a subsidiary or any affiliates, and a history of claims of any other business association in which individual officers or partners or their family members are known to be involved;</p>
          <p>(4) material relating to the investigation, including the statement of any person and the proof of loss;</p>
          <p>(5) billing records; and</p>
          <p>(6) any other information which an authorized person identifies and which appears reasonably related to the investigation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.951.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/574/#laws.0.1.0">1994 c 574 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/258/#laws.0.9.0">1995 c 258 s 9</a>,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/225/#laws.2.1.0">1997 c 225 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/331/#laws.0.2.0">2002 c 331 s 2</a>-8;  <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/135/#laws.3.22.0">2013 c 135 art 3 s 22</a></p>
