Upon the escrow agent's receipt of the acknowledgment of the properly completed transfer of ownership, assignment, or designation of beneficiary from the insurance company, the escrow agent shall pay the settlement proceeds to the viator.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9579.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Tendering consideration.</span></h2>
          <p>Failure to tender consideration to the viator for the viatical settlement contract within the time set forth in the disclosure pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9577#stat.60A.9577.1">60A.9577, subdivision 1</a>, clause (6), renders the viatical settlement contract voidable by the viator for lack of consideration until the time consideration is tendered to and accepted by the viator. Funds shall be deemed sent by a viatical settlement provider to a viator as of the date that the escrow agent either releases funds for wire transfer to the viator or places a check for delivery to the viator by United States mail or other nationally recognized delivery service.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9579.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Health status contacts.</span></h2>
          <p>Contacts with the insured for the purpose of determining the health status of the insured by the viatical settlement provider or viatical settlement broker after the viatical settlement has occurred shall only be made by the viatical settlement provider or broker licensed in this state or its authorized representatives and shall be limited to once every three months for insureds with a life expectancy of more than one year, and to no more than once per month for insureds with a life expectancy of one year or less. The provider or broker shall explain the procedure for these contacts at the time the viatical settlement contract is entered into. The limitations in this subdivision shall not apply to any contacts with an insured for reasons other than determining the insured's health status. Viatical settlement providers and viatical settlement brokers shall be responsible for the actions of their authorized representatives.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9579.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.8.0">2009 c 62 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9581">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9581 PROHIBITED PRACTICES AND CONFLICTS OF INTEREST.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9581.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Solicitations and sales to controlled person.</span></h2>
          <p>With respect to any viatical settlement contract or insurance policy, no viatical settlement broker knowingly shall solicit an offer from, effectuate a viatical settlement with, or make a sale to any viatical settlement provider, viatical settlement purchaser, viatical settlement investment agent, financing entity, or related provider trust that is controlling, controlled by, or under common control with the viatical settlement broker unless this relationship is disclosed to the viator.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9581.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Payment to controlled broker.</span></h2>
          <p>With respect to any viatical settlement contract or insurance policy, no viatical settlement provider knowingly may enter into a viatical settlement contract with a viator, if, in connection with a viatical settlement contract, anything of value will be paid to a viatical settlement broker that is controlling, controlled by, or under common control with the viatical settlement provider or the viatical settlement purchaser, viatical settlement investment agent, financing entity, or related provider trust that is involved in a viatical settlement contract unless this relationship is disclosed to the viator.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9581.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Fraudulent viatical settlement act.</span></h2>
          <p>A violation of subdivisions 1 and 2 is deemed a fraudulent viatical settlement act.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9581.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Advertising.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) No viatical settlement provider shall enter into a viatical settlement contract unless the viatical settlement promotional, advertising, and marketing materials, as may be prescribed by rule, have been filed with the commissioner. In no event shall any marketing materials expressly reference that the insurance is "free" for any period of time. The inclusion of any reference in the marketing materials that would cause a viator to reasonably believe that the insurance is free for any period of time shall be considered a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.957">60A.957</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9585">60A.9585</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) No life insurance producer, insurance company, viatical settlement broker, viatical settlement provider, or viatical settlement investment agent shall make any statement or representation to the applicant or policyholder in connection with the sale or financing of a life insurance policy to the effect that the insurance is free or without cost to the policyholder for any period of time unless provided in the policy.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9581.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.9.0">2009 c 62 s 9</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9582">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9582 ADVERTISING FOR VIATICAL SETTLEMENTS AND VIATICAL SETTLEMENTS PURCHASE AGREEMENTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>This section applies to any advertising of viatical settlement contracts, viatical purchase agreements, or related products or services intended for dissemination in this state, including Internet advertising viewed by persons located in this state. Where disclosure requirements are established pursuant to federal regulation, this section shall be interpreted so as to minimize or eliminate conflict with federal regulation wherever possible.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">System of control.</span></h2>
          <p>Every viatical settlement licensee shall establish and at all times maintain a system of control over the content, form, and method of dissemination of all advertisements of its contracts, products, and services. All advertisements, regardless of by whom written, created, designed, or presented, shall be the responsibility of the viatical settlement licensees, as well as the individual who created or presented the advertisement. A system of control shall include regular routine notification, at least once a year, to agents and others authorized by the viatical settlement licensee who disseminate advertisements of the requirements and procedures for approval prior to the use of any advertisements not furnished by the viatical settlement licensee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Form and content.</span></h2>
          <p>Advertisements shall be truthful and not misleading in fact or by implication. The form and content of an advertisement of a viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement, product, or service shall be sufficiently complete and clear so as to avoid deception and it shall not have the capacity or tendency to mislead or deceive. Whether an advertisement has the capacity or tendency to mislead or deceive shall be determined by the commissioner from the overall impression that the advertisement may be reasonably expected to create upon a person of average education or intelligence within the segment of the public to which it is directed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">False and misleading advertisements.</span></h2>
          <p>Certain viatical settlement advertisements are deemed false and misleading on their face and are prohibited. False and misleading viatical settlement advertisements include, but are not limited to, the following representations:</p>
          <p>(1) "guaranteed," "fully secured," "100 percent secured," "fully insured," "secure," "safe," "backed by rated insurance companies," "backed by federal law," "backed by state law," "state guaranty funds," or similar representations;</p>
          <p>(2) "no risk," "minimal risk," "low risk," "no speculation," "no fluctuation," or similar representations;</p>
          <p>(3) "qualified or approved for individual retirement accounts (IRAs), Roth IRAs, 401(k) plans, simplified employee pensions (SEP), 403(b), Keogh plans, TSA, other retirement account rollovers," "tax deferred," or similar representations;</p>
          <p>(4) utilization of the word "guaranteed" to describe the fixed return, annual return, principal, earnings, profits, investment, or similar representations;</p>
          <p>(5) "no sales charges or fees" or similar representations;</p>
          <p>(6) "high yield," "superior return," "excellent return," "high return," "quick profit," or similar representations; and</p>
          <p>(7) purported favorable representations or testimonials about the benefits of viatical settlement contracts or viatical settlement purchase agreements as an investment, taken out of context from newspapers, trade papers, journals, radio and television programs, and all other forms of print and electronic media.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Disclosures regulated.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The information required to be disclosed under this section shall not be minimized, rendered obscure, or presented in ambiguous fashion or intermingled with the text of the advertisement so as to be confusing or misleading.</p>
          <p>(b) An advertisement shall not omit material information or use words, phrases, statements, references, or illustrations if the omission or use has the capacity, tendency, or effect of misleading or deceiving viators, purchasers, or prospective purchasers as to the nature or extent of any benefit, loss covered, premium payable, or state or federal tax consequence. The fact that the viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement offered is made available for inspection prior to consummation of the sale, or an offer is made to refund the payment if the viator is not satisfied or that the viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement includes a "free look" period that satisfies or exceeds legal requirements, does not remedy misleading statements.</p>
          <p>(c) An advertisement shall not use the name or title of a life insurance company or a life insurance policy unless the advertisement has been approved by the insurer.</p>
          <p>(d) An advertisement shall not represent that premium payments will not be required to be paid on the life insurance policy that is the subject of a viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement in order to maintain that policy, unless that is the fact.</p>
          <p>(e) An advertisement shall not state or imply that interest charged on an accelerated death benefit or a policy loan is unfair, inequitable, or in any manner an incorrect or improper practice.</p>
          <p>(f) The words "free," "no cost," "without cost," "no additional cost," "at no extra cost," or words of similar import shall not be used with respect to any benefit or service unless true. An advertisement may specify the charge for a benefit or a service or may state that a charge is included in the payment or use other appropriate language.</p>
          <p>(g) Testimonials, appraisals, or analysis used in advertisements must be genuine; represent the current opinion of the author; be applicable to the viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement product or service advertised, if any; and be accurately reproduced with sufficient completeness to avoid misleading or deceiving prospective viators or purchasers as to the nature or scope of the testimonials, appraisal, analysis, or endorsement. In using testimonials, appraisals, or analysis, a licensee under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.957">60A.957</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9585">60A.9585</a> makes as its own all the statements contained therein, and the statements are subject to all the provisions of this section.</p>
          <p>(h) If the individual making a testimonial, appraisal, analysis, or endorsement has a financial interest in the party making use of the testimonial, appraisal, analysis, or endorsement, either directly or through a related entity as a stockholder, director, officer, employee, or otherwise, or receives any benefit directly or indirectly other than required union-scale wages, that fact shall be prominently disclosed in the advertisement.</p>
          <p>(i) An advertisement shall not state or imply that a viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement, benefit, or service has been approved or endorsed by a group of individuals, society, association, or other organization unless that is the fact and unless any relationship between an organization and the viatical settlement licensee is disclosed. If the entity making the endorsement or testimonial is owned, controlled, or managed by the viatical settlement licensee, or receives any payment or other consideration from the viatical settlement licensee for making an endorsement or testimonial, that fact shall be disclosed in the advertisement.</p>
          <p>(j) When an endorsement refers to benefits received under a viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement, all pertinent information shall be retained for a period of five years after its use.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Statistics.</span></h2>
          <p>An advertisement shall not contain statistical information unless it accurately reflects recent and relevant facts. The source of all statistics used in an advertisement shall be identified.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Disparaging advertisements.</span></h2>
          <p>An advertisement shall not disparage insurers, viatical settlement providers, viatical settlement brokers, viatical settlement investment agents, insurance producers, policies, services, or methods of marketing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Licensee's name.</span></h2>
          <p>The name of the viatical settlement licensee shall be clearly identified in all advertisements about the licensee or its viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreements, products, or services, and if any specific viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement is advertised, the viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement shall be identified either by form number or some other appropriate description. If an application is part of the advertisement, the name of the viatical settlement provider shall be shown on the application.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Licensee disclosure.</span></h2>
          <p>An advertisement shall not use a trade name, group designation, name of the parent company of a viatical settlement licensee, name of a particular division of the viatical settlement licensee, service mark, slogan, symbol, or other device or reference without disclosing the name of the viatical settlement licensee, if the advertisement would have the capacity or tendency to mislead or deceive as to the true identity of the viatical settlement licensee, or to create the impression that a company other than the viatical settlement licensee would have any responsibility for the financial obligation under a viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Government sponsorship; misleading advertisements.</span></h2>
          <p>An advertisement shall not use any combination of words, symbols, or physical materials that by their content, phraseology, shape, color, or other characteristics are so similar to a combination of words, symbols, or physical materials used by a government program or agency or otherwise appear to be of such a nature that they tend to mislead prospective viators or purchasers into believing that the solicitation is in some manner connected with a government program or agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">State licensure.</span></h2>
          <p>An advertisement may state that a viatical settlement licensee is licensed in the state where the advertisement appears, provided it does not exaggerate that fact or suggest or imply that a competing viatical settlement licensee may not be so licensed. The advertisement may ask the audience to consult the licensee's website or contact the Department of Commerce to find out if the state requires licensing and, if so, whether the viatical settlement provider, viatical settlement broker, or viatical settlement investment agent is licensed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Government entity endorsement.</span></h2>
          <p>An advertisement shall not create the impression that the viatical settlement provider, its financial condition or status, the payment of its claims, or the merits, desirability, or advisability of its viatical settlement contracts or viatical settlement purchase agreement forms are recommended or endorsed by any government entity.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Name.</span></h2>
          <p>The name of the actual licensee shall be stated in all of its advertisements. An advertisement shall not use a trade name, any group designation, name of any affiliate or controlling entity of the licensee, service mark, slogan, symbol, or other device in a manner that would have the capacity or tendency to mislead or deceive as to the true identity of the actual licensee or create the false impression that an affiliate or controlling entity would have any responsibility for the financial obligation of the licensee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Government approval.</span></h2>
          <p>An advertisement shall not directly or indirectly create the impression that any division or agency of the state or of the United States government endorses, approves, or favors:</p>
          <p>(1) any viatical settlement licensee or its business practices or methods of operation;</p>
          <p>(2) the merits, desirability, or advisability of any viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement;</p>
          <p>(3) any viatical settlement contract or viatical settlement purchase agreement; or</p>
          <p>(4) any life insurance policy or life insurance company.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Time frame disclosure.</span></h2>
          <p>If the advertiser emphasizes the speed with which the viatication will occur, the advertising must disclose the average time frame from completed application to the date of offer and from acceptance of the offer to receipt of the funds by the viator.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9582.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Average purchase price.</span></h2>
          <p>If the advertising emphasizes the dollar amounts available to viators, the advertising shall disclose the average purchase price as a percent of face value obtained by viators contracting with the licensee during the past six months.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9582.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.10.0">2009 c 62 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9583">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9583 FRAUD PREVENTION AND CONTROL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9583.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Fraudulent viatical settlement acts, interference, and participation of convicted felons prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person who commits a fraudulent viatical settlement act commits insurance fraud and may be sentenced under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.611#stat.609.611.3">609.611, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) A person shall not knowingly or intentionally interfere with the enforcement of the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.957">60A.957</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9585">60A.9585</a> or investigations of suspected or actual violations of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.957">60A.957</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9585">60A.9585</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) A person in the business of viatical settlements shall not knowingly or intentionally permit any person convicted of a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust to participate in the business of viatical settlements.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9583.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Fraud warning required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Viatical settlements contracts and purchase agreement forms and applications for viatical settlements, regardless of the form of transmission, shall contain the following statement or a substantially similar statement: "Any person who knowingly presents false information in an application for insurance or viatical settlement contract or a viatical settlement purchase agreement is guilty of a crime and may be subject to fines and confinement in prison."</p>
          <p>(b) The lack of a statement as required in paragraph (a) does not constitute a defense in any prosecution for a fraudulent viatical settlement act.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9583.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Mandatory reporting of fraudulent viatical settlement acts.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person engaged in the business of viatical settlements having knowledge or a reasonable suspicion that a fraudulent viatical settlement act is being, will be, or has been committed shall provide to the commissioner such information as required by, and in a manner prescribed by, the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9583.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Viatical settlement antifraud initiatives.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Viatical settlement providers and viatical settlement brokers shall have in place antifraud initiatives reasonably calculated to detect, prosecute, and prevent fraudulent viatical settlement acts. At the discretion of the commissioner, the commissioner may order, or a licensee may request and the commissioner may grant, such modifications of the following required initiatives as necessary to ensure an effective antifraud program. The modifications may be more or less restrictive than the required initiatives so long as the modifications may reasonably be expected to accomplish the purpose of this section.</p>
          <p>(b) Antifraud initiatives shall include:</p>
          <p>(1) fraud investigators, who may be viatical settlement provider or viatical settlement broker employees or independent contractors; and</p>
          <p>(2) an antifraud plan, which shall be submitted to the commissioner. The antifraud plan shall include, but not be limited to:</p>
          <p>(i) a description of the procedures for detecting and investigating possible fraudulent viatical settlement acts and procedures for resolving material inconsistencies between medical records and insurance applications;</p>
          <p>(ii) a description of the procedures for reporting possible fraudulent viatical settlement acts to the commissioner;</p>
          <p>(iii) a description of the plan for antifraud education and training of underwriters and other personnel; and</p>
          <p>(iv) a description or chart outlining the organizational arrangement of the antifraud personnel who are responsible for the investigation and reporting of possible fraudulent viatical settlement acts and investigating unresolved material inconsistencies between medical records and insurance applications.</p>
          <p>(c) Antifraud plans submitted to the commissioner shall be privileged and confidential and shall not be a public record and shall not be subject to discovery or subpoena in a civil or criminal action.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9583.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.11.0">2009 c 62 s 11</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9585">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9585 UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICE.</h1>
        <p>A violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.957">60A.957</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9585">60A.9585</a>, including the commission of a fraudulent viatical settlement act, shall be considered an unfair trade practice under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/72A.20">72A.20</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9585.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.12.0">2009 c 62 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.961"><b>60A.961</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.962"><b>60A.962</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.963"><b>60A.963</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.964">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.964 FEES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.964.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Amount.</span></h2>
          <p>The licensing fee for a viatical settlement provider, viatical settlement broker, or viatical settlement investment agent license is $750 for initial licensure and $250 for each annual renewal. The fees must be limited to the cost of license administration and enforcement and must be deposited in the state treasury, credited to a special account, and appropriated to the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.964.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Automatic revocation.</span></h2>
          <p>A license is automatically revoked for failure to pay the licensing fee within the terms prescribed by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.964.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/151/#laws.0.5.0">1995 c 151 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/250/#laws.3.6.0">1999 c 250 art 3 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.13.0">2009 c 62 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.965"><b>60A.965</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.966"><b>60A.966</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.967"><b>60A.967</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.968"><b>60A.968</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.969"><b>60A.969</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.970"><b>60A.970</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.971"><b>60A.971</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.972"><b>60A.972</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.973"><b>60A.973</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.974"><b>60A.974</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/62/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 62 s 14</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">STRUCTURED SETTLEMENT ANNUITIES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.975">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.975 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.975.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.975">60A.975</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.976">60A.976</a>, the definitions in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.975.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Annuity issuer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Annuity issuer" means an insurer that issues an insurance contract used to fund periodic payments under a structured settlement agreement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.975.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Structured settlement.</span></h2>
          <p>"Structured settlement" means an arrangement for periodic payment of damages entered on behalf of a minor or incompetent person for personal injuries established by settlement or judgment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.975.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Structured settlement agreement.</span></h2>
          <p>"Structured settlement agreement" means the agreement, judgment, stipulation, or release embodying the terms of a structured settlement.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.975.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/131/#laws.0.4.0">2001 c 131 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.976">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.976 ANNUITY ISSUERS FINANCIAL REQUIREMENTS.</h1>
        <p>An annuity purchased to finance a structured settlement agreement may be purchased only from an annuity issuer with a financial rating equivalent to A.M. Best Company A+ Class 8 or better; or a Standard &amp; Poor's AA or better.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.976.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/131/#laws.0.5.0">2001 c 131 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">INFORMATION SECURITY PROGRAM</h1>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.98"><b>60A.98</b> MS 2020 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.29.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 29</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.981"><b>60A.981</b> MS 2020 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.29.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 29</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.60A.982"><b>60A.982</b> MS 2020 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.29.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 29</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.985">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.985 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Terms.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.985">60A.985</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9857">60A.9857</a>, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Authorized individual.</span></h2>
          <p>"Authorized individual" means an individual known to and screened by the licensee and determined to be necessary and appropriate to have access to the nonpublic information held by the licensee and its information systems.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Consumer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Consumer" means an individual, including but not limited to an applicant, policyholder, insured, beneficiary, claimant, and certificate holder who is a resident of this state and whose nonpublic information is in a licensee's possession, custody, or control.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Cybersecurity event.</span></h2>
          <p>"Cybersecurity event" means an event resulting in unauthorized access to, or disruption or misuse of, an information system or nonpublic information stored on an information system.</p>
          <p>Cybersecurity event does not include the unauthorized acquisition of encrypted nonpublic information if the encryption, process, or key is not also acquired, released, or used without authorization.</p>
          <p>Cybersecurity event does not include an event with regard to which the licensee has determined that the nonpublic information accessed by an unauthorized person has not been used or released and has been returned or destroyed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Encrypted.</span></h2>
          <p>"Encrypted" means the transformation of data into a form which results in a low probability of assigning meaning without the use of a protective process or key.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Information security program.</span></h2>
          <p>"Information security program" means the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards that a licensee uses to access, collect, distribute, process, protect, store, use, transmit, dispose of, or otherwise handle nonpublic information.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Information system.</span></h2>
          <p>"Information system" means a discrete set of electronic information resources organized for the collection, processing, maintenance, use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition of nonpublic electronic information, as well as any specialized system such as industrial or process controls systems, telephone switching and private branch exchange systems, and environmental control systems.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Licensee.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensee" means any person licensed, authorized to operate, or registered, or required to be licensed, authorized, or registered by the Department of Commerce or the Department of Health under chapters 59A to 62M, 62Q to 62V, and 64B to 79A.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Multifactor authentication.</span></h2>
          <p>"Multifactor authentication" means authentication through verification of at least two of the following types of authentication factors:</p>
          <p>(1) knowledge factors, such as a password;</p>
          <p>(2) possession factors, such as a token or text message on a mobile phone; or</p>
          <p>(3) inherence factors, such as a biometric characteristic.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Nonpublic information.</span></h2>
          <p>"Nonpublic information" means electronic information that is not publicly available information and is:</p>
          <p>(1) any information concerning a consumer which because of name, number, personal mark, or other identifier can be used to identify the consumer, in combination with any one or more of the following data elements:</p>
          <p>(i) Social Security number;</p>
          <p>(ii) driver's license number or nondriver identification card number;</p>
          <p>(iii) financial account number, credit card number, or debit card number;</p>
          <p>(iv) any security code, access code, or password that would permit access to a consumer's financial account; or</p>
          <p>(v) biometric records; or</p>
          <p>(2) any information or data, except age or gender, in any form or medium created by or derived from a health care provider or a consumer that can be used to identify a particular consumer and that relates to:</p>
          <p>(i) the past, present, or future physical, mental, or behavioral health or condition of any consumer or a member of the consumer's family;</p>
          <p>(ii) the provision of health care to any consumer; or</p>
          <p>(iii) payment for the provision of health care to any consumer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Person.</span></h2>
          <p>"Person" means any individual or any nongovernmental entity, including but not limited to any nongovernmental partnership, corporation, branch, agency, or association.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Publicly available information.</span></h2>
          <p>"Publicly available information" means any information that a licensee has a reasonable basis to believe is lawfully made available to the general public from: federal, state, or local government records; widely distributed media; or disclosures to the general public that are required to be made by federal, state, or local law.</p>
          <p>For the purposes of this definition, a licensee has a reasonable basis to believe that information is lawfully made available to the general public if the licensee has taken steps to determine:</p>
          <p>(1) that the information is of the type that is available to the general public; and</p>
          <p>(2) whether a consumer can direct that the information not be made available to the general public and, if so, that such consumer has not done so.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Risk assessment.</span></h2>
          <p>"Risk assessment" means the risk assessment that each licensee is required to conduct under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9851#stat.60A.9851.3">60A.9851, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">State.</span></h2>
          <p>"State" means the state of Minnesota.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.985.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Third-party service provider.</span></h2>
          <p>"Third-party service provider" means a person, not otherwise defined as a licensee, that contracts with a licensee to maintain, process, or store nonpublic information, or is otherwise permitted access to nonpublic information through its provision of services to the licensee.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.985.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.5.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.14.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 14</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9851">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9851 INFORMATION SECURITY PROGRAM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9851.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Implementation of an information security program.</span></h2>
          <p>Commensurate with the size and complexity of the licensee, the nature and scope of the licensee's activities, including its use of third-party service providers, and the sensitivity of the nonpublic information used by the licensee or in the licensee's possession, custody, or control, each licensee shall develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive written information security program based on the licensee's risk assessment and that contains administrative, technical, and physical safeguards for the protection of nonpublic information and the licensee's information system.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9851.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Objectives of an information security program.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensee's information security program shall be designed to:</p>
          <p>(1) protect the security and confidentiality of nonpublic information and the security of the information system;</p>
          <p>(2) protect against any threats or hazards to the security or integrity of nonpublic information and the information system;</p>
          <p>(3) protect against unauthorized access to, or use of, nonpublic information, and minimize the likelihood of harm to any consumer; and</p>
          <p>(4) define and periodically reevaluate a schedule for retention of nonpublic information and a mechanism for its destruction when no longer needed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9851.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Risk assessment.</span></h2>
          <p>The licensee shall:</p>
          <p>(1) designate one or more employees, an affiliate, or an outside vendor authorized to act on behalf of the licensee who is responsible for the information security program;</p>
          <p>(2) identify reasonably foreseeable internal or external threats that could result in unauthorized access, transmission, disclosure, misuse, alteration, or destruction of nonpublic information, including threats to the security of information systems and nonpublic information that are accessible to, or held by, third-party service providers;</p>
          <p>(3) assess the likelihood and potential damage of the threats identified pursuant to clause (2), taking into consideration the sensitivity of the nonpublic information;</p>
          <p>(4) assess the sufficiency of policies, procedures, information systems, and other safeguards in place to manage these threats, including consideration of threats in each relevant area of the licensee's operations, including:</p>
          <p>(i) employee training and management;</p>
          <p>(ii) information systems, including network and software design, as well as information classification, governance, processing, storage, transmission, and disposal; and</p>
          <p>(iii) detecting, preventing, and responding to attacks, intrusions, or other systems failures; and</p>
          <p>(5) implement information safeguards to manage the threats identified in its ongoing assessment, and no less than annually, assess the effectiveness of the safeguards' key controls, systems, and procedures.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9851.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Risk management.</span></h2>
          <p>Based on its risk assessment, the licensee shall:</p>
          <p>(1) design its information security program to mitigate the identified risks, commensurate with the size and complexity of the licensee, the nature and scope of the licensee's activities, including its use of third-party service providers, and the sensitivity of the nonpublic information used by the licensee or in the licensee's possession, custody, or control;</p>
          <p>(2) determine which of the following security measures are appropriate and implement any appropriate security measures:</p>
          <p>(i) place access controls on information systems, including controls to authenticate and permit access only to authorized individuals, to protect against the unauthorized acquisition of nonpublic information;</p>
          <p>(ii) identify and manage the data, personnel, devices, systems, and facilities that enable the organization to achieve business purposes in accordance with their relative importance to business objectives and the organization's risk strategy;</p>
          <p>(iii) restrict physical access to nonpublic information to authorized individuals only;</p>
          <p>(iv) protect, by encryption or other appropriate means, all nonpublic information while being transmitted over an external network and all nonpublic information stored on a laptop computer or other portable computing or storage device or media;</p>
          <p>(v) adopt secure development practices for in-house developed applications utilized by the licensee;</p>
          <p>(vi) modify the information system in accordance with the licensee's information security program;</p>
          <p>(vii) utilize effective controls, which may include multifactor authentication procedures for any authorized individual accessing nonpublic information;</p>
          <p>(viii) regularly test and monitor systems and procedures to detect actual and attempted attacks on, or intrusions into, information systems;</p>
          <p>(ix) include audit trails within the information security program designed to detect and respond to cybersecurity events and designed to reconstruct material financial transactions sufficient to support normal operations and obligations of the licensee;</p>
          <p>(x) implement measures to protect against destruction, loss, or damage of nonpublic information due to environmental hazards, such as fire and water damage, other catastrophes, or technological failures; and</p>
          <p>(xi) develop, implement, and maintain procedures for the secure disposal of nonpublic information in any format;</p>
          <p>(3) include cybersecurity risks in the licensee's enterprise risk management process;</p>
          <p>(4) stay informed regarding emerging threats or vulnerabilities and utilize reasonable security measures when sharing information relative to the character of the sharing and the type of information shared; and</p>
          <p>(5) provide its personnel with cybersecurity awareness training that is updated as necessary to reflect risks identified by the licensee in the risk assessment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9851.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Oversight by board of directors.</span></h2>
          <p>If the licensee has a board of directors, the board or an appropriate committee of the board shall, at a minimum:</p>
          <p>(1) require the licensee's executive management or its delegates to develop, implement, and maintain the licensee's information security program;</p>
          <p>(2) require the licensee's executive management or its delegates to report in writing, at least annually, the following information:</p>
          <p>(i) the overall status of the information security program and the licensee's compliance with sections 60A.985 to 60A.9858; and</p>
          <p>(ii) material matters related to the information security program, addressing issues such as risk assessment, risk management and control decisions, third-party service provider arrangements, results of testing, cybersecurity events or violations and management's responses thereto, and recommendations for changes in the information security program; and</p>
          <p>(3) if executive management delegates any of its responsibilities under this section, it shall oversee the development, implementation, and maintenance of the licensee's information security program prepared by the delegate and shall receive a report from the delegate complying with the requirements of the report to the board of directors.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9851.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Oversight of third-party service provider arrangements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A licensee shall exercise due diligence in selecting its third-party service provider.</p>
          <p>(b) A licensee shall require a third-party service provider to implement appropriate administrative, technical, and physical measures to protect and secure the information systems and nonpublic information that are accessible to, or held by, the third-party service provider.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9851.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Program adjustments.</span></h2>
          <p>The licensee shall monitor, evaluate, and adjust, as appropriate, the information security program consistent with any relevant changes in technology, the sensitivity of its nonpublic information, internal or external threats to information, and the licensee's own changing business arrangements, such as mergers and acquisitions, alliances and joint ventures, outsourcing arrangements, and changes to information systems.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9851.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Incident response plan.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As part of its information security program, each licensee shall establish a written incident response plan designed to promptly respond to, and recover from, any cybersecurity event that compromises the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of nonpublic information in its possession, the licensee's information systems, or the continuing functionality of any aspect of the licensee's business or operations.</p>
          <p>(b) The incident response plan shall address the following areas:</p>
          <p>(1) the internal process for responding to a cybersecurity event;</p>
          <p>(2) the goals of the incident response plan;</p>
          <p>(3) the definition of clear roles, responsibilities, and levels of decision-making authority;</p>
          <p>(4) external and internal communications and information sharing;</p>
          <p>(5) identification of requirements for the remediation of any identified weaknesses in information systems and associated controls;</p>
          <p>(6) documentation and reporting regarding cybersecurity events and related incident response activities; and</p>
          <p>(7) the evaluation and revision, as necessary, of the incident response plan following a cybersecurity event.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9851.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Annual certification to commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Subject to paragraph (b), by April 15 of each year, an insurer domiciled in this state shall certify in writing to the commissioner that the insurer is in compliance with the requirements set forth in this section. Each insurer shall maintain all records, schedules, and data supporting this certificate for a period of five years and shall permit examination by the commissioner. To the extent an insurer has identified areas, systems, or processes that require material improvement, updating, or redesign, the insurer shall document the identification and the remedial efforts planned and underway to address such areas, systems, or processes. Such documentation must be available for inspection by the commissioner.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner must post on the department's website, no later than 60 days prior to the certification required by paragraph (a), the form and manner of submission required and any instructions necessary to prepare the certification.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9851.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.6.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9852">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9852 INVESTIGATION OF A CYBERSECURITY EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9852.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Prompt investigation.</span></h2>
          <p>If the licensee learns that a cybersecurity event has or may have occurred, the licensee, or an outside vendor or service provider designated to act on behalf of the licensee, shall conduct a prompt investigation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9852.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Investigation contents.</span></h2>
          <p>During the investigation, the licensee, or an outside vendor or service provider designated to act on behalf of the licensee, shall, at a minimum and to the extent possible:</p>
          <p>(1) determine whether a cybersecurity event has occurred;</p>
          <p>(2) assess the nature and scope of the cybersecurity event, if any;</p>
          <p>(3) identify whether any nonpublic information was involved in the cybersecurity event and, if so, what nonpublic information was involved; and</p>
          <p>(4) perform or oversee reasonable measures to restore the security of the information systems compromised in the cybersecurity event in order to prevent further unauthorized acquisition, release, or use of nonpublic information in the licensee's possession, custody, or control.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9852.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Third-party systems.</span></h2>
          <p>If the licensee learns that a cybersecurity event has or may have occurred in a system maintained by a third-party service provider, the licensee will complete the steps listed in subdivision 2 or confirm and document that the third-party service provider has completed those steps.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9852.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Records.</span></h2>
          <p>The licensee shall maintain records concerning all cybersecurity events for a period of at least five years from the date of the cybersecurity event and shall produce those records upon demand of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9852.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.7.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9853">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9853 NOTIFICATION OF A CYBERSECURITY EVENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9853.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Notification to the commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>Each licensee shall notify the commissioner of commerce or commissioner of health, whichever commissioner otherwise regulates the licensee, without unreasonable delay but in no event later than five business days from a determination that a cybersecurity event has occurred when either of the following criteria has been met:</p>
          <p>(1) this state is the licensee's state of domicile, in the case of an insurer, or this state is the licensee's home state, in the case of a producer, as those terms are defined in chapter 60K and the cybersecurity event has a reasonable likelihood of materially harming:</p>
          <p>(i) any consumer residing in this state; or</p>
          <p>(ii) any part of the normal operations of the licensee; or</p>
          <p>(2) the licensee reasonably believes that the nonpublic information involved is of 250 or more consumers residing in this state and that is either of the following:</p>
          <p>(i) a cybersecurity event impacting the licensee of which notice is required to be provided to any government body, self-regulatory agency, or any other supervisory body pursuant to any state or federal law; or</p>
          <p>(ii) a cybersecurity event that has a reasonable likelihood of materially harming:</p>
          <p>(A) any consumer residing in this state; or</p>
          <p>(B) any part of the normal operations of the licensee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9853.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Information; notification.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensee making the notification required under subdivision 1 shall provide the information in electronic form as directed by the commissioner. The licensee shall have a continuing obligation to update and supplement initial and subsequent notifications to the commissioner concerning material changes to previously provided information relating to the cybersecurity event. The licensee shall provide as much of the following information as possible:</p>
          <p>(1) date of the cybersecurity event;</p>
          <p>(2) description of how the information was exposed, lost, stolen, or breached, including the specific roles and responsibilities of third-party service providers, if any;</p>
          <p>(3) how the cybersecurity event was discovered;</p>
          <p>(4) whether any lost, stolen, or breached information has been recovered and, if so, how this was done;</p>
          <p>(5) the identity of the source of the cybersecurity event;</p>
          <p>(6) whether the licensee has filed a police report or has notified any regulatory, government, or law enforcement agencies and, if so, when such notification was provided;</p>
          <p>(7) description of the specific types of information acquired without authorization. Specific types of information means particular data elements including, for example, types of medical information, types of financial information, or types of information allowing identification of the consumer;</p>
          <p>(8) the period during which the information system was compromised by the cybersecurity event;</p>
          <p>(9) the number of total consumers in this state affected by the cybersecurity event. The licensee shall provide the best estimate in the initial report to the commissioner and update this estimate with each subsequent report to the commissioner pursuant to this section;</p>
          <p>(10) the results of any internal review identifying a lapse in either automated controls or internal procedures, or confirming that all automated controls or internal procedures were followed;</p>
          <p>(11) description of efforts being undertaken to remediate the situation which permitted the cybersecurity event to occur;</p>
          <p>(12) a copy of the licensee's privacy policy and a statement outlining the steps the licensee will take to investigate and notify consumers affected by the cybersecurity event; and</p>
          <p>(13) name of a contact person who is familiar with the cybersecurity event and authorized to act for the licensee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9853.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Notification to consumers.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If a licensee is required to submit a report to the commissioner under subdivision 1, the licensee shall notify any consumer residing in Minnesota if, as a result of the cybersecurity event reported to the commissioner, the consumer's nonpublic information was or is reasonably believed to have been acquired by an unauthorized person, and there is a reasonable likelihood of material harm to the consumer as a result of the cybersecurity event. Consumer notification is not required for a cybersecurity event resulting from the good faith acquisition of nonpublic information by an employee or agent of the licensee for the purposes of the licensee's business, provided the nonpublic information is not used for a purpose other than the licensee's business or subject to further unauthorized disclosure. The notification must be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, consistent with the legitimate needs of law enforcement or with any measures necessary to determine the scope of the breach, identify the individuals affected, and restore the reasonable integrity of the data system. The notification may be delayed to a date certain if the commissioner determines that providing the notice impedes a criminal investigation. The licensee shall provide a copy of the notice to the commissioner.</p>
          <p>(b) For purposes of this subdivision, notice required under paragraph (a) must be provided by one of the following methods:</p>
          <p>(1) written notice to the consumer's most recent address in the licensee's records;</p>
          <p>(2) electronic notice, if the licensee's primary method of communication with the consumer is by electronic means or if the notice provided is consistent with the provisions regarding electronic records and signatures in United States Code, title 15, section 7001; or</p>
          <p>(3) if the cost of providing notice exceeds $250,000, the affected class of consumers to be notified exceeds 500,000, or the licensee does not have sufficient contact information for the subject consumers, notice as follows:</p>
          <p>(i) email notice when the licensee has an email address for the subject consumers;</p>
          <p>(ii) conspicuous posting of the notice on the website page of the licensee; and</p>
          <p>(iii) notification to major statewide media.</p>
          <p>(c) Notwithstanding paragraph (b), a licensee that maintains its own notification procedure as part of its information security program that is consistent with the timing requirements of this subdivision is deemed to comply with the notification requirements if the licensee notifies subject consumers in accordance with its program.</p>
          <p>(d) A waiver of the requirements under this subdivision is contrary to public policy, and is void and unenforceable.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9853.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Notice regarding cybersecurity events of third-party service providers.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) In the case of a cybersecurity event in a system maintained by a third-party service provider, of which the licensee has become aware, the licensee shall treat such event as it would under subdivision 1 unless the third-party service provider provides the notice required under subdivision 1.</p>
          <p>(b) The computation of a licensee's deadlines shall begin on the day after the third-party service provider notifies the licensee of the cybersecurity event or the licensee otherwise has actual knowledge of the cybersecurity event, whichever is sooner.</p>
          <p>(c) Nothing in sections 60A.985 to 60A.9858 shall prevent or abrogate an agreement between a licensee and another licensee, a third-party service provider, or any other party to fulfill any of the investigation requirements imposed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9854">60A.9854</a> or notice requirements imposed under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9853.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Notice regarding cybersecurity events of reinsurers to insurers.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) In the case of a cybersecurity event involving nonpublic information that is used by the licensee that is acting as an assuming insurer or in the possession, custody, or control of a licensee that is acting as an assuming insurer and that does not have a direct contractual relationship with the affected consumers, the assuming insurer shall notify its affected ceding insurers and the commissioner of its state of domicile within three business days of making the determination that a cybersecurity event has occurred.</p>
          <p>(b) The ceding insurers that have a direct contractual relationship with affected consumers shall fulfill the consumer notification requirements imposed under subdivision 3 and any other notification requirements relating to a cybersecurity event imposed under this section.</p>
          <p>(c) In the case of a cybersecurity event involving nonpublic information that is in the possession, custody, or control of a third-party service provider of a licensee that is an assuming insurer, the assuming insurer shall notify its affected ceding insurers and the commissioner of its state of domicile within three business days of receiving notice from its third-party service provider that a cybersecurity event has occurred.</p>
          <p>(d) The ceding insurers that have a direct contractual relationship with affected consumers shall fulfill the consumer notification requirements imposed under subdivision 3 and any other notification requirements relating to a cybersecurity event imposed under this section.</p>
          <p>(e) Any licensee acting as an assuming insurer shall have no other notice obligations relating to a cybersecurity event or other data breach under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9853.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Notice regarding cybersecurity events of insurers to producers of record.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) In the case of a cybersecurity event involving nonpublic information that is in the possession, custody, or control of a licensee that is an insurer or its third-party service provider and for which a consumer accessed the insurer's services through an independent insurance producer, the insurer shall notify the producers of record of all affected consumers no later than the time at which notice is provided to the affected consumers.</p>
          <p>(b) The insurer is excused from this obligation for those instances in which it does not have the current producer of record information for any individual consumer or in those instances in which the producer of record is no longer appointed to sell, solicit, or negotiate on behalf of the insurer.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9853.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.8.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9854">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9854 POWER OF COMMISSIONER.</h1>
        <p>(a) The commissioner of commerce or commissioner of health, whichever commissioner otherwise regulates the licensee, shall have power to examine and investigate into the affairs of any licensee to determine whether the licensee has been or is engaged in any conduct in violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.985">60A.985</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9857">60A.9857</a>. This power is in addition to the powers which the commissioner has under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.031">60A.031</a>. Any such investigation or examination shall be conducted pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.031">60A.031</a>.</p>
        <p>(b) Whenever the commissioner of commerce or commissioner of health has reason to believe that a licensee has been or is engaged in conduct in this state which violates sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.985">60A.985</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9857">60A.9857</a>, the commissioner of commerce or commissioner of health may take action that is necessary or appropriate to enforce those sections.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9854.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.9.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 9</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9855">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9855 CONFIDENTIALITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9855.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Licensee information.</span></h2>
          <p>Any documents, materials, or other information in the control or possession of the department that are furnished by a licensee or an employee or agent thereof acting on behalf of a licensee pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9851">60A.9851, subdivision </a>9; section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9853#stat.60A.9853.2">60A.9853, subdivision 2</a>, clauses (2), (3), (4), (5), (8), (10), and (11); or that are obtained by the commissioner in an investigation or examination pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9854">60A.9854</a> shall be classified as confidential, protected nonpublic, or both; shall not be subject to subpoena; and shall not be subject to discovery or admissible in evidence in any private civil action. However, the commissioner is authorized to use the documents, materials, or other information in the furtherance of any regulatory or legal action brought as a part of the commissioner's duties.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9855.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Certain testimony prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>Neither the commissioner nor any person who received documents, materials, or other information while acting under the authority of the commissioner shall be permitted or required to testify in any private civil action concerning any confidential documents, materials, or information subject to subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9855.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Information sharing.</span></h2>
          <p>In order to assist in the performance of the commissioner's duties under sections 60A.985 to 60A.9858, the commissioner:</p>
          <p>(1) may share documents, materials, or other information, including the confidential and privileged documents, materials, or information subject to subdivision 1, with other state, federal, and international regulatory agencies, with the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, its affiliates or subsidiaries, and with state, federal, and international law enforcement authorities, provided that the recipient agrees in writing to maintain the confidentiality and privileged status of the document, material, or other information;</p>
          <p>(2) may receive documents, materials, or information, including otherwise confidential and privileged documents, materials, or information, from the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, its affiliates or subsidiaries, and from regulatory and law enforcement officials of other foreign or domestic jurisdictions, and shall maintain as confidential or privileged any document, material, or information received with notice or the understanding that it is confidential or privileged under the laws of the jurisdiction that is the source of the document, material, or information;</p>
          <p>(3) may share documents, materials, or other information subject to subdivision 1, with a third-party consultant or vendor provided the consultant agrees in writing to maintain the confidentiality and privileged status of the document, material, or other information; and</p>
          <p>(4) may enter into agreements governing sharing and use of information consistent with this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9855.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">No waiver of privilege or confidentiality.</span></h2>
          <p>No waiver of any applicable privilege or claim of confidentiality in the documents, materials, or information shall occur as a result of disclosure to the commissioner under this section or as a result of sharing as authorized in subdivision 3. Any document, material, or information disclosed to the commissioner under this section about a cybersecurity event must be retained and preserved by the licensee for five years.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9855.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Certain actions public.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.985">60A.985</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9857">60A.9857</a> shall prohibit the commissioner from releasing final, adjudicated actions that are open to public inspection pursuant to chapter 13 to a database or other clearinghouse service maintained by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, its affiliates, or subsidiaries.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9855.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Classification, protection, and use of information by others.</span></h2>
          <p>Documents, materials, or other information in the possession or control of the National Association of Insurance Commissioners or a third-party consultant pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.985">60A.985</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9857">60A.9857</a> are classified as confidential, protected nonpublic, and privileged; are not subject to subpoena; and are not subject to discovery or admissible in evidence in a private civil action.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.60A.9855.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/4/#laws.3.10.0">1Sp2021 c 4 art 3 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.60A.9856">
        <h1 class="shn">60A.9856 EXCEPTIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.60A.9856.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Generally.</span></h2>
          <p>The following exceptions shall apply to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.985">60A.985</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9857">60A.9857</a>:</p>
          <p>(1) a licensee with fewer than 25 employees is exempt from sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9851">60A.9851</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9852">60A.9852</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) a licensee subject to and in compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, Public Law 104-191, 110 Stat. 1936 (HIPAA), is considered to comply with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9851">60A.9851</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9852">60A.9852</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9853">60A.9853, subdivisions 3</a> to 5, provided the licensee submits a written statement certifying its compliance with HIPAA;</p>
          <p>(3) a licensee affiliated with a depository institution that maintains an information security program in compliance with the interagency guidelines establishing standards for safeguarding customer information as set forth pursuant to United States Code, title 15, sections 6801 and 6805, shall be considered to meet the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9851">60A.9851 </a>provided that the licensee produce, upon request, documentation satisfactory to the commission that independently validates the affiliated depository institution's adoption of an information security program that satisfies the interagency guidelines;</p>
          <p>(4) an employee, agent, representative, or designee of a licensee, who is also a licensee, is exempt from sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9851">60A.9851</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.9852">60A.9852</a> and need not develop its own information security program to the extent that the employee, agent, representative, or designee is covered by the information security program of the other licensee; and</p>
